broken.title: Variable (kymainomeno) monthly-statement save strands the vacant unit's share as an orphan tenant monthlyCharge and never routes it to the owner ledger — owner under-billed, money invisible everywhere
broken.line: 2407-2461, 2514-2523 (updateMonthlyStatement); contrast 3959-3997 (_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges billableExpenses filter)
broken.brokenShape: updateMonthlyStatement loops EVERY managed unit and pushes a per-unit monthlyCharge whenever computeBuildingChargeForProperty returns share>0 (line 2446-2458). For an equal/thousandths/by_surface variable expense, the engine returns a positive share for a VACANT unit too (a vacant managed unit is an equal party / has thousandths), so the vacant unit gets a real monthlyCharge pushed onto unit.monthlyCharges. But that unit has no tenant, so taskBase (1_base.ts:932-991) — which only iterates each tenant's contract.properties — never reads it: the charge bills nobody. updateMonthlyStatement then calls ONLY _recomputeTenantsForProperty (line 2522); it never calls _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges / recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties. And even if it did, that recompute skips amount-0 non-fixed expenses (billableExpenses filter, line 3959-3961: `e.allocationMethod === 'fixed' || Number(e.amount) > 0`), and a VARIABLE expense carries amount 0 on building.expenses. So with chargeOwnerWhenVacant ON, the vacant unit's slice of the typed statement total is never materialised into ownerMonthlyExpenses (no paid toggle, absent from owner καταβολές settlement and from the dashboard eksoda gap-fill which uses the same amount>0 predicate).
broken.trigger: Building with >=1 vacant managed unit + a variable/kymainomeno building expense (amount 0 on the expense, real figure typed per term) with chargeOwnerWhenVacant=true. Landlord opens the monthly-statement tile for the term, types e.g. €300, saves (PATCH updateMonthlyStatement). The occupied units get their shares billed correctly; the vacant unit's share (e.g. €100 of a 3-way equal split) is pushed as a monthlyCharge on the empty unit, bills no rent, and is never written as a source:'vacant' owner row. The owner is silently undercharged €100/term.

verdict.codeEvidence: buildingmanager.ts:2407-2461 (saveMonthlyStatement, the function the reviewer called "updateMonthlyStatement"; wired at routes.ts:360-362 `POST /:id/monthly-statement`): the per-unit loop iterates ALL units with a propertyId (`for (const unit of units) { if (!unit.propertyId) continue;`) — NO occupancy filter. For each provided expense it computes `share = computeBuildingChargeForProperty(buildingPlain, unit.propertyId, {...buildingExpense, amount: entry.amount, allocationMethod}, term)` (2435-2444) using the landlord-typed `entry.amount`, then `if (share > 0) unit.monthlyCharges.push({...})` (2446-2458). For an equal/thousandths/by_surface expense, computeBuildingChargeForProperty RETURNS a positive share for a vacant managed unit — confirmed at 1_base.ts:565-624 ("the vacant unit's €30 is returned so _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges can route it to the owner ledger") and the thousandths cases at 1_base.ts:489-505. So a real monthlyCharge lands on the EMPTY unit. taskBase (1_base.ts:865-965) only iterates `contract.properties` (tenant-covered units, filtered to entry/exit window) and reads `unit.monthlyCharges` there (946-964) — a vacant unit is in no tenant's contract.properties, so its monthlyCharge is read by nobody → bills nobody. saveMonthlyStatement then calls ONLY `_recomputeTenantsForProperty` (2521-2523), which recomputes tenant rents only (verified 298-412: no vacant-owner call); it never calls `_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges`/`recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties`. And `_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges` would skip it anyway: `billableExpenses = activeExpenses.filter((e) => e.allocationMethod === 'fixed' || Number(e.amount) > 0)` (3959-3961) with the author's own comment at 3955-3958: "Truly-VARIABLE expenses (amount 0, non-fixed — materialised into monthlyCharges at statement time) are still skipped". The ownerExpenses branch (2472-2512) only writes source:'expense' rows from the explicit `ownerExpenses` array, not the per-unit vacant slice.
verdict.reasoning: The finding holds against current code on disk. The chain is complete and unguarded: (1) saveMonthlyStatement pushes a monthlyCharge on EVERY unit with share>0, including vacant managed units, because computeBuildingChargeForProperty deliberately returns the vacant unit's positive share for equal/thousandths/by_surface (the VAC-EQUAL-NOOP fix at 1_base.ts:565-576 made this so, explicitly relying on _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges to route it). (2) The vacant unit's monthlyCharge bills nobody because taskBase only reads monthlyCharges through tenant contract.properties. (3) The owner-routing function is never invoked by saveMonthlyStatement, and even if it were, its billableExpenses filter (amount>0 || fixed) deliberately skips truly-variable (amount-0, non-fixed) expenses — the author's comment assumes the statement path handles them, but the statement path strands them on the empty unit instead of materialising a source:'vacant' owner row. With chargeOwnerWhenVacant=true the owner SHOULD be billed but the flag is never consulted in the per-unit loop, so the vacant unit's slice of a kymainomeno statement total (e.g. €100 of a 3-way €300 equal split) is dropped: it bills no renter, never becomes an owner row, has no paid toggle, and is absent from owner καταβολές settlement and the dashboard eksoda gap-fill (which uses the same amount>0 predicate per the comment at 3952-3954). This is real dropped-money / owner under-billing. The reviewer mislabeled the function name (saveMonthlyStatement, not updateMonthlyStatement) but the line numbers and substance are exactly correct; that does not weaken the finding.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak: services/api/src/managers/buildingmanager.ts saveMonthlyStatement, the per-unit charge loop at 2407-2461 (specifically the unconditional `unit.monthlyCharges.push` at 2447 with no occupancy check) combined with the recompute call at 2521-2523 that invokes only `_recomputeTenantsForProperty` and never `_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges`/`recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties`. For a building with >=1 vacant managed unit and a variable (amount-0, non-fixed) expense with chargeOwnerWhenVacant=true, the vacant unit's share of the typed statement total is pushed as a monthlyCharge on the empty unit (read by no tenant rent in taskBase, 1_base.ts:865-965) and is never materialised as a source:'vacant' ownerMonthlyExpenses row — the owner is silently under-billed by that slice every term. Minimal fix direction: after saving the statement, call recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties for the building's propertyIds (so vacant slices route to the owner) AND either skip pushing monthlyCharges for unoccupied units in the statement loop or have the vacant-owner recompute treat statement-materialised variable amounts as billable for vacant/owner-occupied units — otherwise the billableExpenses amount>0 filter at 3959-3961 will continue to skip the variable expense.

broken.title: Owner rows synthesised from unit.monthlyCharges never set ownerBilled, so a vacant unit's charge is mislabelled 'uncollected' (Αχρέωτα) even when chargeOwnerWhenVacant is ON
broken.line: 377-402 (step-2 monthlyCharges loop) vs 366-372 (step-1 sets ownerBilled), 410-415 (ownerBilledTotal/ownerUnbilledTotal split)
broken.brokenShape: computeBuildingExpenseBreakdown step 2 builds owner rows from unit.monthlyCharges with `...(recipient === 'owner' ? { owners: ownerSlicesFor(...) } : {})` (line 398-401) — it omits the `ownerBilled` key that step 1 sets (line 366-372: `ownerBilled: isOwnerOccupied || !!expense.chargeOwnerWhenVacant`). The totals split at line 410-415 routes any owner row with falsy ownerBilled into ownerUnbilledTotal (the 'Αχρέωτα (κενές μονάδες)' uncollected bucket). So a vacant unit's persisted/stranded monthlyCharge (e.g. the stranded variable-statement share from finding #1, or any monthlyCharge whose unit is now vacant) shows as 'uncollected' on the Expenses breakdown panel even when the source expense has chargeOwnerWhenVacant=true and the share is genuinely owner-borne.
broken.trigger: Any term where computeBuildingExpenseBreakdown runs on a building with a unit.monthlyCharge whose unit has no tenant for the term (getExpenseBreakdown nulls unit.tenant for unoccupied units, line 2573-2577) — e.g. a vacant unit carrying a stranded variable-statement charge, or a unit that went vacant after a statement was saved. The breakdown shows the amount under ownerUnbilledTotal/'uncollected' instead of ownerBilledTotal, contradicting the chargeOwnerWhenVacant=true intent and misreporting what the owner owes vs what evaporates.

verdict.codeEvidence: services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/1_base.ts:298 `recipient = tenant ? 'renter' : 'owner'`; step-1 (recurring expenses) line 366-372 sets `ownerBilled: isOwnerOccupied || !!expense.chargeOwnerWhenVacant`; step-2 (monthlyCharges loop) line 377-402 resolves `srcExpense` at 381-383 but its owner branch at 398-401 spreads ONLY `{ owners: ownerSlicesFor(...) }` — `ownerBilled` is omitted (and `isOwnerOccupied` unused). Split at 410-415: any owner row with falsy `ownerBilled` → `ownerUnbilledTotal`. Writer proof: buildingmanager.ts:2407-2459 the variable-statement save loop pushes `unit.monthlyCharges.push({...})` at 2447 for ANY unit with `share>0` — NO occupied/vacant guard (contrast the repair path 3696-3705 which routes vacant shares to the owner ledger, not monthlyCharges). _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges (3959-3961) `billableExpenses = activeExpenses.filter(e => e.allocationMethod==='fixed' || Number(e.amount)>0)` — comment 3955-3958 confirms truly-VARIABLE expenses are SKIPPED, so NO source:'vacant' ownerMonthlyExpense is created for them. getExpenseBreakdown comment 2583-2587 defers vacant-share display to breakdown.rows. Frontend BuildingExpensePanel.js:777-784 builds the Αχρέωτα/uncollected block from `breakdown.rows.filter(r => r.recipient==='owner' && !r.ownerBilled)`, and line 964 prompts to "Enable Charge owner for vacant units" even when it is already on. Schema: building.ts:143 `chargeOwnerWhenVacant: {type:Boolean}`, 110 `amount:{default:0}` — variable+flag-on is a valid state.
verdict.reasoning: The finding is correct and reachable in current code. A vacant managed unit's share of a VARIABLE building-expense statement (amount 0, non-fixed) is persisted ONLY as a unit.monthlyCharge (buildingmanager.ts:2447 — the statement-save loop has no occupancy guard, unlike the repair path which routes vacant shares to the owner ledger). _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges explicitly skips truly-variable expenses (1_base billableExpenses filter at 3959-3961, comment 3955-3958), so there is NO compensating source:'vacant' ownerMonthlyExpense, and getExpenseBreakdown's ownerDirect list does not carry it. Therefore the only representation in the breakdown is the step-2 monthlyCharges row at 1_base.ts:377-402, whose owner branch (398-401) omits `ownerBilled`. With falsy ownerBilled, the totals split (410-415) puts the euro in ownerUnbilledTotal, and the frontend (BuildingExpensePanel.js:777-784) renders it under the Αχρέωτα 'uncollected' warning — contradicting the expense's chargeOwnerWhenVacant=true intent, and even instructing the landlord to enable a flag that is already enabled. This mislabels genuinely owner-billed money as evaporating/uncollected (wrong-money on a surface). The fix is minimal and the needed data is already in scope: step-2 should set `ownerBilled: isOwnerOccupied || !!srcExpense?.chargeOwnerWhenVacant` (srcExpense resolved at 381-383, isOwnerOccupied at 305), mirroring step-1's line 368. Note the same omission also mislabels an OWNER-OCCUPIED unit's variable-statement monthlyCharge (isOwnerOccupied true) as uncollected.

broken.title: Thousandths basis denominator mismatch: engine divides by FULL building thousandths total (all units) but _shareBasis displays the managed-only total, so the explanation fraction does not reconcile to the billed share
broken.line: 489 / 496 / 503 (engine: building.units.reduce over ALL units) vs 171-181 (_shareBasis: managed = units.filter(u.propertyId), sumT over managed only)
broken.brokenShape: _computeBuildingChargeRaw thousandths branches divide by the sum of thousandths across ALL building.units including unmanaged ones (no propertyId) — Wave-14 F2 intentional. But _shareBasis (used for the breakdown panel's '1,70 € × 50‰ / whole‰ = 0,15 €' explanation) computes `whole` from `managed = (building.units||[]).filter(u => u.propertyId)` (line 146, 171-174). When the building has any unmanaged unit carrying thousandths, the displayed `whole` < the engine's actual denominator, so the displayed part/whole×total does NOT equal the displayed `share`. The billed money is correct; the rendered calc basis is wrong/contradictory.
broken.trigger: A building with at least one unit that has thousandths set but no propertyId (unmanaged unit) — storable since BuildingUnitSchema.propertyId is an optional String and thousandths are free Numbers. Open the Expenses breakdown for any general/heating/elevator-thousandths expense: the per-row explanation shows a denominator (managed-only) that doesn't match the actual division, and part/whole×total ≠ the shown share.

verdict.codeEvidence: services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/1_base.ts: engine thousandths branches compute the denominator over ALL units — line 489 `const generalTotal = building.units.reduce((sum, u) => sum + (Number(u.generalThousandths) || 0), 0)`, line 496 `heatingTotal = building.units.reduce(...)`, line 503 `elevatorTotal = building.units.reduce(...)` (Wave-14 F2 comment, lines 485-488, deliberately uses the full denominator). The returned share is rounded by computeBuildingChargeForProperty (line 66) and stored as the row's `amount` (line 355). BUT _shareBasis (lines 146,171-174) computes `whole` over MANAGED units only: line 146 `const managed = (building.units||[]).filter((u) => u.propertyId)`, lines 171-174 `const sumT = managed.reduce((s,u) => s + (Number(u[key])||0), 0)` → returned as `whole` (line 178) for kind 'thousandths' (line 176). The frontend renders both together: webapps/landlord/src/components/buildings/BuildingExpensePanel.js line 708 `t('{{part}}‰ ÷ {{whole}}‰ × {{total}} € = {{share}} €', {part: basis.part, whole: basis.whole, total: basis.total, share: basis.share})`. Data state reachable: services/common/src/collections/building.ts BuildingUnitSchema has `propertyId: String` (line 69, optional, no required) alongside free `generalThousandths/heatingThousandths/elevatorThousandths: Number` (lines 57-59); buildingmanager.ts repeatedly treats propertyId-less units as legitimate unmanaged units (e.g. line 50 `.filter((u) => u.propertyId)`).
verdict.reasoning: The two denominators genuinely diverge in current code. The billing engine (_computeBuildingChargeRaw, lines 489/496/503) divides by the sum of thousandths across ALL building.units (managed + unmanaged) — this is the intentional Wave-14 F2 behavior and the billed money is correct. But _shareBasis (lines 146/171-174) sums thousandths over `managed = units.filter(u.propertyId)` only, and that managed-only sum becomes `basis.whole`, which the frontend renders verbatim as the divisor in the human-readable calc-basis line `part ‰ ÷ whole ‰ × total € = share €` (BuildingExpensePanel.js:708). Whenever the building has at least one unit carrying thousandths but no propertyId (a normal post-E9-import state — the whole πολυκατοικία is imported, only some units link to a managed property; the schema makes propertyId optional and thousandths free Numbers, and buildingmanager filters managed vs unmanaged exactly this way), the displayed `whole` is smaller than the real engine denominator. Consequently the rendered equation does NOT reconcile: part ÷ whole × total ≠ the displayed share. This is a real render contradiction on a money surface (the Expenses breakdown explanation panel) — the user sees an arithmetic equation that does not add up. No money is mis-billed (the `share`/`amount` is the correct full-denominator value), so impact is cosmetic/low, but it is a confirmed wrong-render in current code, not a misread or already-guarded path. Minimal leak: the `whole`/`sumT` denominator in _shareBasis's thousandths branch (lines 171-174) must mirror the engine's full-building reduce (lines 489/496/503), not the managed-only filter, OR the engine must be normalized to managed-only — but since the engine's full-denominator is load-bearing/intentional, the fix belongs in _shareBasis.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is in _shareBasis thousandths branch, services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/1_base.ts lines 171-174: `sumT` is computed over `managed` (units with propertyId, defined line 146) but should reduce over ALL `building.units` to match the engine denominator at lines 489/496/503 that produced the displayed `share`. Surfaces only when a building has a unit with thousandths set and no propertyId. Result: the breakdown panel's calc-basis line (BuildingExpensePanel.js:708, `{{part}}‰ ÷ {{whole}}‰ × {{total}} € = {{share}} €`) shows a denominator that does not reconcile to the shown share. Display-only; billed amount is correct. Low severity.

broken.title: Thousandths basis equation prints the MANAGED-unit denominator while the billed share is computed against the FULL-building denominator → self-contradictory '÷‰ ×total =share' on the breakdown
broken.line: 171-181 (basis whole = managed.reduce) vs 489/496/503 (engine denominator = building.units.reduce); rendered at webapps/landlord/src/components/buildings/BuildingExpensePanel.js:707-712
broken.brokenShape: For general/heating/elevator_thousandths the per-unit SHARE the engine bills is amount × unit‰ / (sum of ‰ over ALL building.units, incl. UNMANAGED units that have no propertyId) — _computeBuildingChargeRaw lines 489/496/503 reduce over `building.units`. But the explanatory ShareBasis emitted alongside that share computes `whole` = sum over `managed` units only (_shareBasis line 146 `managed = units.filter(u=>u.propertyId)`, used at 171). The frontend renders the basis as `{{part}}‰ ÷ {{whole}}‰ × {{total}} € = {{share}} €` (BuildingExpensePanel.js:708-712), reading `share` straight from the engine. When the building has any unmanaged unit carrying thousandths, the displayed `whole` is smaller than the real denominator, so `part ÷ whole × total` does NOT equal the displayed `share` — e.g. a 250‰ managed unit among 1000‰ total (with 500‰ on unmanaged units) renders '250‰ ÷ 500‰ × 100 € = 25 €' where 250/500×100 = 50 ≠ 25. by_surface does NOT have this bug (engine and basis both use managedUnits surface).
broken.trigger: Building with at least one UNMANAGED unit that carries thousandths (reachable: addUnit accepts generalThousandths>0 with no propertyId — buildingmanager.ts:1897-1929 make propertyId optional, and the sum-to-1000 guard at 1967-1976 sums ALL units, so unmanaged neighbor units legitimately hold ‰). Open the building Overview Expenses breakdown for a thousandths-allocated expense and read any managed renter row's calc-basis tooltip — the printed equation contradicts the printed euro share.

verdict.codeEvidence: 1_base.ts:171 (`const sumT = managed.reduce((s,u)=>s+(Number(u[key])||0),0)` where `managed = (building.units||[]).filter(u=>u.propertyId)` at line 146) computes the basis `whole`. The engine `_computeBuildingChargeRaw` computes the billed share over the FULL building: line 489 `building.units.reduce((sum,u)=>sum+(Number(u.generalThousandths)||0),0)` (likewise heating @496, elevator @503), with the Wave-14 F2 comment explicitly stating it uses "the FULL building denominator (sum across ALL units, including vacant)". The breakdown caller at lines 339-344 sets `share = computeBuildingChargeForProperty(...)` (= the full-denominator engine result) and then at line 361 passes that exact `share` into `_shareBasis(building, unit, expense, total, share, ...)`. So `whole` (managed-only) and `share` (full-building) derive from different denominators. Frontend formatBasis (BuildingExpensePanel.js:707-713) renders `t('{{part}}‰ ÷ {{whole}}‰ × {{total}} € = {{share}} €', {part: basis.part, whole: basis.whole, total: basis.total, share: basis.share})` — all four straight from the server basis. Reachability: addUnit (buildingmanager.ts:1897-1908) validates generalThousandths/heatingThousandths/elevatorThousandths unconditionally (min 0, max 1000) but only validates propertyId when present (line 1914 `if (req.body.propertyId)`), and the building-wide sum guard (lines 1975-1979) reduces over ALL units — so an unmanaged unit (no propertyId) legitimately carries thousandths>0 and inflates the engine denominator beyond the displayed managed `whole`.
verdict.reasoning: Traced the exact path. For general/heating/elevator_thousandths the engine divides by the sum over building.units (ALL units, lines 489/496/503 — intentional per the Wave-14 F2 comment so an unmanaged/vacant unit's slice is absorbed by the owner). The same `share` value (engine output, line 339-344) is handed to `_shareBasis` (line 361), which recomputes the displayed `whole` over `managed` units only (line 171, managed = units with propertyId at line 146). by_surface uses managedUnits in BOTH engine (line 481) and basis (line 150), so it is consistent — only thousandths diverge, exactly as the reviewer claims. The frontend prints all four basis fields verbatim as `part ÷ whole × total = share`, so whenever a building has an unmanaged unit holding thousandths the printed equation is self-contradictory (e.g. managed 250‰ among 1000‰ total with 500‰ on unmanaged units → share = 100×250/1000 = 25, but printed as '250‰ ÷ 500‰ × 100 € = 25 €', where 250/500×100 = 50 ≠ 25). The data state is reachable: addUnit accepts thousandths on a unit with no propertyId and the sum-to-1000 guard counts all units. One correction to the reviewer's report: the CLAIMED IMPACT 'blank-render' is wrong — nothing blanks; the leak is a self-contradictory printed calc-basis tooltip on managed renter/owner rows. The billed euro amount itself is correct (full denominator is the intended behavior); only the explanatory text misleads the landlord into thinking the system mis-divided. The finding (basis text contradicts the billed share) holds.
verdict.correctedDetail: Display-only contradiction (NOT blank-render, NOT wrong money). In services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/1_base.ts, `_shareBasis` computes the thousandths basis `whole` over managed units only (line 171, `managed.reduce`, managed = units with propertyId per line 146), while the `share` it is handed (line 361) was computed by the engine over ALL building.units (lines 489/496/503). When the building has any unmanaged unit (no propertyId) carrying thousandths>0 — reachable because addUnit (buildingmanager.ts:1897-1929) validates thousandths but leaves propertyId optional, and the sum-to-1000 guard sums all units — the breakdown tooltip rendered at BuildingExpensePanel.js:707-713 prints `part ÷ whole × total = share` where `part/whole × total ≠ share`. Minimal fix: make `_shareBasis` thousandths `whole` reduce over `building.units` (the full set) to match the engine denominator, OR pass the engine's actual denominator into `_shareBasis` the way `partyCount` is passed for the equal case.

broken.title: Owner-row amount (persisted ledger) and its grafted calc-basis (live recompute) can disagree on the same row in the building breakdown
broken.line: 2739 (rowAmount from persisted e.amount) and 2792-2794 (basis grafted from live breakdown.rows via basisByKey)
broken.brokenShape: getExpenseBreakdown renders each ownerDirect row's `amount` from the PERSISTED ownerMonthlyExpenses row materialised earlier by _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges (rowAmount = Math.round(e.amount*100)/100, line 2739), but grafts its `basis` (the '÷ N = share' explanation) from the LIVE engine recomputed THIS request (basisByKey at 2691-2695, attached at 2792-2794). The persisted amount and the live basis.share share no recompute. The vacant-owner recompute only re-derives the CURRENT term (and a ±12-month window on lifecycle events), so for a source:'vacant'/'owner-resident' row of a term whose equal-split divisor or surface/thousandths denominator has since changed (a sibling tenant added/removed, a unit's surface edited) without a re-run for that term, the row displays a stale persisted `amount` next to a freshly-computed basis equation whose `share` differs — the row's euro figure contradicts its own printed calculation.
broken.trigger: A building with a chargeOwnerWhenVacant (or owner-occupied) unit that got a materialised owner row in month M; later the equal-divisor or denominator changes (e.g. another tenant in the building exits) without M being re-recomputed; open the Overview Expenses breakdown for month M and read the owner row — amount vs basis '= share' tail disagree.

verdict.codeEvidence: buildingmanager.ts getExpenseBreakdown does NOT recompute the persisted ledger for the requested term — it reads hydrated.ownerMonthlyExpenses directly. For each surviving owner row it sets `rowAmount = Math.round((Number(e.amount) || 0) * 100) / 100` from the PERSISTED subdoc (L2739) and renders `amount: rowAmount` (L2787). The `basis` is grafted from the LIVE engine recomputed THIS request: `basisByKey` is built from `breakdown.rows` (L2691-2695, where breakdown = computeBuildingExpenseBreakdown(hydrated, term) at L2579) and attached as `basis: basisByKey.get(`${e.expenseId}|${e.propertyId}`) || null` (L2792-2794). In 1_base.ts the live row's amount and basis are BOTH derived from the same fresh `share` (L339 share, L355 amount:share, L356-361 basis:_shareBasis(...,share,...)), and the equal divisor is recomputed live from current state via _equalPartyCount(building, term) (L211-244 / L362-364) — i.e. basis.share = fmt(currentShare), not the persisted amount. The recompute that writes e.amount only ever runs for a SINGLE term: addExpense calls _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges(building, realmId, _currentTerm()) (L3042-3046), and the sibling-lifecycle sweep only covers terms [now-11mo … now+12mo] (L4030-4037, loop L4041 calling recompute at L4065). A persisted vacant/owner-resident row for an OUT-OF-WINDOW term whose equal divisor / surface / thousandths denominator later changed (e.g. a sibling tenant exits → _equalPartyCount drops → each share rises) keeps its stale persisted e.amount, but the live engine emits a fresh basis for that same term whenever the row survives the filter (occupancy/opt-in guards at L2646-2654 ensure a surviving row implies a matching live owner-billed row exists). The frontend prints both on one line: BuildingExpensePanel.js L930 `<NumberFormat value={e.amount} />` (persisted) beside L917-920 `({formatBasis(t, e.basis)})` which renders basis.share as the "÷ N units = {{share}} €" tail (L694-699). So the euro shown contradicts its own printed calculation.
verdict.correctedDetail: Real, but the reviewer's impact label is wrong. It is NOT a blank-render. It is a display-consistency defect: a surviving persisted source:'vacant'/'owner-resident' owner row for a term OUTSIDE the ±12-month recompute window (whose equal-divisor / surface / thousandths denominator changed since that term was last recomputed — e.g. a sibling tenant exited) shows its STALE persisted euro (`amount`, buildingmanager.ts:2739/2787) next to a FRESHLY-recomputed `basis` "÷ N units = {share} €" (grafted at 2792-2794 from live breakdown.rows). The two were never produced by the same recompute, so on that one row the printed amount disagrees with its own "= share" tail. No money is mis-charged or dropped (billing/settlement and the ownerDirectTotal both use the persisted amount); the contradiction is purely the grafted display basis. Minimal fix would be to either recompute that term's persisted rows on read before grafting, or to derive the rendered owner-row amount from the same live row the basis came from (or null the grafted basis when basis.share != rowAmount).
verdict.reasoning: I opened buildingmanager.ts L2536-2898 (the whole getExpenseBreakdown handler), 1_base.ts L203-410 (the live engine + _equalPartyCount), the recompute function L3843-3932, its expense-edit caller L3042-3046, the sibling-sweep window L4030-4073, and the frontend renderer BuildingExpensePanel.js L683-934. The handler never recomputes the requested term's persisted ledger; it reads persisted e.amount for the row euro and grafts the live basis by expenseId|propertyId. The live engine always recomputes the requested term's share/basis from current state, while the persisted amount is only refreshed for _currentTerm() (expense edits) or the [now-11mo,now+12mo] window (lifecycle). An out-of-window divisor/denominator change therefore leaves a surviving owner row whose persisted amount is stale but whose grafted basis is fresh, and the UI prints both side-by-side. The occupancy/opt-in survival guards (L2646-2654) guarantee that whenever the row survives, a matching live row (hence a fresh basis) exists, so the contradiction is reliably reachable, not a corner case. The mechanism and all file:line citations in the finding match the code on disk; only the 'blank-render' severity tag is inaccurate (it is a self-contradicting value, not a blank, and does not ship wrong money on the billing path).

broken.title: _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges strips vacant/owner-resident rows UNCONDITIONALLY (no hasPayments guard); rebuild loop skips occupied/flag-off/inactive units → recorded owner καταβολές permanently deleted
broken.line: 3886-3997 (strip 3888-3895; rebuild-loop skips at 3966 occupied, 3970 flag-off, 3959-3961 inactive/amount-0, 3977 share<=0; payOwner writes payments at ownermanager.ts:776-783)
broken.brokenShape: The strip at 3888-3895 pulls EVERY source 'vacant'/'owner-fixed'/'owner-resident' row for the term with NO hasPayments check. priorSettle (3874-3884) snapshots the payments[], but they are only re-attached IF the rebuild loop actually re-pushes that row (carryOwnerPayments/applyCarriedSettlement at 3978-3995). The rebuild loop SKIPS a unit when: occupied.has(propertyId) at 3966 (tenant moved in), !isResident && !flagOn at 3970 (chargeOwnerWhenVacant flipped OFF), the expense fell out of billableExpenses at 3959-3961 (inactive-for-term / amount set to 0), or share<=0 at 3977. In every one of those cases the stripped row's recorded payments are NOT re-pushed and the building is saved (updateExpense at 3239, recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties at 4065), so the payment is physically gone from the DB. The early-return at 3935-3940 is one path to this but not required — the loop skips alone lose the money. Read paths (ownerstatement.ts:140, buildingmanager.ts:2645/4268) all guard `if (hasPayments) return/keep`, this WRITE path does not — it violates building.ts:326-328 'NEVER drop a row carrying recorded payments' and is the one money-path the shared invariant left unenforced.
broken.trigger: Building has expense E with chargeOwnerWhenVacant=true; unit U is vacant for term T so a source:'vacant' owner row R(amount €50) accrues. Landlord records a €50 owner καταβολή on R via payOwner (ownermanager.ts:776 pushes into R.payments). THEN any of: (a) landlord flips E.chargeOwnerWhenVacant OFF — updateExpense calls _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges (3234) then saves (3239); (b) a tenant moves into U — occupantmanager calls recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties which recomputes term T and the loop hits occupied.has(U) at 3966; (c) landlord soft-deletes/ends E or sets its amount to 0. In all three the €50 payment is stripped at 3895 and never re-pushed → permanently lost; the owner ledger silently drops €50 of recorded money with no audit trail.

verdict.codeEvidence: buildingmanager.ts `_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges` (3843-3998). priorSettle snapshots vacant/owner-fixed/owner-resident rows for the term by source+term ONLY (3875-3884) — payment-carrying rows included. Strip at 3888-3895: `building.ownerMonthlyExpenses.pull(e._id)` on ALL such rows with NO hasPayments exclusion. Re-attach of payments (carryOwnerPayments/applyCarriedSettlement, defined ownermanager.ts:97-153) happens ONLY at the two push sites: owner-fixed push (3898-3913) and the per-unit loop push (3962-3997). The per-unit loop SKIPS a unit on `occupied.has(propertyId)` (3966), `!isResident && !flagOn` (3970), `share <= 0` (3977), and never iterates expenses excluded from billableExpenses (3959-3961, amount-0 non-fixed). The function ends at 3998 with NO post-loop orphan re-attach sweep — a stripped priorSettle row whose unit was skipped is never re-pushed. payOwner writes real payments into a source:'vacant' row (ownermanager.ts:775-783 push + save). updateExpense saves the stripped state at 3239 (recompute at 3234); recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties saves at 4071 after iterating a ±12-month window (4030-4037). The READ guards (getBuildingExpenseBreakdown 2641-2645, computeOwnerEksodaByMonth 4265-4271) DO check `if (hasPayments) return true/!hasPayments` — but they only filter DISPLAY; they cannot resurrect a row physically removed by .pull and committed by save. building.ts:325-328 states the invariant the write path violates: "Every recompute that strips + rebuilds an owner row MUST carry payments forward."
verdict.reasoning: The finding is correct. `_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges` is the one WRITE path that does not enforce the hasPayments invariant. The strip at 3895 unconditionally removes every vacant/owner-fixed/owner-resident row for the term; payment carry-forward is wired ONLY into the re-push sites. The per-unit re-push loop has four skip gates (occupied move-in 3966, flag-off 3970, share<=0 3977, non-billable expense 3959-3961) plus the early-return at 3935-3940. In each, a row that carried recorded owner καταβολές is stripped but never re-pushed, and the building is then saved (updateExpense:3239, recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties:4071), physically deleting the payments. Concretely: (a) flag-off via updateExpense strips the current-term vacant row with its €50 καταβολή and returns at 3939 if it was the only opt-in expense and no owner-occupied units; (b) a tenant moving into a previously-vacant unit triggers recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties over the ±12-month window — occupied.has hits at 3966 and the row is dropped for every affected term. The READ-path hasPayments guards (2641, 4265) protect surfaces from double-count but operate on rows that no longer exist after this write. This violates the explicit schema-documented invariant (building.ts:326-328) and the owner-row-staleness invariant in memory ("never drop recorded payments; one predicate on all 4 money surfaces" — the WRITE surface is the one left unenforced). Severity critical: recorded owner money silently and permanently deleted with no audit trail. Minimal fix: in the strip, exclude rows where payments carry value (e.g. keep any row whose payments sum > 0), OR after the rebuild loop, re-push any priorSettle entry with recorded payments that the loop did not re-create (an orphan-reattach sweep mirroring the source:'repair' protection elsewhere).
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is in `_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges` (services/api/src/managers/buildingmanager.ts): the unconditional strip at line 3895 (`building.ownerMonthlyExpenses.pull(e._id)` over the source/term-only filter at 3888-3894) combined with the absence of any post-loop sweep re-pushing skipped priorSettle rows. Recorded payments are lost whenever the per-unit re-push loop skips the row's unit — occupied move-in (3966), chargeOwnerWhenVacant flipped off (3970), expense gone non-billable (3959-3961), share<=0 (3977) — or the early-return at 3935-3940 fires. The building is then committed via _saveBuildingWithVersionCheck (updateExpense:3239 for the current term; recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties:4071 across the ±12-month window 4030-4037), making the deletion permanent.

verdict.codeEvidence: BuildingDashboard.js:383-385 `ownerLedgerThisYear = (building?.ownerMonthlyExpenses||[]).filter(e => Math.floor(Number(e.term||0)/1000000)===currentYear)` — ONLY a year filter; no source/occupancy/flag/inactive/staleness check. ownerLedgerTotal (401-403) sums every row's amount; ownerUnpaid (409) = total − ownerPaid; both rendered in the "Owner expenses paid" tile (563-601, "Unpaid" value at 601). The 3 server surfaces DO drop stale rows: shared predicate isOwnerExpenseRowStale (ownerstatement.ts:122-151) returns stale when src is 'vacant'/'owner-resident' AND (expense gone:141 | vacant&&!chargeOwnerWhenVacant:144 | !active-for-term:145 | tenant-occupied-this-term:149) UNLESS row has recorded payments (137-140); breakdown panel inlines same drop (buildingmanager.ts:2641-2655); dashboard eksoda series inlines it (4265-4292); owner ledger calls it (ownermanager.ts:331-337). verdict.reasoning: The finding is real and money-wrong in current code. The BuildingDashboard "owner expenses paid vs unpaid" tile is the only one of five owner-liability surfaces that reads raw building.ownerMonthlyExpenses without the shared staleness guard. A 'vacant'/'owner-resident' row that the other surfaces drop term-anchored (most durably: an expense whose chargeOwnerWhenVacant was turned OFF, since addExpense/updateExpense recompute only _currentTerm() so the other in-year terms' rows persist with the flag now off and no payment; also: tenant-occupied out-of-window terms, or an inactivated/deleted source expense) is fully counted by ownerLedgerTotal and ownerUnpaid. Because isOwnerExpenseRowStale only ever drops rows with NO recorded payment (137-140), the inflated rows are precisely the unpaid ones — they land entirely in ownerUnpaid. Result: the Overview tile shows a strictly larger owner-total/owner-unpaid than the dashboard eksoda tooltip (computeOwnerEksodaByMonth) and the owner καταβολές ledger for the identical building/year — two surfaces in the same app disagree, the exact double-count/over-count the shared predicate was built to prevent. The double-count-against-tenant-rent framing is also valid for the occupied-out-of-window-term case (the same euro is in the tenant's rent AND in this tile). Verdict BROKEN; minimal leak: the year-only filter at BuildingDashboard.js:383-385 must apply the same source/occupancy/flag/active drop (it lacks any occupancy resolution because the frontend has no per-(propertyId,term) occupied set — the fix likely needs the server to expose a pre-filtered owner-ledger figure, since _toBuildingData ships the raw array).

broken.brokenShape: The strip at 3888-3895 unconditionally pulls EVERY source vacant/owner-fixed/owner-resident row for the term with NO hasPayments guard (verified: no payments check anywhere in 3843-3998). priorSettle (3874-3884) snapshots the row but is only consulted via .get() at the re-push sites (owner-fixed 3900, per-unit 3979). When chargeOwnerWhenVacant is flipped OFF: flagOn=false, and either (a) the early-return at 3935-3940 fires (optInExpenses empty && no owner-occupied units) before the per-unit pass runs, or (b) the per-unit pass runs but `if (!isResident && !flagOn) continue;` (3970) skips that vacant unit. Either way the vacant row is never re-pushed and its priorSettle entry is discarded → recorded money vanishes with no audit trail. broken.trigger: Owner records a καταβολή against a current-term vacant-unit building-expense share (source:'vacant' row gets payments[]). Landlord later PATCHes that expense with {chargeOwnerWhenVacant:false} (or any expense edit while the unit stays vacant). updateExpense (3234) calls _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges(_currentTerm()); the strip pulls the paid vacant row, the rebuild skips it, the payment is gone.

verdict.codeEvidence: buildingmanager.ts:3888-3895 — the strip `const stale = (building.ownerMonthlyExpenses||[]).filter(e => (e.source==='vacant'||'owner-fixed'||'owner-resident') && Number(e.term)===term)` then `for (const e of stale) building.ownerMonthlyExpenses.pull(e._id)` has NO hasPayments guard (verified across the whole function 3843-3998). priorSettle (3874-3884) snapshots each row but is consulted ONLY at re-push sites: owner-fixed `priorSettle.get(`${id}||${term}`)` (3900) and per-unit `priorSettle.get(`${expId}|${propId}|${term}`)` (3979-3981). Unmatched priorSettle entries are silently discarded — no orphan re-push exists; function ends at 3998. When chargeOwnerWhenVacant is flipped OFF: optInExpenses (3849-3851, requires e.chargeOwnerWhenVacant) is empty, so either the early-return at 3935-3940 fires (optInExpenses.length===0 && ownerOccupied.size===0) OR the per-unit pass hits `if (!isResident && !flagOn) continue;` (3970, flagOn=!!expense.chargeOwnerWhenVacant=false at 3963) → the vacant unit is skipped. Trigger: updateExpense does `expense.set(patchBody)` (3232) then UNCONDITIONALLY calls `_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges(building, realm._id, _currentTerm())` (3234-3238) and persists via `_saveBuildingWithVersionCheck(building)` (3239). A source:'vacant' row CAN carry payments: payOwner resolves the live subdoc and does `t.row.payments.push({date,amount,...})` (ownermanager.ts:776) on any charge in agg.charges incl. vacant rows. Contrast the READ path which IS guarded: breakdown filter `if (hasPayments) return true;` (buildingmanager.ts:2641-2645) and carryOwnerPayments/applyCarriedSettlement (ownermanager.ts:97-153) — but the read guard is moot once the write path deletes the row from the persisted ownerMonthlyExpenses array.
verdict.reasoning:
I independently opened and read the entire _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges function (3843-3998), the updateExpense trigger (3130-3246), the read-path occupancy guard (2599-2657), and the carry helpers (ownermanager.ts:97-153) plus payOwner's payment write (ownermanager.ts:726-785). The reviewer's structural reading is exactly correct in the CURRENT code:

(1) The strip at 3888-3895 unconditionally pulls every source vacant/owner-fixed/owner-resident row for the term with no hasPayments check.

(2) priorSettle is only ever read at the two re-push sites (3900, 3978-3981). There is NO loop over leftover priorSettle entries that failed to re-push — I read to the function's closing brace at 3998 and confirmed.

(3) Flipping chargeOwnerWhenVacant OFF makes optInExpenses empty, so for a building whose only non-tenant unit is the now-flag-off vacant unit, the early-return at 3935-3940 fires before the per-unit loop. Even with other owner-occupied units present, the vacant unit hits `if (!isResident && !flagOn) continue;` at 3970. In both cases the paid vacant row's priorSettle entry is never consulted → carried payments discarded.

(4) The trigger is real and unconditional: updateExpense calls the recompute on _currentTerm() after ANY expense.set, then saves. No earlier guard in updateExpense protects recorded owner payments (the validators there only check customAllocations shapes).

(5) The READ path's hasPayments guard (2641-2645) does NOT save us: it filters the PERSISTED ownerMonthlyExpenses array, which the write path has already deleted the row from. The breakdown/dashboard re-read the persisted array, they do not re-materialize vacant rows from scratch.

This drops recorded money (a καταβολή recorded against a current-term vacant share) permanently with no audit trail when the landlord flips the flag off — matching the documented invariant in building.ts:326-328 that every strip+rebuild MUST carry payments forward, which this write path violates. The READ-side sibling code at 2641-2645 proves the team KNOWS this invariant (it guards reads) but the guard was never mirrored into this write-side strip. Default is HOLDS, but I traced the exact leak path in code I read line-by-line, so the verdict is BROKEN. Minimal fix locus: the strip at 3888-3895 must exclude (or the rebuild must re-push) any row with recorded payments — exactly the hasPayments predicate already used at 2642-2645.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is at buildingmanager.ts:3888-3895 (the unconditional strip) combined with the rebuild's failure to re-push orphaned paid rows (early-return 3935-3940 / per-unit skip 3970). When chargeOwnerWhenVacant is PATCHed false on an expense whose current-term source:'vacant' row carries recorded payments[], updateExpense (3234-3238) runs the recompute: the strip pulls the paid row, optInExpenses is empty so the rebuild skips that vacant unit, the priorSettle entry is discarded, and _saveBuildingWithVersionCheck (3239) persists the loss. Minimal fix: add a hasPayments guard to the strip filter at 3888-3894 (exclude rows with recorded payments from `stale`), mirroring the already-present read-side guard at 2642-2645 — i.e. `&& !(Array.isArray(e.payments) && e.payments.some(p => Number(p&&p.amount) > 0))`.

broken.title: saveMonthlyStatement strips source:'expense' owner rows then re-pushes only amount>0 entries — re-saving a statement that zeroes/omits a previously-paid owner expense silently drops its recorded καταβολές

broken.brokenShape: The strip at 2486-2494 removes ALL source:'expense' rows for the term. priorExpenseSettle (2478-2484) captures payments keyed by expenseId, but the rebuild loop (2496-2511) re-pushes only entries where `entry.amount > 0` (guard 2497) AND present in the client-supplied ownerExpenses array (2334). A row whose corresponding ownerExpenses entry is omitted or set to amount 0 is stripped and never re-pushed; its captured priorExpenseSettle payments are discarded. The carry-forward only protects rows that survive into a positive-amount re-push.
broken.trigger: Landlord typed a variable owner amount (e.g. €100) into a monthly statement → source:'expense' row materialised → records a €100 καταβολή against it. Later re-opens the same month's statement, removes that line (or sets it to 0) and saves. (2) Lines 2478-2484: priorExpenseSettle Map captures source:'expense' rows for the term, keyed by expenseId — captures payments. (3) Lines 2486-2494: strips ALL source:'expense' rows for the term (`(e.source||'expense')==='expense' && e.term===Number(term)` → pull). (4) Re-push loop 2496-2511: `for (const entry of ownerExpenses)` with guard `if (!entry.amount || entry.amount <= 0) continue;` (line 2497) — only entries present in client array AND amount>0 are re-pushed; carryOwnerPayments(priorExpenseSettle.get(entry.expenseId)) (2498-2500) only runs for those survivors. No orphan-recovery pass exists for stripped rows whose entry was omitted/zeroed; their captured payments are discarded. Reachability confirmed: ownermanager.ts:323-350 — _aggregateOwners iterates ALL ownerMonthlyExpenses (src defaults to 'expense' at 350) and the staleness drop (326-345) is scoped to 'vacant'/'owner-resident' only, so source:'expense' rows surface in the owner ledger; ownermanager.ts:752,776-783 — payOwner resolves the row by .id(ownerExpenseId) and pushes a recorded payment onto it. verdict.reasoning: Independently re-read the function on disk at HEAD f6f75966. The reviewer's trace is accurate line-for-line. The strip at 2486-2494 is source-scoped (correct, fixes the older source-blind data-loss bug), and the priorExpenseSettle capture at 2478-2484 carries payments forward — but ONLY for rows that are re-pushed by the 2496-2511 loop, which is gated by (a) presence in the client-supplied ownerExpenses array and (b) `entry.amount > 0` (line 2497). A row whose corresponding ownerExpenses entry is omitted, or set to amount 0, is stripped and never re-pushed; carryOwnerPayments/applyCarriedSettlement are never invoked for it; its captured payments in priorExpenseSettle are simply discarded when the function returns. I confirmed reachability: source:'expense' rows are NOT theoretical — _aggregateOwners (ownermanager.ts:323/350) includes them in the owner ledger and the staleness guard does not drop them, and payOwner (ownermanager.ts:752/776) records payments directly onto them by _id. Therefore a previously-paid variable owner statement line, when removed or zeroed on a subsequent save of the same month, silently drops its recorded καταβολές. No test covers this omit/zero-with-prior-payment path (grep over __tests__ and e2e specs found none). This is a real dropped-money bug. Compare the sibling paths (_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges at 3962-3996, repair at 3568-3579) which re-derive their rows from the building's own state (vacancy/expense), so a row reappears as long as the underlying condition holds — whereas saveMonthlyStatement's source:'expense' rows are driven SOLELY by the client array, so omission is terminal.

broken.title: _distributeRepairCharge drops recorded payments on a source:'repair' / 'repair-vacant' owner row when a repair is edited to remove the owner portion or after the unit became tenant-occupied
broken.line: repair strip 3557-3580 (re-push gated by ownerPortion>0 at 3567); repair-vacant strip 3639-3645 (re-push gated by share>0 + vacant-only branch 3705-3727); caller updateRepair 4749

Neither strip has a hasPayments guard, unlike the read paths.
broken.trigger: (a) Owner pays a καταβολή on a 'repair' owner-portion row, then landlord edits the repair's chargeableTo from 'owners'/'split' to 'tenants' (ownerPortion→0); updateRepair re-distributes, strips the paid row, never re-pushes → payment lost. (b) A repair-vacant owner row carries a payment; a tenant later moves into that unit; landlord edits the repair (any field) → re-distribution writes the share to the new tenant's rent and drops the paid repair-vacant row → double-loss (vanishes from owner ledger; the comment at 4258 even asserts repair-vacant is never touched by tenancy changes, but an edit AFTER a move-in is exactly this sequence).

verdict.codeEvidence: services/api/src/managers/buildingmanager.ts `_distributeRepairCharge`: (1) source:'repair' path snapshots prior settlement into priorRepairSettle at 3551-3556, unconditionally strips matching rows at 3563-3565 (`ownerMonthlyExpenses.pull(e._id)`), and re-pushes WITH carried payments only inside `if (ownerPortion > 0)` (3567) via carryOwnerPayments(3568)+applyCarriedSettlement(3579). For chargeableTo:'tenants' the share math is sharePercentage=100 (line 3531) → ownerPortion = cost*(1-100/100) = 0 (line 3539) → the `if (ownerPortion > 0)` block is skipped, priorRepairSettle is never consumed, function early-returns at 3583-3592. (2) source:'repair-vacant' path snapshots into priorRepairVacantSettle at 3624-3632, strips unconditionally at 3643-3645, and re-pushes carried payments ONLY inside the vacant else-branch at 3705-3727 (carriedRV at 3713, applyCarriedSettlement at 3727); when `occupiedForRepair.has(String(unit.propertyId))` is true (3697) the share is written as a tenant monthlyCharge (3699-3704) and the carried repair-vacant settlement is discarded. _occupiedPropertyIdsForTerm (3812-3839) returns occupied propertyIds from tenant lease dates, so a tenant whose lease covers the term flips this true. Neither strip has a hasPayments guard — unlike the read/recompute twin at 4265-4271 which explicitly states "NEVER drop a row carrying recorded payments — recorded money must survive on every settlement surface (round-4-review-2 finding)". updateRepair (caller) at 4744-4749 does repair.set(patch) then calls _distributeRepairCharge with no other payment-preservation step. payOwner (ownermanager.ts 752, 776-782) resolves an ownerMonthlyExpenses row by ownerExpenseId and pushes onto row.payments, so a source:'repair' / 'repair-vacant' row genuinely carries recorded καταβολές.
verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds against the current code. _distributeRepairCharge strips owner rows for the edited repair unconditionally (3563-3565, 3643-3645) and only re-applies the carried settlement when the row remains a valid owner liability. Two reachable edits orphan a recorded payment:

(a) Reclassify a repair from chargeableTo:'owners' (or 'split' with owner portion) to 'tenants' after an owner recorded a καταβολή on the source:'repair' row. ownerPortion collapses to 0, the `if (ownerPortion > 0)` re-push is skipped, priorRepairSettle is discarded, and the function returns — the recorded payment is permanently deleted from the ledger with no audit trace. This needs NO tenancy change, just a repair edit, so it is the cleanest reachable leak.

(b) A repair-vacant owner row carries a payment, a tenant then occupies the unit for the charge term, and the landlord edits the repair (any field). On re-distribution occupiedForRepair is now true (3697), the share goes to a tenant monthlyCharge, and priorRepairVacantSettle is discarded — the καταβολή vanishes from the owner ledger while the cost re-materialises as tenant rent (double-loss of the owner's recorded money). Notably the comment at 4256-4262 argues repair-vacant is safe because it is "re-run only on repair add/edit, NEVER on a tenancy change" — but an edit AFTER a move-in is exactly that re-run, and that is when the drop occurs.

This violates the project's own established invariant (the hasPayments 'NEVER drop a row carrying recorded payments' guard at 4266-4271) on the write path while the read/recompute path is guarded. Severity high: silently dropped recorded money on a settlement surface. Minimal leak location: the two unguarded strips (3563-3565 and 3643-3645) whose carried snapshots (priorRepairSettle / priorRepairVacantSettle) are only consumed in the conditional re-push branches; an orphaned-settlement check is needed before discarding any stripped row that carries payments.

broken.brokenShape: ownerLedgerThisYear filters building.ownerMonthlyExpenses ONLY by calendar year (383-385). It applies NO isOwnerExpenseRowStale / occupancy / flag-off / inactive drop — unlike the other live surfaces: breakdown (buildingmanager.ts:2624-2658), dashboard eksoda series (4265-4294, which DOES drop stale vacant/owner-resident rows), and aggregation (ownermanager.ts:336-345). So a source:'vacant'/'owner-resident' row whose unit is now tenant-occupied for that term, or whose expense had chargeOwnerWhenVacant flipped off / went inactive, still contributes its full amount to ownerLedgerTotal (401) and ownerUnpaid (409). The same euro is then also the present tenant's rent → double-count, and the Overview tile disagrees with the dashboard eksoda chart on the same data.
broken.trigger: A unit had a vacant-owner charge for term T (source:'vacant', no payment). A tenant moves in for T (so the expense live-bills to their rent), OR the landlord flips chargeOwnerWhenVacant off. The dashboard eksoda chart drops the now-stale row (4279/4291) but the Overview paid-vs-unpaid tile keeps counting it — owner liability and the 'unpaid' bar are inflated by a euro that the tenant is actually paying.

verdict.codeEvidence: BuildingDashboard.js:383-385 — ownerLedgerThisYear = building.ownerMonthlyExpenses.filter(e => Math.floor(Number(e.term)/1000000) === currentYear). The ONLY filter is calendar year; no source/occupancy/flag/inactive/expense-gone drop. 401-409 — ownerLedgerTotal = Σ _rowAmount(e); ownerPaid = Σ _rowPaidAmount(e) (0 for an unpaid row with paid:false); ownerUnpaid = max(0, total − paid). 563-604 — the tile renders ownerPaid / ownerLedgerTotal (577-582) and "Outstanding": ownerUnpaid (599-601), gated on ownerLedgerTotal>0. Feed is RAW: buildingmanager.ts:99-104 _toBuildingData returns {...building, units, managedCount, unitCount} — ownerMonthlyExpenses is spread untouched. The OTHER live surfaces DO read-time-drop stale vacant/owner-resident rows: breakdown ownerEntries filter (buildingmanager.ts:2641-2655: expense gone→2647, flag-off→2648, inactive→2649, occupied→2652) and dashboard eksoda computeOwnerEksodaByMonth (4265-4291: expense gone→4273, flag-off→4279, inactive→4280, occupied→4291), and the shared predicate isOwnerExpenseRowStale (ownerstatement.ts:122-151, same four drops). The writer _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges strips/rebuilds ONLY Number(e.term)===term (3886-3895); the lifecycle window is bounded to trailing-12 + forward-12 months (4030-4037); and the expense add/update path recomputes only _currentTerm() (3042-3046). So an in-window non-current-term source:'vacant' row whose expense had chargeOwnerWhenVacant flipped off, or whose unit later becomes tenant-occupied for that term without a recompute trigger, persists in the array and is counted by the tile but dropped by the other two surfaces.
verdict.reasoning: The reviewer's claim holds against the current code. The paid-vs-unpaid tile in BuildingDashboard.js (383-409, rendered 563-604) is the 5th live owner-liability surface and it is the ONLY one that does not apply the shared staleness drop. I confirmed all three legs: (1) the tile filters only by year; (2) the server feeds the raw, unpruned ownerMonthlyExpenses array via _toBuildingData (99-104); (3) the breakdown (2641-2655) and dashboard-eksoda (4265-4291) surfaces both drop stale vacant/owner-resident rows on the exact four conditions (expense gone, vacant+flag-off, inactive-for-term, tenant-occupied-for-term), matching isOwnerExpenseRowStale (ownerstatement.ts:122-151). The leak is reachable because the writer never physically removes out-of-current-term stale rows: _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges strips only Number(e.term)===term (3886-3895), the lifecycle hook covers only a bounded 24-month window (4030-4037), and the expense create/update path recomputes only _currentTerm() (3042-3046). Concretely: a unit with a chargeOwnerWhenVacant expense accrues source:'vacant' rows for several recent in-window months; the landlord then flips chargeOwnerWhenVacant OFF (recompute touches only the current term) OR a tenant moves in for a past in-window term without a tenancy-change recompute for that exact term. The now-stale rows for the OTHER current-year terms keep their full amount: they inflate ownerLedgerTotal (the denominator) and ownerUnpaid (the Outstanding bar, since _rowPaidAmount is 0 for an unpaid paid:false row). The same euro is simultaneously billed to the present tenant's rent (engine buildingCharges) → double-count, and the Overview tile disagrees with the dashboard eksoda chart on identical data. One scoping correction to the reviewer's trigger: a stale row from a PRIOR calendar year is excluded by the year filter (383-385), so the leak requires a stale row whose own term is in the CURRENT calendar year but is not the term that a recompute last touched. That still leaves a real, reachable window (any current-year non-current-term vacant row after a flag-off or untriggered occupancy change). The fix is to apply the same occupancy/flag/inactive/expense-gone drop (or reuse isOwnerExpenseRowStale, which needs the live expense + per-(propertyId,term) occupancy that the frontend lacks — so this is most correctly fixed server-side by having _toBuildingData prune, or by feeding the dashboard the already-filtered eksoda series rather than the raw array).

broken.line: 383-409 (tile) vs services/api/src/managers/buildingmanager.ts:4265-4294 (dashboard eksoda), buildingmanager.ts:2641-2657 (breakdown), services/api/src/managers/ownermanager.ts:336-345 + services/common/src/utils/ownerstatement.ts:122-151 (ledger)

verdict.codeEvidence:
webapps/landlord/src/components/buildings/BuildingDashboard.js:383-385 — `ownerLedgerThisYear = (building?.ownerMonthlyExpenses || []).filter((e) => Math.floor(Number(e.term || 0) / 1000000) === currentYear)` — calendar-year ONLY, no source filter, no staleness predicate. Lines 401-409 sum every such row into ownerLedgerTotal/ownerPaid/ownerUnpaid; lines 563-601 render it as a "Paid vs Outstanding" progress tile (`finance.ownerLedgerTotal > 0 && (...) finance.ownerUnpaid`). NOTE: the SAME file's `recordedOwnerEksoda` (lines 335-340) DOES exclude `source==='vacant'/'owner-resident'/'owner-fixed'`, so the tile's omission is a real inconsistency, not a deliberate design.
_toBuildingData (buildingmanager.ts:88-105) returns `...building` raw — ownerMonthlyExpenses delivered to the client unfiltered.
The three other surfaces DROP the same rows: owner ledger ownermanager.ts:336-344 calls `OwnerStatement.isOwnerExpenseRowStale(...)` → `continue`; dashboard eksoda buildingmanager.ts:4279 `if (row.source === 'vacant' && !src.chargeOwnerWhenVacant) continue;`; breakdown panel buildingmanager.ts:2648 `if (e.source === 'vacant' && !src.chargeOwnerWhenVacant) return false;`; predicate body ownerstatement.ts:144 `if (src === 'vacant' && !expense.chargeOwnerWhenVacant) return true;`.
Trigger confirmed: updateExpense buildingmanager.ts:3234-3238 calls `_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges(building, realm._id, _currentTerm())` — current term only; the materialiser strips/rebuilds ONLY rows where `Number(e.term) === term` (lines 3880, 3893: `for (const e of stale) building.ownerMonthlyExpenses.pull(e._id)`). Flipping chargeOwnerWhenVacant OFF therefore removes only the current month's vacant row; the other 11 months persist as stale flag-off rows that the tile counts.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is at webapps/landlord/src/components/buildings/BuildingDashboard.js:383-409. The `ownerLedgerThisYear` filter that feeds the Overview "owner expenses paid vs unpaid" tile lacks the staleness/source-routing predicate that the API applies on the three settlement surfaces (owner ledger via isOwnerExpenseRowStale, dashboard Έξοδα chart, and building Έξοδα breakdown). A source:'vacant'/'owner-resident' row becomes stale when (a) its source expense is gone, (b) chargeOwnerWhenVacant is flipped OFF for a 'vacant' row, (c) the expense is inactive for that term, or (d) a tenant occupies the unit for that term — and because updateExpense recomputes ONLY _currentTerm(), the most common path is flipping chargeOwnerWhenVacant OFF, which strips only the current month's row and leaves the other 11 calendar-year rows stale. The tile counts those stale rows into ownerLedgerTotal and the Outstanding segment, so the building Overview shows owner liability the dashboard chart / breakdown / owner ledger all render as €0 for the same expense — opposite values on surfaces the landlord compares side by side. Minimal fix: apply the same source-routing + staleness guard (the file already excludes source vacant/owner-resident/owner-fixed for recordedOwnerEksoda at lines 335-340; the tile filter at 383-409 should at minimum apply that same source exclusion, ideally the full isOwnerExpenseRowStale predicate) before summing the tile totals.
verdict.reasoning: I independently opened all cited locations on disk at HEAD. (1) The tile filter (BuildingDashboard.js:383-385) is purely calendar-year with no staleness/source guard, and its outputs are rendered as a paid/outstanding tile (563-601). (2) _toBuildingData passes ownerMonthlyExpenses raw (`...building`, line 100). (3) All three other money surfaces apply the staleness drop with verbatim-matching line numbers (ownermanager.ts:336-344, buildingmanager.ts:4279, buildingmanager.ts:2648, ownerstatement.ts:144). (4) The trigger is real: updateExpense recomputes only _currentTerm() (3234-3238) and _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges strips/rebuilds only the matching-term rows (3880/3893), so 11 stale rows survive a chargeOwnerWhenVacant flip. This is a genuine, unguarded read-time divergence in current code that renders a wrong (inflated) owner-liability euro on the building Overview while three comparison surfaces show €0. The same-file recordedOwnerEksoda exclusion proves the author knew the source-routing rule and simply did not extend it to the new paid/unpaid tile. Confirmed BROKEN; the leak is localized to the client-side tile filter.

broken.title: Owner charge marked paid via setOwnerExpensePaid (paid flag, no payments[]) shows PAID on the Overview tile + dashboard Έξοδα chart but fully OUTSTANDING on the owner καταβολές ledger — opposite paid-state for the same charge on two settlement surfaces
broken.line: 2922-2923 (writer) vs services/api/src/managers/ownermanager.ts:346-366 (ledger: paidAmount from payments only) vs webapps/landlord/src/components/buildings/BuildingDashboard.js:393-399 + buildingmanager.ts:4302 (tile/chart: paid = paid?amount:0)
broken.brokenShape: setOwnerExpensePaid sets entry.paid=true and entry.paidDate but writes NO payment record (payments[] stays empty). The Overview tile (_rowPaidAmount, BuildingDashboard.js:398: fromFlag = e.paid ? amount : 0) and the dashboard eksoda chart (computeOwnerEksodaByMonth:4302: fromFlag = row.paid ? amount : 0) BRIDGE the flag → both count the row as fully paid. But _aggregateOwners (the live owner-debt ledger feeding GET /owners) computes paidAmount purely from payments[] (ownermanager.ts:347-348) and derives charge.paid = paidAmount >= amount-0.005 (366), ignoring the stored paid flag entirely → the charge shows outstanding = full amount, paid:false. The same charge is 'settled' on the tile/chart and 'still owed' on the ledger.
broken.trigger: Either (a) legacy rows marked paid via the now-removed breakdown checkbox (CLAUDE.md/tile comment BuildingDashboard.js:386-391 explicitly acknowledge such rows exist with paid:true and empty payments), or (b) any current PATCH /buildings/:id/owner-expense/:ownerExpenseId/paid (route still wired at routes.ts:372). Landlord sees that owner expense as 100% paid on the Overview/dashboard but the owner-debt ledger keeps billing it as fully outstanding.

verdict.codeEvidence:
WRITER — buildingmanager.ts:2922-2923 (setOwnerExpensePaid): `entry.paid = paid; entry.paidDate = paid ? new Date() : null;` — sets flag, writes NO payment record. Route still wired: routes.ts:371-373 `buildingsRouter.patch('/:id/owner-expense/:ownerExpenseId/paid', ... buildingManager.setOwnerExpensePaid)`.
TILE bridges flag→PAID — BuildingDashboard.js:393-399: `const fromFlag = e.paid ? _rowAmount(e) : 0; return Math.min(Math.max(fromPayments, fromFlag), _rowAmount(e));`. Comment 386-391 explicitly: "OR the full amount when the row carries the manual paid flag (paid:true) with no payment record... keeps old checkbox-marked-paid rows ... counted as paid".
CHART bridges flag→PAID — buildingmanager.ts:4302-4304 (computeOwnerEksodaByMonth): `const fromFlag = row.paid ? amount : 0; const rowPaid = Math.min(Math.max(fromPayments, fromFlag), amount); addPaid(term, rowPaid);`.
LEDGER ignores flag→OUTSTANDING — ownermanager.ts:346-366 (_aggregateOwners): `const payments = Array.isArray(row.payments) ? row.payments : []; const paidAmount = _round(payments.reduce(...));` then charge `paidAmount, outstanding: _round(amount - paidAmount), paid: paidAmount >= amount - 0.005`. grep for `row.paid`/`.paid` across ownermanager.ts returns matches ONLY in recomputeOwnerExpensePaid (l.66), carryOwnerPayments (l.117) and applyCarriedSettlement (l.147-150) — NONE on the read path. GET /owners (all, l.512-521) and GET /owners/:ownerKey (one, l.535-549) read `Collections.Building.find(...).lean()` and call `_aggregateOwners(...)` directly with no recompute/reconcile pass, so a bare-flag-paid row is never materialized into payments before aggregation. Client: restcalls.js:21-22 fetchOwners() → GET /owners feeds OwnerList/OwnerListItem with no flag bridge.
verdict.correctedDetail: A charge marked paid via PATCH /buildings/:id/owner-expense/:ownerExpenseId/paid (or any legacy row with paid:true and empty payments[]) shows PAID on the building Overview owner-expenses tile (BuildingDashboard.js:393-399) and PAID on the dashboard Έξοδα chart (buildingmanager.ts:4302-4304, both bridge `paid?amount:0`), but shows fully OUTSTANDING (paid:false, outstanding=full amount) on the owner καταβολές ledger GET /owners (ownermanager.ts:346-366), because _aggregateOwners derives paidAmount purely from payments[] and never consults row.paid. Minimal leak: _aggregateOwners at ownermanager.ts:346-366 must apply the same flag-bridge the tile/chart use (e.g. paidAmount = max(Σpayments, row.paid ? amount : 0)), OR setOwnerExpensePaid must write a synthetic payment, so the three settlement surfaces agree.
verdict.reasoning: All three legs of the finding are confirmed in the current code on disk at the exact lines cited. The writer sets a bare paid flag with no payment record via a still-wired route. The Overview tile and the dashboard Έξοδα chart both explicitly bridge `row.paid ? amount : 0` into their paid totals (with comments acknowledging bare-flag-paid rows). The owner-debt ledger _aggregateOwners — which feeds GET /owners (the settlement surface where the landlord records owner καταβολές) — computes paidAmount strictly from payments[] and derives paid = paidAmount >= amount-0.005, with zero reads of row.paid anywhere on the read path (verified by grep). The all/one handlers read lean docs and aggregate directly, with no recomputeOwnerExpensePaid/reconcile pass to materialize the flag. The codebase's own comment at ownermanager.ts:90-95 proves the agent knew these bare-flag rows exist and bridged them in the carry-forward path and the tile, but never in the live aggregation read — so the same charge legitimately renders settled on two surfaces and fully owed on the third. This is a concrete wrong-money / contradictory-state display bug, reachable today, not a misread or already-guarded case.

broken.title: _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges strips vacant/owner-resident rows unconditionally before the opt-in early-return, deleting recorded owner καταβολές on those rows — the one write path that violates the 'never drop a row carrying recorded payments' invariant every read path enforces
broken.line: 3886-3940 (strip 3888-3895 has no hasPayments guard; early-return 3935-3940; per-unit re-push 3962-3997 only for isResident||flagOn)
broken.brokenShape: priorSettle (3874-3884) snapshots payments for vacant/owner-fixed/owner-resident rows of this term. The strip at 3888-3895 then pulls ALL such rows for the term with NO hasPayments guard. owner-fixed rows are re-materialised (3897-3913, carrying payments). But a source:'vacant' row for an EMPTY unit is only re-pushed inside the per-unit loop when (isResident || flagOn) is true (3970). If the expense's chargeOwnerWhenVacant is OFF and the unit is not owner-occupied, the row is never re-pushed and carryOwnerPayments is never called for it — priorSettle still holds it but is discarded. There is no end-of-function re-attach pass (verified: carry only at the two push sites). The early-return at 3935-3940 makes it unconditional for the whole term when optInExpenses is empty and there are no owner-occupied units.
broken.trigger: Current-term source:'vacant' row carries a recorded owner καταβολή (payments[] non-empty, e.g. landlord recorded the owner's payment for the vacant unit's building-expense share). Landlord PATCHes that expense to flip chargeOwnerWhenVacant OFF (updateExpense → _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges at _currentTerm, then _saveBuildingWithVersionCheck at 3239). The vacant row — and its recorded payment — is permanently deleted from building.ownerMonthlyExpenses, so the παent money vanishes from the ledger, the dashboard, the breakdown, and the tile simultaneously.

verdict.codeEvidence: services/api/src/managers/buildingmanager.ts: (1) updateExpense applies the flag flip BEFORE recompute — `expense.set(patchBody)` at 3232, then `await _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges(building, realm!._id, _currentTerm())` at 3234, then `_saveBuildingWithVersionCheck(building!)` at 3239. (2) _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges reads the now-OFF flag: `optInExpenses = expenses.filter(e => e.chargeOwnerWhenVacant && ...)` at 3849-3851. (3) priorSettle snapshots vacant rows at 3875-3884 (matches source 'vacant'/'owner-fixed'/'owner-resident' && term). (4) STRIP at 3888-3895: `building.ownerMonthlyExpenses.pull(e._id)` for every matching source+term row — NO hasPayments guard, NO flag guard. (5) early-return 3935-3940: `if (optInExpenses.length === 0 && (ownerOccupied.size === 0 || activeExpenses.length === 0)) return;`. (6) per-unit re-push loop 3962-3996 guarded by `if (!isResident && !flagOn) continue;` at 3970 (flagOn=false after flip). (7) Function ends at 3998 — verified no end-of-function re-attach pass; carryOwnerPayments/applyCarriedSettlement only run at the two push sites (3899/3912 owner-fixed, 3978/3995 per-unit). Contrast: the READ path computeOwnerEksodaByMonth DOES guard — `const hasPayments = ((row.payments||[]).some(p=>Number(p.amount)>0)); if (!hasPayments) {...drop...}` at 4268-4293 — but it only computes from rows that still exist; it cannot recover a row the write path already pulled. payOwner records payments onto these subdocs: `t.row.payments.push({date,amount,...})` at ownermanager.ts:776, so a vacant row genuinely carries recorded καταβολές.
verdict.reasoning: The finding is confirmed in current code. I independently traced the full path. A source:'vacant' row for an empty unit can carry a recorded owner payment (payOwner pushes into row.payments[], ownermanager.ts:776). When the landlord flips chargeOwnerWhenVacant OFF, updateExpense applies the new flag in memory (3232) before calling _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges at the current term (3234). Inside that function the strip at 3888-3895 pulls every source-vacant/owner-fixed/owner-resident row for the term with no hasPayments and no flag check, physically removing the row (and its payments) from building.ownerMonthlyExpenses. priorSettle (3875-3884) holds a copy, but it is only consulted at the two re-push sites. The vacant row is re-pushed only when (isResident || flagOn) is true (3970); with the flag now OFF and the unit not owner-occupied, neither holds, so the row and carryOwnerPayments call never fire for it. If E was the only opt-in expense and there are no owner-occupied units, the early-return at 3935-3940 short-circuits before the loop, same outcome. The function ends at 3998 with no re-attach pass for orphaned priorSettle entries. _saveBuildingWithVersionCheck (3239) then persists the deletion. The read-path hasPayments guard (4268-4293) cannot help because the row no longer exists to be read. This is the single write path that violates the 'never drop a row carrying recorded payments' invariant the read paths enforce — recorded owner money vanishes from the ledger, dashboard, breakdown, and tile simultaneously. Note the trigger is general: ANY recompute at the row's term while the flag is OFF and the unit non-resident drops it; the flag-flip PATCH is the cleanest reproduction. The minimal leak is the unguarded strip at 3888-3895 combined with the absence of an end-of-function re-attach for priorSettle entries that were not re-pushed.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak location: services/api/src/managers/buildingmanager.ts strip at lines 3888-3895 (pulls vacant/owner-fixed/owner-resident rows with no hasPayments guard) combined with no end-of-function re-attach pass — the only two carryOwnerPayments call sites (3898-3913 owner-fixed, 3962-3996 per-unit with the `if (!isResident && !flagOn) continue` gate at 3970) never re-push a vacant row whose expense flag is OFF and whose unit is not owner-occupied. priorSettle (3875-3884) holds the payments but is discarded when the function returns at 3998 (or short-circuits at the 3935-3940 early-return). Minimal fix surface: after the per-unit loop, re-attach any priorSettle entry that (a) carried payments and (b) was not re-materialised, preserving its recorded καταβολές — mirroring the read-path hasPayments guard at 4268-4271 but on the write side.
