verdict.codeEvidence: setOwnerExpensePaid (buildingmanager.ts:2922-2923): `entry.paid = paid; entry.paidDate = paid ? new Date() : null;` — sets the flag with NO inspection of entry.payments[] and NO call to recomputeOwnerExpensePaid. The route is live+unguarded at routes.ts:371-373 (`buildingsRouter.patch('/:id/owner-expense/:ownerExpenseId/paid', ... setOwnerExpensePaid)`). The collected-money bridge is identical on all 3 surfaces: BuildingDashboard.js:393-399 `const fromFlag = e.paid ? _rowAmount(e) : 0; return Math.min(Math.max(fromPayments, fromFlag), _rowAmount(e));`; buildingmanager.ts:4298-4303 (inside computeOwnerEksodaByMonth's materialised-row loop) `const fromFlag = row.paid ? amount : 0; const rowPaid = Math.min(Math.max(fromPayments, fromFlag), amount);` — whose paidByTerm feeds dashboardmanager.ts:648-661 `_expensesRollup` (`const paid = Math.min(paidByTerm.get(term) || 0, owed); bucket.paid += paid;`). The OWNER LEDGER disagrees: _aggregateOwners (ownermanager.ts:346-366) computes `paidAmount = Σ payments`, `outstanding = _round(amount - paidAmount)`, `paid: paidAmount >= amount - 0.005` — payments-only, ignoring the flag. recomputeOwnerExpensePaid (ownermanager.ts:59-78) IS the payment-aware derivation and IS called by the rebuild paths (lines 138, 783) but is NOT called by setOwnerExpensePaid.
verdict.reasoning: Traced the exact path: payOwner records payments:[{60}] on a 100 charge and calls recomputeOwnerExpensePaid → paid=false (60<100). PATCH paid=true hits setOwnerExpensePaid (2922) which overwrites entry.paid=true WITHOUT recompute, leaving {amount:100, payments:[{60}], paid:true}. Building tile (BuildingDashboard.js:399) computes Math.min(Math.max(60,100),100)=100; dashboard Έξοδα rollup (computeOwnerEksodaByMonth 4303 → _expensesRollup 655) computes the same 100; but the owner καταβολές ledger (_aggregateOwners 364-366) computes paidAmount=60/outstanding=40/paid=false. Net: a 40-euro cross-surface disagreement, tiles over-stating collected owner income. All cited line numbers match the file on disk at HEAD f6f75966. The leak is real and the route is live/unguarded. NUANCE (lowers practical severity but not correctness): no current SOURCE component imports setOwnerExpensePaid — `grep -rn setOwnerExpensePaid webapps/landlord/src` returns ONLY restcalls.js:467; the breakdown checkbox toggle was removed (BuildingDashboard.js:388-391 comment: 'paid via the now-removed breakdown toggle'). So a user clicking the current UI cannot create this state via the toggle; it requires a direct PATCH or a stale client bundle. But the route, the restcall helper, and the unrecompute'd handler all still ship — the reviewer's TRIGGER ('PATCH the same ownerExpenseId paid=true') is exercisable against production and yields the wrong money. The minimal fix: setOwnerExpensePaid must call recomputeOwnerExpensePaid (or reject paid=true when 0 < Σpayments < amount) so the flag can never disagree with recorded καταβολές.

broken.title: Multi-building owner payment partial-commit reported to the landlord as a total failure (recorded money the UI says was not recorded)
broken.line: ownermanager.ts:787-801 (sequential per-building save loop; building #1's payments[] push is persisted before building #2's b.save() can throw VersionError→409); ownermanager.ts:764-771 (comment acknowledges partial commit 'accepted for v1'); OwnerPaymentDialog.js:206-238 (mutateAsync rejects → committedDraftIndexes is NOT pushed for this draft (push is success-only at line 207); with length 0 the catch shows only the raw error and leaves all drafts intact)
broken.brokenShape: A single auto/custom payment for an owner whose outstanding charges span 2+ buildings resolves all targets (ownermanager.ts:740-762), then saves buildings sequentially. If building #1 saves OK and building #2 throws VersionError (a concurrent edit / the documented test-account double-write), pay() throws 409 AFTER building #1's payment slice is already persisted. The client treats the whole call as failed: committedDraftIndexes stays empty, the toast shows the bare 409 ('...changed concurrently, please retry'), and the dialog keeps all drafts. The landlord believes nothing was recorded, but building #1 now carries a real καταβολή. (A retry does NOT double-pay because the server re-aggregates fresh outstanding and the cap/auto-spread account for the applied slice — but the landlord is misled about what landed.)
broken.trigger: An owner with outstanding charges in two different buildings; record one auto/custom payment; a concurrent write bumps the second building's __v between this handler's find and its save. Result: building #1's payment is persisted, the UI reports failure, and the charge silently shows settled on the next refresh while the toast said it failed.

verdict.codeEvidence: ownermanager.ts:787-801 — sequential per-building save loop with no MongoDB transaction: `for (const b of buildings ...) { ... await b.save(); } catch (err) { if (err.name === 'VersionError') throw new ServiceError(... 409) }`. Buildings are loaded as independent Mongoose docs at line 652 (`Collections.Building.find(...)`), no session/transaction. ownermanager.ts:764-771 comment explicitly: "a partial commit is possible only across DISTINCT buildings under concurrent edits, an accepted edge for v1". The targets/allocation can span multiple buildings (auto-spread at line 712 over `_ownerOwedLines(agg)` where `agg` aggregates the owner across ALL buildings; targets built 740-762; touchedBuildings 784). OwnerPaymentDialog.js: line 206 `const res = await mutation.mutateAsync(it.payload);` then line 207 `committedDraftIndexes.push(it.draftIndex);` — push is SUCCESS-ONLY (after the awaited call resolves). A single mutateAsync that rejects with 409 never pushes. Catch block 224-238: only when `committedDraftIndexes.length > 0` does it show `${t('Some payments were recorded; the rest were not.')} ${msg}` (line 236); otherwise (length 0) it shows the bare `msg` (line 237).
verdict.reasoning: The finding traces a real path. A single payOwner call for an owner whose outstanding charges span 2+ buildings produces a multi-building target set. The server mutates all targets in memory (774-785) then saves buildings sequentially (787-801) with no cross-building transaction — building #1's payments[] push is durably persisted by its own b.save() before the loop reaches building #2, whose VersionError throws 409. On the client this is ONE mutateAsync call; its rejection means line 207 never runs, so committedDraftIndexes stays empty (the tracking is per-DRAFT, not per-building). With length 0 the catch shows only the bare 409 text, NOT the 'Some payments were recorded' prefix. The landlord is told nothing was recorded, but building #1 carries a genuine καταβολή that shows settled on next refresh. The finding correctly self-limits severity: a retry re-aggregates fresh outstanding (line 652+) so it does not double-pay — this is a UI-truthfulness defect (misleading failure message on a partial commit), not money loss/double-count. The granularity mismatch is the minimal leak: server atomicity is per-building (no transaction), client commit-tracking is per-draft, so a single draft landing partially across buildings is invisible to the partial-success message branch. Default-HOLDS does not apply because I traced the exact path to the wrong-outcome in the code on disk; line numbers cited match the files.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak: OwnerPaymentDialog.js handleSubmit tracks commits at draft granularity only (committedDraftIndexes, pushed success-only at line 207), but a single payOwner call (one mutateAsync / one draft) can partially commit across multiple buildings server-side (ownermanager.ts:787-801 sequential save loop, no transaction). When building #1 saves and building #2 throws VersionError→409, the single mutateAsync rejects, committedDraftIndexes stays length-0, and the catch (OwnerPaymentDialog.js:234-237) shows only the bare 409 message instead of the 'Some payments were recorded; the rest were not.' prefix (line 236, gated on length>0). Result: landlord is told the whole payment failed while building #1's καταβολή is durably persisted and shows settled on next refresh. No double-pay on retry (server re-aggregates fresh outstanding at line 652), so impact is misleading-UI / wrong-reported-state, severity low. Minimal fix would be either wrapping the per-building saves in a mongo session/transaction (the documented v1 follow-on) or having the server return a partial-commit signal the client can surface.

broken.title: Tenant move-in to a previously-vacant unit physically DELETES the recorded owner καταβολή on that unit's 'vacant' row (write-path strip has no hasPayments guard)
broken.line: 3886-3896 (strip), 3962-3997 (rebuild occupied-skip at 3966); trigger fan-out occupantmanager.ts:1136,1573
broken.brokenShape: _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges strips EVERY source:'vacant'|'owner-fixed'|'owner-resident' row for the term via .pull() (3888-3895) with NO payment check, then in the rebuild loop does `if (occupied.has(String(unit.propertyId))) continue;` (3966). priorSettle captures the paid row's payments (3874-3884) but nothing re-homes them when the unit is now occupied, so the carried payments are never re-applied. The row — including its recorded payments[] — is gone from the building doc after _saveBuildingWithVersionCheck (the fingerprint at 4048-4067 sees before!==after, sets changed=true, and persists the deletion). This directly violates the codebase-wide invariant that a row carrying recorded payments must NEVER be dropped — enforced on the READ side at ownerstatement.ts:137-140 (isOwnerExpenseRowStale returns false when hasPayments) and buildingmanager.ts:4266-4271 (computeOwnerEksodaByMonth keeps paid vacant rows) — but the WRITE side that actually mutates the doc has no such guard.
broken.trigger: Unit P is vacant for term T; landlord records an owner καταβολή against P's source:'vacant' ownerMonthlyExpenses row (the row now has payments[].amount>0, paid=true). Later a tenant is added/updated whose lease window covers term T (occupantmanager create at :1136 or update at :1573) → recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties runs _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges for term T → the paid 'vacant' row is .pull()'d (3895) and NOT re-added because occupied.has(P) is now true (3966) → the recorded payment is permanently deleted from mongo with no audit trail. The owner ledger, dashboard eksoda, and statement PDF all then read €0 paid for a euro the owner actually paid.

verdict.codeEvidence: buildingmanager.ts:3888-3895 — the strip filter `(e.source==='vacant'||'owner-fixed'||'owner-resident') && Number(e.term)===term` then `for (const e of stale) building.ownerMonthlyExpenses.pull(e._id)` has NO payments/hasPayments condition; it removes every matching row including paid ones. priorSettle (3874-3884) only snapshots payments; carryOwnerPayments/applyCarriedSettlement (ownermanager.ts:97-153) re-home payments ONLY onto a row that gets re-pushed. buildingmanager.ts:3966 `if (occupied.has(String(unit.propertyId))) continue;` skips the now-occupied unit, so its priorSettle entry (key expenseId|propertyId|term, looked up at 3978-3980) is never consumed and the function returns at 3998 with no orphan re-home loop. recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties calls _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges at 4065 over terms now-11..now+12 (4030-4037); the before/after fingerprint at 4048-4067 sees before!==after and persists via _saveBuildingWithVersionCheck (4071). Triggered on move-in at occupantmanager.ts:1136 (add) and 1573 (update). The two READ surfaces explicitly guard paid rows — computeOwnerEksodaByMonth at 4265-4271 ("NEVER drop a row carrying recorded payments") and getBuildingExpenseBreakdown at 2641-2645 ("A row carrying recorded payments is never dropped") — but the WRITE strip has no equivalent guard, so those guards protect a row that has already been physically deleted.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak: services/api/src/managers/buildingmanager.ts:3888-3895 (unconditional .pull strip) + 3962-3997 rebuild that skips occupied units at 3966, with NO orphan re-home of unconsumed paid priorSettle entries before the function returns at 3998. When a tenant moves into a unit P that was vacant for term T and had a recorded owner καταβολή on its source:'vacant' row (payments[].amount>0, paid=true), the move-in fan-out (occupantmanager.ts:1136 add / 1573 update → recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties → _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges for term T in the now-11..now+12 window) strips the paid row at 3895, then 3966 `occupied.has(P)` is true so the row is never re-pushed and priorSettle.get(expenseId|P|term) is never consumed. The captured payments are discarded; _saveBuildingWithVersionCheck persists the deletion. Minimal fix: in the strip (3888-3895) skip rows with payments[].amount>0 (or, after the rebuild loop, re-push any priorSettle entry that carried payments but was not re-materialised), mirroring the read-side hasPayments guards at 4268-4271 and 2642-2645. This violates the codebase-wide invariant (project_owner_row_staleness_invariants) that a row carrying recorded payments must never be dropped.
verdict.reasoning: I independently opened buildingmanager.ts and read the full _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges body (3843-3998), the trigger recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties (4008-4074), the two read-side guards (2624-2658, 4245-4284), the carry helpers in ownermanager.ts (97-153), and both occupantmanager trigger sites (1136, 1573). The reviewer's trace holds in CURRENT code: (1) the strip at 3888-3895 is unconditional — no hasPayments check, confirmed by re-reading 3886-3895 verbatim; (2) carryOwnerPayments only carries payments onto a re-pushed row, and applyCarriedSettlement only fires on a pushed subdoc; (3) the rebuild loop continues past occupied units at 3966 without re-pushing, and there is no end-of-function loop that re-homes unconsumed paid priorSettle entries (the function ends at 3998); (4) the fingerprint at 4048-4067 includes source+propertyId so the deletion registers as changed=true and is persisted at 4071. The READ paths were hardened with explicit hasPayments guards (4268, 2642) precisely to honor 'recorded money must survive on every settlement surface', but those guards are powerless once the WRITE path has physically pulled the row from building.ownerMonthlyExpenses. The trigger is reachable (move-in writes occupancy then calls the recompute; term T of a current/recent lease is inside the now-11..now+12 window). This is real dropped-money: the owner's recorded καταβολή vanishes from mongo with no audit trail, and every downstream surface (ledger, dashboard eksoda, statement PDF) then reads €0 paid.

broken.title: Editing a repair's chargeTerm A→B drops the recorded owner καταβολή on its source:'repair' owner row (carry keyed on the NEW term only)
broken.line: 3551-3565 (priorRepairSettle keyed Number(e.term); strip across all terms), 3568 (rebuild uses priorRepairSettle.get(term) with term=Number(repair.chargeTerm) per 3541)
broken.brokenShape: _distributeRepairCharge snapshots prior repair-owner settlement into priorRepairSettle keyed by the row's term (3554), then strips ALL source:'repair' rows for the repair across every term (3557-3565), then rebuilds ONE row at the current repair.chargeTerm using carryOwnerPayments(priorRepairSettle.get(term)) (3568) where `term` is the NEW chargeTerm (3541). When the landlord moves the repair's chargeTerm from A to B, the prior paid row lived at key A; the rebuild looks up key B → miss → carryOwnerPayments(undefined) returns empty payments → the freshly-pushed row at term B has no payments and the term-A row was already pulled. Recorded owner money on the repair is silently lost.
broken.trigger: Owner-borne repair charged to term A; landlord records an owner καταβολή against the source:'repair' row (payments[].amount>0). Landlord then edits the repair and changes its chargeTerm to B (e.g. corrects which month it belongs to) → _distributeRepairCharge strips the term-A row and rebuilds at term B with an empty carry → the recorded payment vanishes.

verdict.codeEvidence: services/api/src/managers/buildingmanager.ts: line 3541 `const term = Number(repair.chargeTerm);` (NEW term B after edit). Lines 3551-3556 build `priorRepairSettle` keyed by the row's OWN term: `priorRepairSettle.set(Number(e.term), e)` for each `source:'repair'` row of this repairId. Lines 3557-3565 strip ALL `source:'repair'` rows for this repair across every term (`.pull(e._id)`). Line 3568 rebuilds with `carryOwnerPayments(priorRepairSettle.get(term))` where `term` = the NEW chargeTerm B → on a term change the prior row was keyed under OLD term A, so `.get(B)` is undefined. ownermanager.ts lines 103-105: `carryOwnerPayments(undefined)` returns `{ payments: [], priorPaid: false, ... }`. Line 3570-3578 then pushes a fresh row at term B with `payments: carriedRepair.payments` = []. Edit path confirmed: line 4744 `repair.set(repairPatchBody)` mutates chargeTerm to B in place; line 4749 `_distributeRepairCharge(building, repair, ...)`. The `_assertChargeTermNotFrozen` guard (lines 4507-4528) returns early for `chargeableTo === 'owners'` (line 4513) so it does NOT protect the owner-side payment. The repair-vacant path repeats the same defect: snapshot keyed `${propertyId}|${Number(e.term)}` (line 3623/3630), lookup `priorRepairVacantSettle.get(`${propertyId}|${term}`)` with NEW term (line 3714).
verdict.correctedDetail: Dropped owner money on repair chargeTerm edit. Two leak sites, both in `_distributeRepairCharge`: (1) source:'repair' — line 3568 `carryOwnerPayments(priorRepairSettle.get(term))` looks up by the NEW chargeTerm while the snapshot at line 3554 keyed the single prior paid row by its OLD term; since the strip at 3557-3565 already pulled the old-term row, the carry returns empty and the new term-B row is written with payments:[]. Because there is exactly one source:'repair' row per repair, the snapshot/lookup should not be term-keyed at all (key by repairIdStr or take the single surviving prior row). (2) source:'repair-vacant' — identical defect at line 3714 keyed `propertyId|newTerm` vs snapshot `propertyId|oldTerm` at 3630, dropping recorded καταβολές on vacant-unit repair shares when chargeTerm moves. Trigger: owner-borne repair (chargeableTo:'owners' or 'split') with a recorded owner καταβολή (payments[].amount>0), then PATCH /buildings/:id repair with a different chargeTerm.
verdict.reasoning: I independently opened the file at the cited lines and traced the full edit path end to end. The snapshot (line 3554) keys by the row's own term, the strip (3557-3565) removes the prior row across all terms, and the rebuild lookup (3568) uses the NEW chargeTerm — so on a term change the key misses and carryOwnerPayments(undefined) returns empty payments (verified in ownermanager.ts 103-105), wiping the recorded owner καταβολή. The edit route (4744 repair.set + 4749 _distributeRepairCharge) confirms the building still holds the old-term row when the new term is read. No upstream guard protects this: _assertChargeTermNotFrozen exits for owners-borne repairs and only concerns tenant-side frozen terms. The repair-vacant path has the same structural mismatch. This is dropped recorded money, matching the high-severity claim. The finding is not a misread and is not already guarded in current code.

broken.title: Editing a repair's chargeTerm A→B drops recorded καταβολές on its source:'repair-vacant' owner rows (carry keyed propertyId|term, rebuilt only at the new term)
broken.line: 3622-3632 (priorRepairVacantSettle keyed `${propertyId}|${term}`), 3634-3645 (strip across all terms), 3713-3715 (rebuild uses get(`${propertyId}|${term}`) with the new term)
broken.brokenShape: priorRepairVacantSettle is keyed `${String(e.propertyId)}|${Number(e.term)}` (3622-3623). The strip removes ALL source:'repair-vacant' rows for the repair across every term (3634-3645, intentionally to avoid orphaning term-A). The rebuild only writes rows for the CURRENT term (the loop pushes with term=the new chargeTerm, 3717-3722) and looks up carryOwnerPayments(priorRepairVacantSettle.get(`${unit.propertyId}|${term}`)) where term is the new chargeTerm (3714). A paid repair-vacant row whose prior term was A is keyed `P|A`; the rebuild at term B looks up `P|B` → miss → empty carry → recorded payment lost. (Same root defect as the source:'repair' case but for the vacant-unit repair share.)
broken.trigger: Repair charged to term A affects a VACANT unit P → a source:'repair-vacant' owner row is materialised; landlord records a καταβολή against it. Landlord edits the repair's chargeTerm to B → all repair-vacant rows pulled, the rebuild at term B finds no `P|B` carry → the recorded payment on `P|A` is dropped.

verdict.codeEvidence: services/api/src/managers/buildingmanager.ts. Line 3541: `const term = Number(repair.chargeTerm);` — on a chargeTerm A→B edit this is the NEW term B (the repair arg already carries the edited chargeTerm). Lines 3622-3623: `const repairVacantPaidKey = (e: any) => \`${String(e.propertyId)}|${Number(e.term)}\`;` keys each prior row by its OWN stored term — a row created at chargeTerm A is keyed `P|A`. Lines 3639-3645: strip pulls ALL source:'repair-vacant' rows for this repairId across every term (so the term-A row, with its recorded payments[], is deleted). Lines 3713-3715: rebuild does `carryOwnerPayments(priorRepairVacantSettle.get(\`${String(unit.propertyId)}|${term}\`))` with `term`=B → key `P|B`. The prior row was keyed `P|A` → miss → carryOwnerPayments(undefined). Confirmed in ownermanager.ts:103-105: `if (!prior) return { payments: [], priorPaid: false, priorPaidDate: null, priorAmount: 0 };` → fresh row at term B (push line 3717-3726) gets EMPTY payments; applyCarriedSettlement (ownermanager.ts:136-152) then sets paid=false. The recorded καταβολή on the P|A row is gone.
verdict.reasoning: I independently opened the file and traced the path. The carry map priorRepairVacantSettle is keyed by each prior row's OWN term (Number(e.term), line 3623), but the rebuild lookup uses the post-edit chargeTerm `term` (line 3541 = new B; lookup at line 3714). When a landlord edits a repair's chargeTerm from A to B and a unit affected by the repair is vacant: the strip at 3639-3645 deletes the term-A repair-vacant row (which holds recorded καταβολές in payments[]), and the rebuild at term B looks up `P|B`, misses the `P|A` carry entry, and pushes a fresh row with empty payments/paid=false. carryOwnerPayments(undefined) returns empty (ownermanager.ts:103) confirming the loss is silent. No compensating logic, no normalization that would make prior rows be keyed at term B, and no test exercises the chargeTerm-edit carry path (repairCharges.test.js only tests computeRent-side filtering; ownerEksodaByMonth/ownerStatement seed rows directly without re-running _distributeRepairCharge with a changed term). This is the identical root defect as the source:'repair' case (line 3554 stores by old term, 3568 looks up by new term) — the reviewer correctly identifies it as the same class. Result: dropped recorded money (high severity). Minimal leak: the term component of the lookup key at line 3714 (and 3568 for source:'repair') must not assume prior carry rows share the new chargeTerm; carry should be matched per-propertyId (single repair-vacant row per propertyId for a given repair) rather than per (propertyId|new-term), or the strip should preserve/transfer the prior term's payments onto the new term's row.

broken.title: Non-atomic multi-building owner payment double-pays the first building on client retry after a mid-save 409
broken.line: 787-801 (sequential per-building save loop, VersionError→409 after building #1 already persisted); webapps/landlord/src/components/owners/OwnerPaymentDialog.js:206-227 (committed only on resolve; whole draft re-sent on retry)
broken.brokenShape: pay() resolves all targets, then saves each touched building sequentially (787-801). If the owner has charges in 2+ buildings and building #1 saves successfully but building #2 throws VersionError, the handler throws 409 (793-798) AFTER building #1's payments[].push is already committed to mongo (791). The single payOwner call is thus partially applied. The client's mutateAsync rejects → committedDraftIndexes does NOT receive this draft (it is pushed only after a resolved mutateAsync, OwnerPaymentDialog.js:207) → on the user's retry the WHOLE draft (covering both buildings) re-posts → building #1's charge receives a SECOND payment slice. The server-side outstanding cap (ownermanager.ts:695) is computed from the snapshot loaded at 652-658 before either save, so on the fresh retry building #1 now shows reduced outstanding and the cap correctly limits, but if the original slice exactly settled the charge the retry will still 422; if it partially settled, the retry double-applies up to the (now smaller) remaining outstanding — net over-payment relative to the typed amount across the two attempts.
broken.trigger: An owner has outstanding charges in building A and building B; landlord settles both in one draft (auto or custom allocation spanning both). A concurrent edit bumps building B's __v between the handler's find (652) and its save (791). Building A saves, building B throws VersionError → 409. Landlord retries the same payment → building A's charge is paid twice.

verdict.codeEvidence: ownermanager.ts pay(): allocation resolved against ALL the owner's charges across every building (chargeById built from agg.charges, 737-739; targets resolved to whichever building owns each charge, 749-762). Save loop 787-801 is SEQUENTIAL per touched building; building #1's t.row.payments.push (776-783) + b.save() (791) commit BEFORE building #2; if building #2 throws VersionError the handler throws 409 (793-798) AFTER #1 is persisted — the code comment at 764-771 explicitly calls this "a partial commit is possible only across DISTINCT buildings under concurrent edits, an accepted edge for v1." Custom-mode cap is recomputed from the FRESH snapshot each call: line 695 `if (a.amount > c.outstanding + 0.005)` 422s, but a PARTIAL slice (e.g. €40 on a €100 charge whose remaining is now €60 after attempt 1) passes (40 ≤ 60). Client OwnerPaymentDialog.js: each draft = ONE payOwner call (104, 174-212); committedDraftIndexes.push happens only AFTER a RESOLVED mutateAsync (206-207), so a single cross-building draft whose mutateAsync rejects with 409 leaves committedDraftIndexes empty → the catch block's drop+refresh (224-228) is skipped entirely (guarded by `committedDraftIndexes.length > 0`) → the unmodified full custom draft survives. The client custom guard (137) only checks allocSum>amt, never live outstanding, so a retry re-posts the SAME [{cA,40},{cB,50}] allocation; cA (building #1) is re-applied a SECOND €40 (now €80 recorded vs the single €40 the landlord typed). draftToPayload custom branch (127-141) permits partial slices (no slice==outstanding requirement). No idempotency key / duplicate detection exists on the server (grep: only string `reference`, no nonce/requestId).
verdict.correctedDetail: Real but narrower than the title implies. NOT vulnerable in AUTO mode: autoSpreadOwnerPayment (608-621) fills oldest-first via min(remaining,line.amount) then `break`s when remaining is exhausted, so the only partially-filled charge is the LAST one reached and no later building is touched/saved — a saved building's charges are always fully settled (outstanding→0), and on retry _ownerOwedLines filters outstanding<=0.005 (595), so they cannot be re-paid. NOT vulnerable for an EXACT custom settle either: the retry's cap (695) sees outstanding 0 and 422s. The leak is specifically CUSTOM mode with a PARTIAL slice on a building-#1 charge: building #1 saves, building #2 (different building, concurrently __v-bumped between find at 652 and save at 791) 409s, the single-draft client path skips drop+refresh (OwnerPaymentDialog.js:224), and the retried partial slice on the already-committed building-#1 charge re-applies (capped only to the reduced remaining outstanding, 695) — double-applying a slice the landlord typed once. Trigger: owner with outstanding charges in 2+ buildings, custom allocation with a partial amount on building A's charge, concurrent edit bumps building B's __v mid-handler, building A iterated/saved before building B. Money landed stays ≤ owed (bounded, no negative outstanding, no dropped money), but the landlord's single intended slice is recorded twice. Minimal fixes: wrap the per-building saves in a mongo transaction/session (the comment already names this as the follow-on), OR have the client treat a 409 on a single-draft cross-building payment the same as a partial-commit (refetch owners + force the user to re-derive the draft from fresh outstanding before any retry).
verdict.reasoning: I opened both cited files and traced the exact path. The server save loop (787-801) is non-atomic across distinct buildings and the code comment (764-771) admits the partial-commit edge. The decisive question was whether the server outstanding cap defangs the retry double-pay. It does for auto mode (full-fill-then-break means a saved building is always fully settled) and for exact custom settles (retry 422s on outstanding 0). But for a PARTIAL custom slice on the already-committed building, the cap is recomputed from the post-attempt-1 (reduced) outstanding and the same partial slice passes again — re-applying it. The client confirms the retry re-posts the whole draft: committedDraftIndexes is only pushed after a resolved mutateAsync, so a single cross-building draft that 409s never enters the drop/refresh branch (gated on length>0), and no other refresh fires on 409. There is no idempotency/duplicate guard server-side. This is a concrete data-state + concurrent-edit + lifecycle sequence that makes the current code record money twice against one charge from one user action, so the finding is confirmed (in the narrower custom-partial form).

broken.line: ownermanager.ts:346-366 (paidAmount/outstanding/paid from payments[] only); BuildingDashboard.js:393-399 (fromFlag = e.paid ? amount : 0; Math.max(fromPayments,fromFlag)); buildingmanager.ts:4302-4303 (identical flag-bridge in computeOwnerEksodaByMonth, drives dashboard rollup); setOwnerExpensePaid buildingmanager.ts:2918-2925 sets paid=true with NO payment pushed

broken.trigger: On a building's Overview/Expenses, tick the paid checkbox for an owner-side monthly-expense row (or any legacy checkbox-paid row carried forward). verdict.codeEvidence: ownermanager.ts:346-349 — aggregation computes `const payments = Array.isArray(row.payments) ? row.payments : []; const paidAmount = _round(payments.reduce((s,p)=>s+(Number(p.amount)||0),0))`; line 366 sets `paid: paidAmount >= amount - 0.005` and line 365 `outstanding: _round(amount - paidAmount)`. The bare `row.paid` flag is NEVER read in this path (grep of the file: `row.paid` appears only as a WRITE at lines 66, 147, 150 inside recomputeOwnerExpensePaid/applyCarriedSettlement; the only read of `prior.paid` is line 117 for the carry, not the aggregation). The read endpoints `all` (514-521) and `one` (542-549) load `.lean()` buildings and call `_aggregateOwners` with NO recompute, so a row's bare flag flows straight in. buildingmanager.ts:2922-2923 setOwnerExpensePaid does `entry.paid = paid; entry.paidDate = paid ? new Date() : null;` and pushes NOTHING to payments[]. ownermanager.ts:146-148 applyCarriedSettlement PRESERVES that bare paid across recomputes when amount unchanged (`row.paid = true`). BuildingDashboard.js:392-399 `_rowPaidAmount`: `fromFlag = e.paid ? _rowAmount(e) : 0; return Math.min(Math.max(fromPayments, fromFlag), _rowAmount(e))` over `building.ownerMonthlyExpenses` (line 383). buildingmanager.ts:4298-4303 computeOwnerEksodaByMonth: identical `fromFlag = row.paid ? amount : 0; rowPaid = Math.min(Math.max(fromPayments, fromFlag), amount)`. Consumers: owners/[id].js:52-54 derives paid from owner.totalPaid (ledger, unbridged), line 176 colours by c.paid; OwnerPaymentDialog.js:77-83 filters outstanding>0.005 so the flagged-paid row still lists as settleable.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is the asymmetric paid-derivation between two surface families reading the same building.ownerMonthlyExpenses rows. After PATCH /buildings/:id/owner-expense/:id/paid (setOwnerExpensePaid, buildingmanager.ts:2918-2925) a row holds paid=true with payments=[]. (1) Building Overview "owner expenses paid" tile (BuildingDashboard.js:392-399) and the realm Dashboard Έξοδα paid rollup (computeOwnerEksodaByMonth, buildingmanager.ts:4298-4303) bridge the bare flag → rowPaid = amount = fully PAID. (2) Owner ledger (_aggregateOwners ownermanager.ts:346-366, consumed by GET /owners + GET /owners/:key → owners/[id].js paid card + charges badge + OwnerPaymentDialog.outstandingCharges) reads payments[] only → paidAmount=0, outstanding=amount, paid=false = fully UNPAID. applyCarriedSettlement:146-148 keeps the flag alive across recomputes, so the contradiction is durable, and the OwnerPaymentDialog will happily record a καταβολή against a charge the Overview/Dashboard already count as paid (double-count of money against a notionally-settled liability). Minimal fix: make _aggregateOwners bridge the bare paid flag the same way the two building/dashboard surfaces do (or make setOwnerExpensePaid push a synthetic settling payment), so all "Owner expenses paid" surfaces share one paid predicate.
verdict.reasoning: I opened all four cited locations and they match the file on disk exactly. The aggregation (ownermanager.ts:346-366) derives paid/outstanding from payments[] alone and never consults row.paid; both building-facing surfaces (BuildingDashboard.js:392-399 and buildingmanager.ts:4298-4303) explicitly bridge the bare flag via Math.max(fromPayments, paid?amount:0). setOwnerExpensePaid writes the flag with no payment, and applyCarriedSettlement deliberately preserves it. The two read paths (all/one) run no recompute on read, so the divergent state survives. The result is the same physical ownerMonthlyExpenses row reported as fully PAID on the building Overview + Dashboard tiles and fully UNPAID/Outstanding on every owner-καταβολές surface, with the payment dialog still offering it for settlement — confirmed double-count risk. Not guarded anywhere in current code; the carry helper actively keeps the contradiction durable.

broken.title: Express-pay records UNDISCOUNTED owed-line sum while the dialog shows the discounted figure — over-records cash by the full discount on any contract-discounted tenant
broken.line: 103-189 (_computeOwedLines), 548-613 (bulkExpressPayment), 555-557 + 566-567 + 602 (amount), cross-ref 7_total.ts:64-67 (grandTotal subtracts discount), frontdata.ts:129 (UI value), ExpressPaymentDialog.js:46-48
broken.brokenShape: _computeOwedLines (rentmanager.ts:103-189) pushes previousBalance + rent(preTax) + propertyCharge + buildingCharge/repair + vat(rent.total.vat, already net of the negative discount-VAT line from 4_vats.ts:75-83) + extracharge, but NEVER subtracts the discount principal in rent.discounts[]. grandTotal (7_total.ts:65) = preTax+charges+building+debts - discount + vat + balance DOES subtract it. So for a rent with rent.discounts populated (contract.discount → 3_discounts.ts:13-22 origin 'contract'), monthlyOwed = sum(monthLines) (rentmanager.ts:555-557) overstates grandTotal by exactly the discount principal. bulkExpressPayment then sets the recorded payment amount = monthlyOwed (rentmanager.ts:567, persisted at :602) with NO clamp to grandTotal before passing it to _updateByTerm (:627). Meanwhile ExpressPaymentDialog.js:46-48 derives the displayed monthlyOwed from r.totalWithoutBalanceAmount = grandTotal - balance (frontdata.ts:129) = the DISCOUNTED amount. UI shows €900, server writes €1000.
broken.trigger: Tenant on a lease with contract.discount = 100 (e.g. rent 1000, no VAT). Landlord opens the rents-list Express εξόφληση dialog, sees the unit's owed as €900, ticks 'monthly' and submits. POST /api/v2/rents/express records a €1000 transfer payment. rent.total.payment(1000) > grandTotal(900) → next month carry-in (5_balance.ts:17-20 = prev.grandTotal - prev.payment = 900-1000 = -100) is a phantom €100 credit that silently understates the following month's bill; the receipt/saved-tile overstate cash received by €100. Reachable from live ExpressPaymentDialog.js:138 with no user override (rentmanager.ts:458 comment confirms caller cannot pass an amount). No test covers express-pay with a discount.

verdict.codeEvidence: rentmanager.ts:103-189 (_computeOwedLines) pushes lines for: previousBalance (106-113), preTaxAmounts (117-129), charges (132-142), buildingCharges (145-160), VAT scalar = rent.total.vat (169-176), debts/extracharge (179-186). There is NO branch reading rent.discounts[] — the discount principal is never subtracted. 7_total.ts:64-67: grandTotal = round((preTaxAmount + charges + buildingChargesTotal + debts - discount + vat + balance)*100)/100 — explicitly subtracts `discount` (the sum of rent.discounts[], computed at 7_total.ts:38-43). The discount line is populated for any tenant with contract.discount via 3_discounts.ts:10-23 (origin 'contract'); contract.discount = occupant.discount || 0 at rentmanager.ts:790; tenant.discount is a writable schema field (tenant.ts:147) set via tenant-create/duplicate (NewTenantDialog.js:149) and lease/import flows (BillingForm.js:23-25 comment). 4_vats.ts:75-83 pushes a NEGATIVE vat line per discount, so rent.total.vat is already net of discount-VAT — meaning _computeOwedLines's vat line (rentmanager.ts:169) reflects the discount's VAT but NOT its principal. bulkExpressPayment: monthlyOwed = _round(monthLines.reduce(s+l.amount)) (rentmanager.ts:555-557); on it.monthly===true the recorded payment amount = monthlyOwed (rentmanager.ts:566-567) persisted at rentmanager.ts:602. UI side: ExpressPaymentDialog.js:46-49 monthlyOwed = Number(r.totalWithoutBalanceAmount); frontdata.ts:129 totalWithoutBalanceAmount = rent.total.grandTotal - rent.total.balance (the DISCOUNTED figure). No clamp: _updateByTerm validates only payment date range (rentmanager.ts:982-1031) and amount>=0.01 (1052-1054), never grandTotal; comment at rentmanager.ts:995 states "Contract.payTerm has no clamp". Over-record consequence: 5_balance.ts:17-20 next-term balance = prev.grandTotal - prev.payment, which goes negative (phantom credit) when payment > grandTotal.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak location: rentmanager.ts:103-189 (_computeOwedLines) omits a subtractive `rent.discounts[]` line, so the express-pay monthlyOwed sum at rentmanager.ts:555-557 overstates `grandTotal - balance` by exactly the discount PRINCIPAL (the discount's VAT is already reflected via rent.total.vat; only the principal is missing). bulkExpressPayment records that inflated amount as the transfer payment (rentmanager.ts:602) with no clamp. The displayed figure (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:46-49 via frontdata.ts:129 grandTotal-balance) IS discounted, so the dialog shows e.g. €900 while the server writes €1000 on any tenant with a non-zero discount; the €100 over-record then becomes a phantom negative carry-in next month via 5_balance.ts:17-20. Minimal fix: have _computeOwedLines subtract sum(rent.discounts[].amount) (clamping the affected/rent line, or emitting a negative 'discount' line) so monthlyOwed == grandTotal - balance, matching the UI and grandTotal. Note the same _computeOwedLines is reused by the regular single-payment auto-spread at rentmanager.ts:1048, but that path is user-confirmed; express (auto-recorded, no review) is the silent-money path the finding correctly targets.
verdict.reasoning: Independently opened and read all cited files. The asymmetry is real and unguarded in current HEAD code: grandTotal subtracts the discount principal (7_total.ts:65) but _computeOwedLines does not (no rent.discounts[] handling anywhere in lines 103-189). bulkExpressPayment sums those lines into the recorded payment amount with no clamp against grandTotal (confirmed by the explicit "Contract.payTerm has no clamp" comment at 995 and the date-only validation in 982-1031). The UI sources its displayed owed from totalWithoutBalanceAmount = grandTotal - balance (frontdata.ts:129, ExpressPaymentDialog.js:48), which is discounted — so the UI/server disagree by the discount principal, the express endpoint silently over-records cash, and the surplus poisons next month's balance (5_balance.ts:17-20 → negative carry-in). The discount field is reachable (tenant.ts:147 writable, NewTenantDialog.js:149 duplicate path, BillingForm comment confirms lease/import populate it) and 3_discounts.ts:10-23 turns it into a contract-origin discount on every term. No express-pay-with-discount test exists. The reviewer's only imprecision was implying the discount-VAT is also missing; in fact rent.total.vat already nets the negative discount-VAT line (4_vats.ts:75-83) so the over-record equals the principal only — which still matches their stated €100 example (no-VAT case) and their core claim. Verdict: BROKEN.

broken.title: Express-pay records FULL term owed against a partially-paid term, silently destroying the existing payment and recording more than the UI showed
broken.line: 548-557, 596-614 (bulkExpressPayment) + 1052-1118, 1235-1243 (_updateByTerm replaces payments)
broken.brokenShape: bulkExpressPayment computes monthlyOwed = sum of _computeOwedLines(targetRent) (rentmanager.ts:548-557) which is the GROSS per-line owed for the term and is NOT reduced by payments already recorded on that rent. It builds a paymentData.payments array containing ONLY the one new express payment (lines 600-608). _updateByTerm then runs Contract.payTerm with settlements.payments = just that one payment; taskPayments (6_payments.ts:50-54) pushes only settlements.payments, so the term's existing payments array is REPLACED, not appended (the persist at rentmanager.ts:1235-1243 does $set:{rents}). Meanwhile the UI (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:46-66) computes monthlyOwedRemaining by subtracting r.payment already paid, so it shows the landlord the REMAINING owed (e.g. €200 of a €400 term).
broken.trigger: Tenant has a €400 term with €200 already recorded (partiallypaid). Landlord opens the Express payment drawer: the row shows 'Μηνιαίο €200' (remaining). Landlord ticks it and submits. Server resolves monthlyOwed=€400 (full, _computeOwedLines ignores the €200 already paid), records ONE €400 transfer dated today, and the prior €200 payment (its date/reference/type) is wiped. Recorded amount (€400) ≠ amount the UI offered (€200); the first payment's audit record is destroyed.

verdict.codeEvidence: rentmanager.ts:548 `_computeOwedLines(targetRent)` builds lines from rent.preTaxAmounts/charges/buildingCharges/total.balance/total.vat/debts — all GROSS. 7_total.ts:59-69 proves preTaxAmounts/charges are full-bill (only rent.total.payment line 69 tracks paid), so monthlyOwed (rentmanager.ts:555-557) ignores the €200 already paid → 400. rentmanager.ts:596-611 builds paymentData.payments = a SINGLE new express payment (no read of targetRent.payments). rentmanager.ts:731-737 explicit comment: "payments array is REPLACED, not appended. Callers must include all existing payments + new ones." rentmanager.ts:1052 `settlements.payments = paymentData.payments.filter().map()` (only the new payment). contract.ts:283 payTerm → BL.computeRent for the target term using that settlements; index.ts:28 starts rent.payments=[]; 6_payments.ts:10-50 pushes ONLY settlements.payments into the fresh array. rentmanager.ts:1241 persists `$set:{rents}`. UI ExpressPaymentDialog.js:46-66 computes monthlyOwedRemaining = monthlyOwed(400) − r.payment(200) and displays row.monthly=200 (line 268); submit (lines 127-132) sends only booleans {monthly:true}, not the amount.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is in bulkExpressPayment: it is a caller of _updateByTerm that violates _updateByTerm's documented REPLACE-semantics contract (rentmanager.ts:731-737). For a partially-paid term (e.g. €400 owed, €200 already recorded), the dialog displays the REMAINING €200 (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:55-66,268) but bulkExpressPayment resolves monthlyOwed=€400 GROSS via _computeOwedLines (rentmanager.ts:548-557, gross because 7_total.ts never reduces preTaxAmounts/charges by payment) and constructs paymentData.payments with ONLY one new €400 transfer (rentmanager.ts:596-611) — it never reads/re-includes targetRent.payments. _updateByTerm then sets settlements.payments to just that one payment (rentmanager.ts:1052) and Contract.payTerm rebuilds the term via computeRent, whose 6_payments task pushes only settlements.payments into a fresh rent.payments=[] (index.ts:28, 6_payments.ts:50). Result on persist (rentmanager.ts:1241 $set:{rents}): the prior €200 payment record (its date/reference/type/audit) is destroyed and a single €400 payment is recorded — €400 ≠ the €200 the UI offered. Minimal fix: bulkExpressPayment must either (a) prepend the existing targetRent.payments into paymentData.payments and set amount to only the remaining owed, or (b) compute owed net of rent.total.payment so amount matches what the UI showed AND still preserve existing payments.
verdict.reasoning: I independently opened every link in the chain. (1) _computeOwedLines (103-189) reads only bill fields; 7_total.ts (59-69) confirms the stored rent keeps full-bill preTaxAmounts/charges and tracks payment only in total.payment — so monthlyOwed is gross, not remaining. (2) bulkExpressPayment (468-614) builds a single new-payment array with no reference to existing payments. (3) _updateByTerm has an explicit comment (731-737) documenting REPLACE-not-append and that callers MUST include existing payments — bulkExpressPayment does not. (4) settlements.payments = paymentData.payments at 1052 (replace), Contract.payTerm (283) rebuilds via computeRent which starts rent.payments=[] (index.ts:28) and 6_payments pushes only settlements.payments (6_payments.ts:50). (5) persist is $set:{rents} (1241). (6) The UI shows the remaining (€200) while booleans-only items mean the server re-resolves gross (€400). All line numbers verified against the files on disk at HEAD. This is dropped-money + over-recording (recorded €400 destroying the €200 audit record), not guarded anywhere. The reviewer's trace matches the current code; only minor line-number labels differ (their 600-608 / 1052 / 1235-1243 are accurate). Finding CONFIRMED.

broken.title: _computeOwedLines omits the contract discount, so express-pay over-records cash by the discount and seeds a phantom overpayment credit
broken.line: 103-189 (_computeOwedLines, no discount) vs services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/7_total.ts:64-67 (grandTotal subtracts discount)
broken.brokenShape: _computeOwedLines pushes previousBalance + rent(preTax) + propertyCharge + buildingCharge + repair + vat(net) + extracharge and NEVER subtracts rent.discounts/total.discount. The contract discount is a separate rent.discounts[] entry with origin:'contract' (3_discounts.ts:13-22) that does NOT reduce preTaxAmounts; grandTotal subtracts it (7_total.ts:65). So sum(_computeOwedLines) = grandTotal + discountPrincipal. The net VAT is correct (4_vats.ts:75-83 adds the negative discount-VAT and _computeOwedLines reads total.vat), but the discount PRINCIPAL is missing. bulkExpressPayment uses this inflated sum as the recorded payment amount with no user override (rentmanager.ts:566-567,602) and no negative-clamp.
broken.trigger: Tenant with contract.discount = 100, rent 1000, no VAT → grandTotal 900. Landlord uses Express εξόφληση (or auto-spread PATCH) to settle the month. Server records a €1000 payment (the undiscounted owed sum), €100 over the €900 bill. newBalance = payment - grandTotal = +100 carries a phantom −€100 balance into next month (5_balance.ts:17-20); the receipt overstates cash by €100. The UI showed €900 (totalWithoutBalanceAmount is discounted, frontdata.ts:129) so the divergence is invisible to the landlord.

verdict.codeEvidence: rentmanager.ts:103-189 _computeOwedLines pushes: previousBalance (106-113), preTaxAmounts (117-129), charges (132-142), buildingCharges/repair (145-160), VAT from rent.total.vat (169-176), debts/extracharge (179-186). It NEVER reads rent.discounts[] or rent.total.discount. 1_base.ts:882-888 builds preTaxAmounts from property.rent only (no discount applied). 3_discounts.ts:10-23 pushes the contract discount ONLY into rent.discounts[] (origin 'contract'). 7_total.ts:64-67 grandTotal = preTaxAmount+charges+buildingCharges+debts-discount+vat+balance (discount subtracted here ONLY). 4_vats.ts:75-83 adds a NEGATIVE discount-VAT line into rent.total.vat, so _computeOwedLines' VAT term IS net-correct, but the discount PRINCIPAL is absent. bulkExpressPayment rentmanager.ts:548-567: allLines=_computeOwedLines(targetRent); monthlyOwed=sum(monthLines); amount=monthlyOwed with NO clamp/override; written via paymentData.payments[0].amount (596-608). _updateByTerm rentmanager.ts:808-814 validates amount only {min:0,max:1e7} — no grandTotal clamp; contract.discount=occupant.discount (790) so payTerm→computeRent regenerates the discount and grandTotal stays discounted. 5_balance.ts:17-20 next-term balance = prevGrandTotal - prevPayment.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is in bulkExpressPayment (rentmanager.ts:548-567): the server-derived recorded payment amount = sum of _computeOwedLines month-lines, which omits the contract discount PRINCIPAL (the discount-VAT is correctly netted via rent.total.vat, but the principal is not). For contract.discount=100, rent 1000, no VAT: preTaxAmounts=[1000], discounts=[{origin:'contract',100}], grandTotal=900, but monthlyOwed=1000. Express εξόφληση records a €1000 payment (no user override, no clamp in _updateByTerm which validates only min0/max10M). After payTerm→computeRent, total.payment=1000 > grandTotal=900, so 5_balance carries balance=900-1000=-100 into next month (phantom overpayment credit) and the receipt overstates cash by the discount. The regular PATCH path's _computeOwedLines use (rentmanager.ts:1048-1080) is NOT affected: there it only spreads a user-typed amount into allocation buckets; the recorded total equals what the user typed. Minimal fix: subtract sum(rent.discounts[].amount) (the discount principal) from monthlyOwed in bulkExpressPayment, or have _computeOwedLines emit a negative 'discount' line, or clamp the express amount to grandTotal.
verdict.reasoning: I independently opened and traced every file in the chain. _computeOwedLines demonstrably never references discounts. preTaxAmounts is built pre-discount (1_base:882). The discount is a separate discounts[] entry (3_discounts) subtracted only into grandTotal (7_total:65), with its VAT correctly netted into total.vat (4_vats:80) which _computeOwedLines reads — so only the discount PRINCIPAL is missing, exactly as the finding states. bulkExpressPayment uniquely DERIVES the recorded amount from this inflated sum (line 567) with no user override and no clamp; _updateByTerm validation (min0/max1e7) does not clamp to grandTotal; payTerm/computeRent record it verbatim and regenerate the discount, so total.payment (1000) exceeds grandTotal (900) and 5_balance seeds a -100 phantom credit. The auto-spread PATCH path is not affected because there _computeOwedLines only allocates a user-supplied amount. The trigger requires a tenant with a non-zero contract.discount settled via Express εξόφληση (or the auto-spread that derives amount). This is a concrete, unguarded wrong-money / phantom-credit path in current HEAD code. Verdict: BROKEN.

broken.title: Recording a payment against a CLOSED past month re-prices that month's building/property charges at CURRENT rates, breaking the past-term freeze guarantee
broken.line: 261-291 (payTerm target exempt from freeze) + services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts:774-795 (live buildings, no historical pin)
broken.brokenShape: Contract.payTerm's freeze-skip is `if (rent.term !== targetTerm && _isFrozen(rent, currentTerm))` (contract.ts:270) — the term being paid is EXEMPT from the freeze even when it is a closed past month. _updateByTerm builds contract.buildings from the live Building docs (rentmanager.ts:774-779) and passes them in. When payTerm recomputes the target via BL.computeRent → taskBase (1_base.ts:968-989), recurring building-expense shares are recomputed live from the CURRENT expense.amount, not the amount billed when that month was originally closed. The Tier I-1 freeze (contract.ts:104-114, test contract-freeze-past-unpaid.test.js) only protects past months from UNRELATED edits via Contract.update — it does NOT cover the Contract.payTerm path, which re-derives the paid term from scratch.
broken.trigger: March is a closed/billed month with a €50 cleaning building-charge. In May the landlord raises the cleaning expense to €80. Tenant pays March's rent late; landlord opens March's rents page (date within March +7d passes the rentmanager.ts:1006-1030 guard) and records the payment. payTerm recomputes March's buildingCharges at the NEW €80 rate, March.grandTotal jumps €30, and the recorded payment/receipt no longer matches what March was actually billed.

verdict.codeEvidence: contract.ts:270 `if (rent.term !== targetTerm && _isFrozen(rent, currentTerm))` — the freeze-skip explicitly EXEMPTS the term being paid; a closed past target term (`_isFrozen` true via contract.ts:318 `rent.term < currentTerm → return true`) is NOT skipped because the `rent.term !== targetTerm` half is false. contract.ts:283 then runs `contract.rents[index] = BL.computeRent(contract, current..., previousRent, settlements)`. index.ts:19-39 shows computeRent starts from a FRESH rent with empty buildingCharges (no preservation of the previously-billed amount); index.ts:51-53 runs taskBase. 1_base.ts:917 `rent.buildingCharges = []`, then 1_base.ts:968-989 re-prices recurring expenses LIVE via computeBuildingChargeForProperty(building, propertyId, expense, rent.term) using the CURRENT `expense.amount` (1_base.ts:473/475/491 etc.), skipping only expenses overridden by a persisted monthlyCharge (1_base.ts:944-949,971). rentmanager.ts:774-779 fetches buildings live from Collections.Building with the current expense.amount and rentmanager.ts:786-795 sets contract.rents = occupant.rents; rentmanager.ts:1220 calls Contract.payTerm directly then saves at 1235 with no Contract.update re-freeze. The freeze that pins past months (contract.ts:104-114 in Contract.update) only runs on the expense-EDIT path (buildingmanager.ts:518 _recomputeTenantsForBuilding uses Contract.update), and the freeze test contract-freeze-past-unpaid.test.js:115 only describes 'Contract.update — past-unpaid freeze', never payTerm.
verdict.reasoning: I independently traced the full path and it lands exactly where the reviewer says. payTerm's freeze-skip (contract.ts:270) exempts the target term, so a CLOSED PAST month being paid late is rebuilt via BL.computeRent from a fresh empty rent object — its buildingCharges are recomputed live from the current expense.amount in taskBase (1_base.ts:968-989), NOT pinned to what was billed when the month was originally closed. The protective freeze (Contract.update, contract.ts:104-114) is only applied on the expense-edit recompute path (buildingmanager.ts:518), never on the payment path; rentmanager.ts:1220 calls payTerm and immediately persists. The only thing that would protect a past term here is a persisted per-unit monthlyCharge for that term (1_base.ts:944-949 / 971), which a plain recurring expense (the reviewer's €50→€80 cleaning charge) does not create. The payment-date guard (rentmanager.ts:1006-1030) rejects only dates before the term-month-first-day and after term-last-day+7d, so a March payment dated within March passes — the trigger is reachable from the real UI flow. Net effect: recording a late payment against a closed past month silently re-prices that month's building charges at current rates, so grandTotal/receipt no longer match what the tenant was actually billed (wrong-money). Minimal leak: contract.ts:270 — the `rent.term !== targetTerm` exemption must also respect `_isFrozen` for past terms (e.g. preserve the target's preTaxAmounts/charges/buildingCharges/vats when it is a past frozen term, replaying only the new payment), OR snapshot/restore the target's billed lines around the payTerm recompute.
