(7) rentmanager.ts:566-567/581 `amount = _round(amount + monthlyOwed)`; rentmanager.ts:596-607 records `payments:[{amount, date, type:'transfer', allocation}]` with no clamp to grandTotal. (8) 6_payments.ts:50-54 pushes that amount verbatim into rent.payments; 7_total.ts:52-57 sums it into rent.total.payment. (9) services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/5_balance.ts:17-19 `balance = prev.total.grandTotal - prev.total.payment` → grandTotal - (grandTotal+discount) = -discount. (10) services/api/src/managers/frontdata.ts:128-129 `totalAmount: rent.total.grandTotal` and `totalWithoutBalanceAmount: rent.total.grandTotal - rent.total.balance` — the dialog (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:46-48 reads r.totalWithoutBalanceAmount) shows the DISCOUNT-NET figure.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is in rentmanager.ts `_computeOwedLines` (103-189): it omits any negative line for `rent.discounts`, so the per-line owed sum used by bulkExpressPayment (monthlyOwed, rentmanager.ts:555-557) overstates grandTotal by exactly the contract/settlement discount. That gross amount is recorded as a real `transfer` payment (rentmanager.ts:596-607, no override/clamp), while the dialog displays the discount-net figure (frontdata.ts:129). Net effects: (a) recorded cash overstated by the discount for the current month; (b) next-month carry-in balance goes to -discount (phantom tenant credit) via 5_balance.ts:18-19; (c) receipt PDF / dashboard sums of payments overstate collected cash. Minimal fix: have _computeOwedLines emit (or net out) the discount — e.g. subtract sum(rent.discounts[].amount) from the rent/preTax lines or add a negative 'discount' OwedLine — so monthlyOwed equals grandTotal-balance. Reviewer's only inaccuracy is harmless line-number drift; the chain is exact. Note: any other caller that records monthlyOwed as cash (single-tenant express settle, if any) shares the defect since the bug is in the shared helper.
verdict.reasoning: Independently opened and read all cited files at HEAD f6f75966. The discount is a structurally separate ledger line (rent.discounts[]) that ONLY 7_total.ts subtracts when forming grandTotal; preTaxAmounts carries the gross rent (1_base.ts:882). _computeOwedLines deliberately enumerates every owed category EXCEPT discounts, so its sum = grandTotal + discount. bulkExpressPayment server-resolves the recorded amount from that sum (the comment at 458 confirms the caller cannot override it), pushes it as a real payment with no clamp, and the balance task then produces a negative carry-in. The displayed dialog figure (frontdata totalWithoutBalanceAmount) is discount-net, so the landlord sees the smaller number while the larger one is billed/recorded. I searched for any guard (clamp to grandTotal, discount netting in the owed path) and found none. This is a confirmed, unguarded wrong-money defect triggered by any tenant with occupant.discount > 0 (or an active settlement discount) when express-pay 'Monthly' is recorded.

broken.title: PaymentTabs dialog shows two contradictory totals for the SAME rent simultaneously: 'Rent due' (discounted grandTotal) vs allocation 'Total owed' (undiscounted sum)
broken.line: AllocationBlock owedTotal 121 & 316 (from computeOwedLines, paymentAllocation.js:43-138, no discount); RentSelector RentDetails.js:16-18,32-34 uses totalAmount=grandTotal (discounted)
broken.brokenShape: In one PaymentTabs payment dialog the RentSelector 'Rent due'/'Remaining' is built from getRentAmounts(rent).totalAmount = rent.totalAmount = grandTotal (RentDetails.js:38, RentSelector.js:16-18,32), which is discount-inclusive. The AllocationBlock 'Total owed' (AllocationBlock.js:121,316) is sum of computeOwedLines (paymentAllocation.js:43-138) which — like the server — omits rent.discounts entirely. The two figures on the same screen differ by exactly the contract discount.
broken.trigger: Open the payment dialog for a tenant with occupant.discount=100 on a 1000 rent. Header/'Rent due' shows 900; the allocation Preview 'Total' (owed-before) shows 1000. The landlord cannot reconcile which is correct, and auto-spreading the typed amount under-fills lines by 100.

verdict.codeEvidence: CONFIRMED in current code. (1) RentSelector.js:16 `const _gt = Number(rentAmounts?.totalAmount) || 0;` and :32 `amount={rentAmounts.totalAmount}` label `t('Rent due')` — "Rent due"/"Remaining" come from rentAmounts.totalAmount. (2) rents/RentDetails.js:38 `totalAmount: rent.totalAmount` (the reviewer cited components/payment/RentDetails.js which does NOT exist — the file is components/rents/RentDetails.js, imported at RentSelector.js:1 `import { getRentAmounts, RentAmount } from '../rents/RentDetails';`; content matches). (3) frontdata.ts:128 `totalAmount: rent.total.grandTotal`. (4) 7_total.ts:64-67 `const grandTotal = ...(preTaxAmount + charges + buildingChargesTotal + debts - discount + vat + balance)...` — grandTotal SUBTRACTS discount. (5) AllocationBlock.js:121-124 `const owedTotal = payableLines.reduce((s,l)=>s+(Number(l?.amount)||0),0);` and :316 `{fmt(owedTotal)}` (the Preview "Total" Before column). payableLines come from owedLines = computeOwedLines(rent) (PaymentTabs.js:423-424). (6) paymentAllocation.js computeOwedLines (lines 43-139) sums balance(53) + preTaxAmounts(65-74) + charges(79-88) + buildingCharges(95-107) + vat(115-123) + extracharge(126-136) — NO discount line. Server mirror rentmanager.ts _computeOwedLines:103-189 also omits discount. (7) The discount is an independent rent.discounts[] entry, NOT a reduction of preTaxAmounts: 3_discounts.ts:10-23 pushes {origin:'contract', amount} to rent.discounts; 1_base.ts:885-888 pushes preTaxAmounts at full `property.rent`. rentmanager.ts:790 `discount: occupant.discount || 0` feeds contract.discount.
verdict.reasoning: For any tenant with a contract discount (occupant.discount > 0), the PaymentTabs payment dialog shows two contradictory totals for the SAME rent at the same time. With occupant.discount=100 on a 1000 rent: the RentSelector header "Rent due" / "Remaining" = totalAmount = grandTotal = 900 (discount subtracted in 7_total.ts:65), while the AllocationBlock Preview "Total" Before column (AllocationBlock.js:316 -> owedTotal -> computeOwedLines) = 1000, because computeOwedLines (and the server's _computeOwedLines it mirrors) build owed lines from preTaxAmounts (full 1000) and never emit a discount line. The discount lives in rent.discounts[] and is only honored by grandTotal, not by the per-line owed model. Concrete wrong-value-on-a-surface outcome: a landlord recording the discounted 900 (the figure the header tells them is due) sees auto-spread fill 900 of 1000 owed-lines, leaving a phantom 100 "remaining" line in the Preview even though the rent is actually fully settled (the discount covers the gap). The two on-screen figures can never reconcile for a discounted tenant, and the allocation Preview never reaches zero-owed. This is not merely cosmetic: it makes the per-line allocation model structurally inconsistent with the rent's actual liability whenever a discount is present, mis-guiding both auto and custom allocation. Note this is a display/allocation-model defect, not a server money-loss: auto-spread only distributes what is typed, so it does not by itself over-charge in this dialog (the express-settlement path at rentmanager.ts:548-557 separately computes monthlyOwed from undiscounted lines, which is a related but distinct over-charge concern outside this finding's scope). Severity is medium-high: a real, reproducible wrong/contradictory value on a money surface for every discounted lease, exactly as the finding describes. The only inaccuracy in the report is the file path for RentDetails (it is under components/rents/, not components/payment/) — a citation slip, not a misread; the asserted behavior holds.

broken.title: Single-payment auto-spread allocation under-attributes by the discount, leaving owed lines marked unpaid after a full-balance payment
broken.line: _runningOwedLines 1048-1050 (from _computeOwedLines), auto-spread consume loop 1080-1104
broken.brokenShape: In _updateByTerm, _runningOwedLines = _computeOwedLines(_targetRent) (rentmanager.ts:1048-1050) — discount-free, so the line owed total exceeds the true grandTotal by the discount. When a payment with no caller allocation auto-spreads (rentmanager.ts:1080 _computeAutoSpreadLines), a payment equal to the true grandTotal (e.g. 900) cannot fully cover the inflated owed lines (1000), so the last line(s) remain partially unallocated. The persisted payments[].allocation then drives the AllocationBlock/saved-tile (PaymentTabs.js:813, 990) and dashboard category attribution to show a residual owed on a line the tenant has actually fully settled.
broken.trigger: Tenant occupant.discount=100, rent 1000 → grandTotal 900. PATCH /rents/payment/:id/:term with a single 900 payment and no explicit allocation. Auto-spread fills preTax line to 900 of its 1000 owed; the saved-tile/preview shows 100 still owed against rent even though grandTotal is fully paid (newBalance 0).

verdict.codeEvidence: services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/7_total.ts:64-67 computes grandTotal = preTaxAmount + charges + buildingChargesTotal + debts - discount + vat + balance — the discount is subtracted ONLY at the grandTotal level. services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/3_discounts.ts:13-22 pushes the discount solely into rent.discounts[] (a separate line); it never reduces rent.preTaxAmounts[].amount. services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts:103-189 _computeOwedLines builds lines from rent.preTaxAmounts (line 120-129), rent.charges, rent.buildingCharges, total.vat, debts, and total.balance — it never reads rent.discounts / total.discount and emits no discount line, so sum(owedLines) = grandTotal + discount. The client mirror webapps/landlord/src/utils/paymentAllocation.js:43-139 computeOwedLines does the same (preTax at line 64-74; never reads rent.discount, which the docstring at lines 40-41 confirms arrives as a flattened total). At rentmanager.ts:1048-1050 _runningOwedLines = _computeOwedLines(_targetRent) and at :1080 a no-allocation payment calls _computeAutoSpreadLines(amt, _runningOwedLines), which (lines 199-218) fills each line up to its owed amount until the payment is exhausted — a 900 payment against a 1000 preTax line allocates only 900, leaving 100 unallocated. On the surfaces: AllocationBlock.js:104-105/318 displays remainingTotal from applyAllocation(payableLines, allocation) (payableLines = owedLines), and PaymentTabs.js:423-433 derives owedLines = computeOwedLines(rent) minus saved allocations, so after a full-balance save the rent line still advertises a residual = discount on reopen/next-payment preview.
verdict.reasoning: The finding's core premise holds against current code: the discount is netted into grandTotal (7_total.ts:65) but is NEVER subtracted from the per-line preTaxAmounts (3_discounts.ts only pushes a discounts[] line), and neither _computeOwedLines (server, rentmanager.ts:103-189) nor computeOwedLines (client, paymentAllocation.js:43-139) emits a discount-reducing line. Therefore sum(owedLines) = grandTotal + discount. Trigger is realistic: contract.discount=100, rent 1000 → grandTotal 900 (frontdata.toRentData sends preTaxAmounts un-discounted plus a separate discount field, line 127/134). A single 900 payment with no caller allocation auto-spreads 900 into the 1000 preTax line; the AllocationBlock preview (line 318) shows remainingTotal=100 as still-owed, and the persisted payments[].allocation under-attributes by 100, which carries into the next dialog open via PaymentTabs owedLines (line 423-432). This is unguarded — I found no code netting the discount into owed lines nor capping the residual at grandTotal. SCOPE CORRECTION vs the reviewer: the impact is strictly display/attribution. The actual balance and paid-status are CORRECT — 7_total.ts:52-57/69 sums rent.total.payment from full payment.amount (not allocation), and frontdata newBalance = payment - grandTotal = 0, so the month correctly reads paid. No money is dropped, double-counted, or mis-totalled in the ledger. So this is BROKEN as a phantom-residual display/attribution defect (medium, matching the reviewer's 'severity medium / impact none'), not a money-loss bug. The minimal leak: owed-line construction omits the discount in both _computeOwedLines (rentmanager.ts:103-189) and computeOwedLines (paymentAllocation.js:43-139), so any discount-bearing tenant shows a phantom owed equal to the discount after a full-balance auto-spread payment.

broken.title: Per-payment promo (settlement discount) is double-credited in carry-forward settlement check → underpaid month wrongly flips to 'paid'
broken.brokenShape: In _isSettledByCarryForward, monthlyBill = grandTotal - carryIn is ALREADY net of the discount (7_total.ts line 65 subtracts `discount` when computing grandTotal). But cashIn = paymentsSum + settlementDiscounts (line 42) adds the settlement discount AGAIN. So the running deficit is reduced by the discount amount twice. running += monthlyBill - cashIn then dips to <=0.01 (line 55 trigger) even when the tenant paid LESS than the discounted bill. Concretely (no VAT for clarity): preTax rent 1000, per-payment promo 100, payment 800. grandTotal = 1000 - 100 = 900; monthlyBill = 900; paymentsSum = 800; settlementDiscounts = 100; cashIn = 900; running = 900 - 900 = 0 <= 0.01 and totalCashIn = 900 > 0.005 → returns true. Tenant actually owes 100 (paid 800 of a 900 discounted bill). In toRentData: directPaid = 800 > 0, newBalance = 800 - 900 = -100 (< -0.005) so the primary 'paid' branch (line 250) is skipped, falling to line 252-257 which calls _isSettledByCarryForward → true → status = 'paid'. With a contract VAT rate the discount is stored net-of-VAT so the over-credit is the net portion, but the over-credit is still nonzero and the underpaid month is still mis-promoted in proportion to the promo.
broken.trigger: Record a payment with a per-payment promo/discount where the cash paid is short of the post-discount grandTotal by up to (≈) the promo amount: e.g. tenant rent 1000, enter one payment of 800 with promo 100 in the katavoli dialog. The rents list (rentsOfOccupant passes allRents) and the immediate PATCH /rents/payment response (savedOccupant.rents passed as allRents) both render status 'paid' and the row drops out of the 'In arrears' filter even though 100 is still owed.

verdict.codeEvidence: frontdata.ts:34 `const monthlyBill = grandTotal - carryIn;` — grandTotal already net of the settlement discount: 7_total.ts:64-67 computes grandTotal as `preTaxAmount + charges + ... - discount + vat + balance` (line 65 subtracts the full `discount` reduce over rent.discounts which INCLUDES the settlement-origin discount). frontdata.ts:39-42 then re-adds the same discount as cash: `settlementDiscounts = rent.discounts.filter(d.origin==='settlement').sum(amount)` and `const cashIn = paymentsSum + settlementDiscounts;` frontdata.ts:43 `running += monthlyBill - cashIn;` so the discount is subtracted from running once via monthlyBill and again via cashIn → double credit. frontdata.ts:55 trigger `if (reachedTarget && running <= 0.01 && totalCashIn > 0.005) return true;`. Per-payment promo is stored with origin 'settlement': rentmanager.ts:1157-1161 `settlements.discounts.push({ origin: 'settlement', ... amount: promo * _vatFactor })`; 3_discounts.ts:30-34 carries `origin: discount.origin || 'settlement'` into rent.discounts[]. Status tree frontdata.ts:248-257: directPaid=rent.total.payment, newBalance (line 123) = payment - grandTotal; for paid 800 of 900 net bill newBalance=-100 so line 250 (`>= -0.005`) is skipped, line 252-257 calls _isSettledByCarryForward → true → status='paid'. Callers pass full ledger as allRents: rentmanager.ts:1256-1264 (PATCH payment response) and rentmanager.ts:1288 (rentsOfOccupant).
verdict.reasoning: Traced the full path end to end. (1) Per-payment promo IS persisted as a discount with origin 'settlement' (rentmanager.ts:1157-1161 → 3_discounts.ts:30-34), exactly what _isSettledByCarryForward filters for at frontdata.ts:40. (2) That discount IS already subtracted from grandTotal in 7_total.ts:65 (and the compensating negative VAT line in 4_vats.ts:75-83 makes grandTotal drop by the full gross promo), so monthlyBill at frontdata.ts:34 is net of it. (3) frontdata.ts:42 adds the stored (net-of-VAT) discount BACK into cashIn → the running deficit is reduced by the discount twice. (4) For no-VAT rent 1000, promo 100, payment 800: grandTotal=900, monthlyBill=900, paymentsSum=800, settlementDiscounts=100, cashIn=900, running=900-900=0 ≤ 0.01, totalCashIn=900>0.005 → returns true. The status tree (frontdata.ts:248-257) skips the primary 'paid' branch because newBalance=-100<-0.005, then hits the carry-forward branch and sets status='paid' for a month where the tenant still owes 100. Both render surfaces (PATCH /rents/payment response and rentsOfOccupant list) pass the full ledger as allRents, so the mislabel ships to the UI and the row drops out of the 'In arrears' filter. With a contract VAT rate the over-credit is the net portion (gross/(1+rate)) since the stored amount is net, but it is still nonzero, so the month is still mis-promoted in proportion to the promo. This is accept-invalid: a genuinely underpaid month is reported 'paid'. The minimal leak is the inclusion of settlementDiscounts in cashIn at frontdata.ts:42 — the discount is a bill reduction (already in monthlyBill), not received cash.

broken.title: ExpressPaymentDialog 'pay outstanding' is rejected for any past-month rents page (backdate guard fires on today's date)
broken.brokenShape: bulkExpressPayment dates every express payment to today (todayDDMMYYYY = moment.utc().format('DD/MM/YYYY'), line 504; payment.date = todayDDMMYYYY, line 603) and uses the viewed-month term verbatim (const term = String(it.term), line 528). Each item then routes through _updateByTerm whose per-payment guard rejects a payment dated after termLastDay = termFirstDay.endOf('month') + 7 days with 422 (lines 1016-1030). For any rents page older than ~7 days into the current month, today's date is > termLastDay, so EVERY express item 422s. ExpressPaymentDialog has no client-side date/term guard; it surfaces the failures only as a generic 'Recorded {recorded} of {total} payments ({failed} failed)' warning toast (ExpressPaymentDialog.js lines 166-172) with no actionable reason. The carry/previousBalance arrears settlement is exactly the case where the landlord opens a past month — express is unusable for it, and unlike the single PaymentTabs dialog (which lets the user pick a date inside the past term) there is no workaround in express because the date is hardcoded to today.
broken.trigger: Navigate to a prior month's rents page (e.g. /<org>/rents/2026.04 while it is June), open Express settlement, tick any tenant's Monthly or Prior balance, click Record. Server rejects every item (date today > 07/05) and the user sees only 'Recorded 0 of N payments (N failed)'.

verdict.codeEvidence: rentmanager.ts:504 `const todayDDMMYYYY = moment.utc().format('DD/MM/YYYY')`; :528 `const term = String(it.term)`; :603 `date: todayDDMMYYYY` — every express item is dated today against the viewed-month term verbatim. The per-payment guard in _updateByTerm: :999-1005 builds `termFirstDay` from the 10-char YYYYMMDDHH term; :1016-1020 `const termLastDay = termFirstDay.clone().endOf('month').add(7,'days')`; :1021-1030 `if (parsed.isValid() && termLastDay.isValid() && parsed.isAfter(termLastDay)) throw new ServiceError('payments[..].date is after this rent month ...', 422)`. Rejection is captured at :631-637 (_liveErrorByKey) and emitted as `failed: true` at :656. Client ExpressPaymentDialog.js:129 sends `term: String(row.term)` (the viewed-month term), has NO date control (server hardcodes today), and at :157,166-172 shows only `toast.warning('Recorded {{recorded}} of {{total}} payments ({{failed}} failed)')`. RentTable.js:645 passes the page's `rents` to the dialog; :686-703 the express button renders unconditionally on any month. Rent terms are 10-char YYYYMMDDHH (1_base.ts:840 `rent.term = Number(currentMoment.format('YYYYMMDDHH'))`; tests use 2026040100), so `termStr.length === 10` is true and the guard runs.
verdict.reasoning: Traced the full path on disk. On a genuinely past-month rents page, express dates every payment to today (line 603) but uses that month's term (line 528). _updateByTerm computes termLastDay = last-day-of-month + 7d and 422s any payment dated after it (lines 1021-1030). For a month whose endOf('month')+7d is before today (e.g. viewing April 2026 in mid-June), today is always after termLastDay, so EVERY item 422s, gets marked failed:true (line 656), and the client surfaces only a generic 'Recorded 0 of N (N failed)' warning with no date control to work around it (ExpressPaymentDialog has no per-payment date picker, unlike PaymentTabs). This makes express settlement unusable for the exact arrears/prior-balance scenario it targets when the landlord opens a past month. This is a genuine reject-valid defect in current code. Correction to the reviewer's imprecise framing: it is NOT '~7 days into the current month' — the current-month page works because today is within [firstDay, lastDay+7d]; the failure is total only for months strictly in the past beyond the 7-day cushion. The leak and medium severity stand.
verdict.correctedDetail: Minimal leak: in bulkExpressPayment (services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts) the payment date is hardcoded to today (line 504/603) while the term is taken from the viewed (possibly past) month (line 528). When that term's month is older than today minus the 7-day cushion, _updateByTerm's upper-bound guard (lines 1021-1030, termLastDay = endOf('month')+7d) rejects every item with 422, and ExpressPaymentDialog.js (lines 129, 157, 166-172) has no date control and only shows a generic 'N failed' warning. Fix would be to date express payments to a date inside the target term (e.g., last day of the term month, or expose a date control) rather than always today, OR exempt express writes from the termLastDay upper-bound guard.

broken.title: Editing/deleting a saved payment on a now-PAST (frozen) term silently re-prices that closed month, un-paying it
broken.line: 261-292 (payTerm walk) + freeze guard 270 `rent.term !== targetTerm && _isFrozen(...)`; reachable via rentmanager.ts _updateByTerm:1220 and PaymentTabs.js saved-tile Edit/Delete (PaymentTabs.js:865 edit btn unconditional, 875 delete btn unconditional, 632 payRent)
broken.brokenShape: The Tier I-1 immutable-closed-month freeze is enforced only in Contract.update (the contract-edit path, contract.ts:115-166), NOT in the payment path. payTerm always recomputes the TARGET term via BL.computeRent because the freeze guard explicitly excludes `rent.term === targetTerm`. computeRent reads LIVE state — property.rent (1_base.ts:882) and building expenses (1_base.ts buildingCharges). So a PATCH /rents/payment/:id/:pastTerm that merely re-saves the existing saved payments (PUT-replace) re-prices the past month with whatever the building expense / property rent is TODAY. I proved this against the compiled dist: a past month billed & fully paid at 400/400 (balance 0), after the landlord later raises the building cleaning expense by 50 and then edits the saved payment (added only a reference, amount unchanged), the past term's grandTotal jumps 400 -> 450 with a 50 buildingCharge line that was never billed, and the previously-Settled month now shows a 50 unpaid balance. Same for deleting one of several saved tiles. The carry-in sweep then propagates the phantom 50 forward into the next month's balance.
broken.trigger: 1) Past month M billed & paid in full. 2) Later (month M+1 or beyond) the landlord edits a building expense share or the property's monthly rent. 3) Landlord navigates the rents page to month M (URL /rents/YYYY.MM), opens a tenant's payment dialog, clicks the pencil on a saved tile and changes anything (reference/type/note) OR deletes one of multiple saved tiles, then presses Record. The saved payment's date is inside [M-1, M-end+7d] so the backdate guard passes; the PUT-replace re-prices M against current state, turning a Settled month into partiallypaid/notpaid and inflating arrears.

verdict.codeEvidence: contract.ts:270 freeze guard `if (rent.term !== targetTerm && _isFrozen(rent, currentTerm))` — explicitly EXEMPTS the target term from the freeze. In the payTerm loop (contract.ts:261-292), previousRentIndex = index of (target-1); the first processed index (previousRentIndex+1) IS the target term, so line 270's `rent.term !== targetTerm` is FALSE → no skip → line 283 `contract.rents[index] = BL.computeRent(contract, current..., previousRent, settlements)` unconditionally recomputes the target against whatever `contract` carries. rentmanager.ts:774-779 fetches LIVE buildings, rentmanager.ts:786-795 builds `contract = {buildings: <live>, rents: occupant.rents}`, rentmanager.ts:1220 calls `Contract.payTerm(contract, term, settlements)`. 1_base.ts:968-989 computes recurring building charges via `isExpenseActiveForTerm(expense, rent.term)` (1_base.ts:795-827 — date-range only on startTerm/endTerm) reading the LIVE `expense.amount` (no per-term snapshot for recurring expenses; only unit.monthlyCharges at 1_base.ts:946-964 are term-pinned). buildingmanager.ts:3232 `expense.set(patchBody)` mutates expense.amount in place on edit; its recompute uses Contract.update (buildingmanager.ts:518) which DOES freeze-restore past terms (contract.ts:104-207) — but payTerm never calls update(), so the asymmetry stands. Frontend: PaymentTabs.js:596 `clonedValues.payments = [...savedPayments, ...drafts]` re-submits all saved tiles with their original in-month DD/MM/YYYY dates (edit handler 888-893 preserves date; delete just drops one tile), which pass the backdate guard (PaymentTabs.js:504-531 and server rentmanager.ts:1006-1031); the 3-month block (PaymentTabs.js:466) only fires for FUTURE terms, so past-term tile edits are unblocked.
verdict.reasoning: The finding is correct and reproduces in current code. Contract.update() (the contract-edit path) freezes past terms by restoring their billed charges from the original document (contract.ts:104-207, _isFrozen at 315-319 makes any past term always frozen). But Contract.payTerm() — the function the payment path uses — exempts the TARGET term from the freeze (line 270 `rent.term !== targetTerm`) and unconditionally recomputes it via BL.computeRent against the LIVE contract.buildings supplied by _updateByTerm (rentmanager.ts:774-795). Recurring building expenses are NOT term-snapshotted: isExpenseActiveForTerm only checks the startTerm/endTerm date range and 1_base.ts:982-987 bills the live `expense.amount`. updateExpense (buildingmanager.ts:3232) mutates expense.amount in place, and its own recompute (Contract.update) correctly leaves past tenant rents at the billed value — so the building's recurring expense permanently holds the new amount while the past rent still shows the old. A later edit/delete of a saved payment tile on that past (frozen) term re-submits the existing payments (PaymentTabs.js:596) with their original in-month dates (passing both client and server backdate guards), which the server feeds to payTerm; payTerm re-prices term M against the now-higher live expense, inflating grandTotal and flipping a Settled month to partiallypaid/notpaid with phantom arrears that the carry-in sweep (5_balance / contract.ts:188-204) propagates forward. No clamp or restoration protects the target term on the payment path. Minimal leak: contract.ts:270 + 283 (target-term exemption + live-state recompute) with no freeze-restore equivalent to Contract.update on the payTerm path.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak: services/api/src/managers/contract.ts payTerm() recomputes the TARGET term against live building/property state with no freeze. The guard at contract.ts:270 (`rent.term !== targetTerm && _isFrozen(...)`) skips the freeze for the term being paid, so contract.ts:283 calls BL.computeRent(contract,...) using the live contract.buildings injected at rentmanager.ts:774-795. Because recurring building expenses bill the live expense.amount (1_base.ts:968-989 + isExpenseActiveForTerm 1_base.ts:795-827, no per-term amount snapshot) and updateExpense mutates amount in place (buildingmanager.ts:3232), editing/deleting a saved payment tile on a now-past frozen term (PaymentTabs.js:596 PUT-replace with original in-month dates, past-term unblocked at PaymentTabs.js:466) re-prices that closed month: grandTotal rises by the expense delta, the Settled month flips to underpaid, and the phantom balance carries forward. Fix would mirror Contract.update's freeze-restore for the target term inside payTerm (restore the stored billed charges for a frozen target instead of recomputing against live state), or snapshot recurring expense amounts per term.

broken.title: Express settlement on a past-month rents page 422s EVERY row (dated today, rejected by backdate guard) and reports it as an opaque 'N failed' toast
broken.line: 504 todayDDMMYYYY = moment.utc(); 528 term = String(it.term); 603 date: todayDDMMYYYY; rejected at 1021-1030 (parsed.isAfter(termLastDay = termFirstDay.endOf('month')+7d)); client has no term/today guard (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:118-138) and surfaces failures generically (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:166-172)
broken.brokenShape: bulkExpressPayment dates every express payment to today and unconditionally targets the viewed-month term (it.term). _updateByTerm's round-3t guard rejects any payment dated after termFirstDay.endOf('month')+7d with 422. So if the viewed month is more than ~7 days behind the current calendar month, today > termLastDay for every selected row and the entire batch fails. ExpressPaymentDialog has no client-side date/term guard; it posts whatever rows are eligible and renders the per-item failures only as toast.warning('Recorded {recorded} of {total} payments ({failed} failed)') with no per-row reason — the user cannot tell WHY nothing recorded. The button is rendered for every month (RentTable.js:686-703) and the rents page is parameterized by [yearMonth] so past-month viewing is normal navigation.
broken.trigger: On 16/06, navigate the rents page to April (/rents/2026.04), open Express settlement, tick any tenants' Monthly/Prior balance and press Record. Server stamps each payment 16/06/2026; termLastDay for April = 07/05/2026; 16/06 > 07/05 -> 422 for every row. User sees 'Recorded 0 of N payments (N failed)' with no actionable cause; the legitimate arrears action is impossible via Express on any sufficiently-old month.

verdict.codeEvidence: rentmanager.ts:504 `const todayDDMMYYYY = moment.utc().format('DD/MM/YYYY')`; :528 `const term = String(it.term)` (viewed-month term, never validated against today); :603 `date: todayDDMMYYYY` inside paymentData.payments[0]; :627 each item dispatched to `_updateByTerm(...p.term, p.paymentData)` via Promise.allSettled. In _updateByTerm: :982 `const parsed = moment.utc(p.date, 'DD/MM/YYYY', true)`; :1001-1020 `termFirstDay = moment.utc(YYYY-MM-01)`, `termLastDay = termFirstDay.clone().endOf('month').add(7,'days')`; :1021-1030 `if (parsed.isValid() && termLastDay.isValid() && parsed.isAfter(termLastDay)) throw new ServiceError('payments[...].date is after this rent month — switch to that month's rents page', 422)`. Server DOES surface a per-item reason — rentmanager.ts:649-658 returns `{failed:true, error: errMsg}` per item — but the client throws it away: ExpressPaymentDialog.js:156-172 reads only `results.filter(r=>r.failed).length` and toasts the generic `'Recorded {{recorded}} of {{total}} payments ({{failed}} failed)'` (no `error`). Client has no date/term guard before posting: ExpressPaymentDialog.js:120-138 posts `term: String(row.term)` for every eligible row. Button rendered unconditionally for every month: RentTable.js:686-703 (`data-cy="expressPaymentBtn"` inside StatusLegend, fed `rents={rents}` at :645). Route wiring: routes.ts:243-244 `POST /express → rentManager.bulkExpressPayment`. Page parameterized by month: webapps/landlord/src/pages/[organization]/rents/[yearMonth]/index.js — past-month viewing is normal navigation.
verdict.reasoning: I independently traced the full path and it reaches the wrong outcome in current code. (1) bulkExpressPayment dates every express payment to today (moment.utc, line 504) and unconditionally targets the viewed-month term it.term (line 528, used at line 627). (2) _updateByTerm's round-3t guard rejects any payment dated after termLastDay = termFirstDay.endOf('month')+7d with 422 (lines 1016-1030). Concrete arithmetic: viewing April 2026 (term 2026040100) → termFirstDay=2026-04-01, endOf('month')=2026-04-30, +7d → termLastDay=2026-05-07. Any current-month settlement done after 07/05 stamps today (e.g. 16/06/2026), parsed.isAfter(2026-05-07) is TRUE → 422 for EVERY selected row. Both moment calls are UTC so there is no timezone escape that makes today land before the cutoff. (3) The client has no date/term guard before posting (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:118-138) and (4) renders failures only as the opaque toast.warning('Recorded {recorded} of {total} payments ({failed} failed)') (lines 166-172) — even though the server returns a precise per-item `error` string (lines 649-658), the client discards it. (5) The Express button is rendered for every month (RentTable.js:686-703, unconditional StatusLegend) and the page is parameterized by [yearMonth], so navigating to a past month and running Express is normal, supported UI. Net: the legitimate arrears-settlement action is impossible via Express on any month more than ~7 days behind the current calendar month, every row 422s, and the user sees 'Recorded 0 of N payments (N failed)' with no actionable cause. This is reject-valid + opaque-error, exactly as claimed. Minimal leak: the per-payment date should default to a term-anchored value (e.g. min(today, termLastDay)) when express-settling a past month, OR the client should pass through and display the server's per-item `error` so the user knows why; the round-3t guard itself is intentional, but Express's unconditional today-stamp collides with it.

broken.title: Payment-dialog allocation preview omits the VAT owed line for every VAT-rated tenant — owed Total understates the rent-table/receipt balance and VAT cannot be targeted in Specific/Custom mode
broken.line: 115-123 (client) vs services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts:169 and services/api/src/managers/frontdata.ts:118-139,197-209
broken.brokenShape: Client computeOwedLines builds the VAT owed line from `_round(Number(rent?.vat) || sumAmounts(rent?.vats))` (paymentAllocation.js:115). But the rent object the dialog receives is the frontdata.toRentData shape (frontdata.ts:118-139), which exposes NEITHER a top-level `vat` field NOR a `vats` array — it only exposes `vatAmount`/`vatRatio` (frontdata.ts:197-209). So on real data `rent.vat` is undefined and `rent.vats` is undefined, the VAT branch evaluates to 0, and NO `{category:'vat',lineKey:'vat'}` line is ever produced client-side. The server _computeOwedLines runs on the persisted rent and DOES produce the VAT line from `rent.total.vat`/`rent.vats` (rentmanager.ts:169). The two owed-line lists were declared mirrors (paymentAllocation.js:11 'Mirrors ... _computeOwedLines. Keep the two in sync') but diverge by exactly the VAT component. Consequence on AllocationBlock (AllocationBlock.js:104-124,273-320): the preview 'owed Total' and per-line Before/After sum to grandTotal MINUS VAT, i.e. less than the balance shown on the originating RentTable row and on the receipt PDF; and the Specific/Custom mode dropdown/rows (AllocationBlock.js:195-199,221-243) never list a VAT row, so the landlord cannot direct a payment to VAT (only auto-spread, which works server-side, covers it).
broken.trigger: Open the payment dialog (NewPaymentDialog → PaymentTabs) for any tenant whose lease carries vatRatio > 0 (commercial lease) with an unpaid term, type any amount > 0 to reveal AllocationBlock. The preview's owed Total renders grandTotal-minus-VAT while the rents table for the same tenant/term shows the full VAT-inclusive balance; choosing Specific/Custom shows no VAT line to allocate to.

verdict.codeEvidence: paymentAllocation.js:115 — `const vat = _round(Number(rent?.vat) || sumAmounts(rent?.vats));` then 116-123 push a `{category:'vat',lineKey:'vat'}` line only if `vat > 0.005`. frontdata.ts builds `rentToReturn` (line 118-139) listing preTaxAmounts/charges/buildingCharges/discounts/debts but NOT `vats` and NOT a scalar `vat`; the only VAT field added is `vatAmount` via Object.assign (line 197-209) and `vatRatio` (line 347). I grepped the whole file (line 115 `rent.vats=[]` mutates the INPUT rent, not rentToReturn; line 394 returns rentToReturn) — confirming `rentToReturn.vat`/`rentToReturn.vats` are undefined. 4_vats.ts:29-37 stores VAT ONLY in `rent.vats[]` (never folded into preTaxAmounts/charges). 7_total.ts:63-68 + rent.test.js:327-333 prove `grandTotal = preTax(net) + charges + ... + vat(separate) + debts` (test: 1000+100+50-200+190+300=1440, total.vat=190). Server _computeOwedLines (rentmanager.ts:117-129 + 169-176) therefore emits a separate vat line from `rent.total.vat`; client cannot. AllocationBlock.js:121-124 computes `owedTotal` from `payableLines` and renders it as the preview Total (314-320); 195-199 builds the Specific dropdown from `payableLines` only.
verdict.reasoning: The client owed-line list (computeOwedLines) and the server one (_computeOwedLines) were declared mirrors (paymentAllocation.js:11) but diverge by the VAT component. preTaxAmounts and charges are stored NET of VAT (4_vats.ts adds VAT only into rent.vats[]); grandTotal/balance shown on the RentTable is gross-of-VAT (7_total.ts: grandTotal includes total.vat as a separate addend, proven by the 1440-with-190-vat test). The frontdata shape the dialog actually receives (NewPaymentDialog passes selectedRent = defaultRent or fetchRents() result, both toRentData-shaped) exposes vatAmount/vatRatio but neither `vat` nor `vats`. So on any VAT-rated tenant (vatRatio>0, commercial lease) computeOwedLines' VAT branch reads undefined||sumAmounts(undefined)=0 and pushes NO vat line. Consequences are exactly as claimed: (1) AllocationBlock's preview owedTotal/remainingTotal sum the current term to grandTotal MINUS VAT — understating the balance the same RentTable row and receipt PDF show; (2) the Specific/Custom dropdown (built from payableLines) never lists a VAT row, so the landlord cannot target VAT; only auto-spread is unaffected because the SERVER re-derives owed lines including VAT at payTerm. Severity medium (wrong-render of an owed total + a targeting gap), not a money-drop, since the persisted server allocation recomputes VAT independently. The leak is purely the client owed-line list missing the VAT component.
verdict.correctedDetail: Minimal leak: webapps/landlord/src/utils/paymentAllocation.js:115 — `Number(rent?.vat) || sumAmounts(rent?.vats)` reads fields that do not exist on the frontdata-shaped rent the payment dialog receives. frontdata.ts:118-139,197-209 exposes the contract-VAT total only as scalar `vatAmount`, never as `vat` or `vats`. Fix is to read `rent.vatAmount` (or include `vats`/`vat` in toRentData's rentToReturn) so the client VAT owed line matches server _computeOwedLines (rentmanager.ts:169). Affects only VAT-rated (commercial) tenants with an unpaid current-term VAT; manifests as the AllocationBlock preview Total understating by the VAT amount (AllocationBlock.js:121-124,314-320) and the Specific/Custom dropdown omitting a VAT row (AllocationBlock.js:195-199,221-243).

broken.title: Dashboard rent bar over-reports notPaid for a tenant whose month is settled by overpayment carry-credit (negative balance not credited on the paid side)
broken.line: 426-451 (notPaid arithmetic), cross-checked vs frontdata.ts:20-59 _isSettledByCarryForward and 5_balance.ts:17-20
broken.brokenShape: Per-month notPaid for revenues[] is `tenantPaid < tenantMonthDue ? tenantMonthDue - tenantPaid : 0` where tenantMonthDue = max(0,grandTotal) - balance and balance = prev.grandTotal - prev.payment (5_balance.ts:17). When a tenant overpaid in a prior month, this month carries a NEGATIVE balance (a credit). tenantDue clamps grandTotal at 0 but tenantBalance (negative) is subtracted UNCLAMPED, so tenantMonthDue correctly reconstructs the gross this-month bill — but tenantPaid is only THIS month's cash, with the carry-in credit never added to the paid side of the comparison. Result: a fully-settled tenant shows phantom notPaid equal to the carry-credit. Worked example: prior overpayment leaves balance=-100; this month bill=500 so grandTotal=400; tenant pays the net 400. tenantDue=400, tenantBalance=-100, tenantMonthDue=400-(-100)=500, notPaid=(400<500)->100. The tenant owes nothing (500 bill, 100 credit + 400 cash) yet the YearFigures bar (YearFigures.js:104-108 renders data.notPaid as 'Owed') shows 100 outstanding. _isSettledByCarryForward (used in topUnpaid at dashboardmanager.ts:357 and by /rents status) is NOT applied to the revenues[] aggregator, so /rents marks the month 'paid' while the dashboard bar shows it unpaid — cross-surface money disagreement.
broken.trigger: Any tenant who overpays one month (creating a negative carry-forward balance) and in a later month pays exactly the credit-reduced grandTotal. Open the dashboard YearFigures (annual rent bar) for that year: the credit-covered month renders a notPaid segment equal to the prior overpayment, even though /rents shows the tenant fully paid.

verdict.codeEvidence: dashboardmanager.ts:426-451 (HEAD on disk): `const tenantDue = Math.max(0, rent.total?.grandTotal || 0); const tenantPaid = rent.total?.payment || 0;` ... line 448 `const tenantBalance = rent.total?.balance || 0;` line 449 `const tenantMonthDue = tenantDue - tenantBalance;` line 450-451 `acc[key].notPaid += tenantPaid < tenantMonthDue ? tenantMonthDue - tenantPaid : 0;`. Balance sign confirmed in 7_total.ts:64-67 (`grandTotal = ...+ (rent.total.balance||0)`) and tasks/5_balance.ts:17-20 (`balance = prev.grandTotal - prev.payment`) — a prior overpayment yields a NEGATIVE balance carried in. So with negative balance, `tenantMonthDue = grandTotal - balance` = this-month gross bill, but the carry-credit is never added to `tenantPaid`. Cross-surface: frontdata.ts:248-251 sets `/rents` status='paid' when `directPaid > 0 && rentToReturn.newBalance >= -0.005`. The finalize map at dashboardmanager.ts:494-511 only `_round`/`Math.abs` — no netting. Render: YearFigures.js:104-108 shows `data.notPaid > 0` as an "Owed" line, and handleClick (line 82-87) routes the bar to `/rents/{yearMonth}?statuses=notpaid`.
verdict.reasoning: The reviewer's worked example holds in current code. Full two-month ledger: M1 gross 500, balance 0 → grandTotal 500, tenant pays 600 (overpay 100). M2: balance = 500-600 = -100 (credit); M2 gross 500 → grandTotal = 500+(-100) = 400; tenant pays net 400. Tenant is fully settled (1000 billed, 1000 paid). Dashboard notPaid: M1 → tenantMonthDue = max(0,500)-0 = 500, paid 600 → notPaid 0 (the +100 surplus is dropped, never credited forward). M2 → tenantDue = max(0,400) = 400, tenantBalance = -100, tenantMonthDue = 400-(-100) = 500, tenantPaid = 400 → notPaid = 500-400 = 100 phantom. The finalize .map only rounds + Math.abs, so 100 reaches the response. Meanwhile frontdata.ts:250 marks M2 'paid' (directPaid 400>0, newBalance 0 >= -0.005). So the YearFigures bar shows an 'Owed: 100' segment for a month /rents reports as paid, and clicking it navigates to a notpaid list that does not contain the tenant — a real cross-surface money disagreement and an over-reported notPaid. The dashboard.test.js mirror (lines 165-166) uses the stale pre-Wave-14 formula `tenantPaid - tenantDue < 0` and never exercises the production `tenantMonthDue = tenantDue - tenantBalance` path, so the suite does not catch this. _isSettledByCarryForward is applied to topUnpaid (line 357) but NOT to the revenues[] notPaid aggregator. The leak is the negative-balance (credit) case at dashboardmanager.ts:449-451 inflating notPaid by the unreturned carry-credit. Minimal fix would be to clamp the credit out of tenantMonthDue (e.g. use the positive own-month bill but cap notPaid contribution by what is actually unsettled, or apply _isSettledByCarryForward / net the negative balance into the paid side) for negative-balance terms.

broken.title: Pie legend 'Receipts' (Εισπράξεις) total includes VAT/previousBalance/extracharge payments that the colored paid arcs deliberately drop; 'Receipts' can exceed 'Owed' on a VAT/carry-forward tenant
broken.line: 416-423 (totalDue / totalPaid) vs dashboardmanager.ts:78-152 _computePaidByBucket drops vat/previousBalance/extracharge at 90-93 and 150
broken.brokenShape: totalPaid = currentRevenues.paid = Σ rent.total.payment (7_total.ts:52-57: payment is the sum of ALL payment amounts incl. vat/previousBalance/extracharge allocations). The pie's colored paid sub-segments come from tenant.paidByBucket, which _computePaidByBucket builds while SILENTLY dropping the vat/previousBalance/extracharge allocation categories (dashboardmanager.ts:91-93 returns without _add for those cats; legacy branch comment at 150). So for a tenant paying VAT or paying down a previousBalance, Σ(colored paid arcs) < legend 'Receipts'. Separately totalDue (line 416-422) = baseRent + charges + ΣbuildingChargesByType, which EXCLUDES vat/debts/balance, while totalPaid INCLUDES them — so 'Receipts' can render LARGER than 'Owed' for a VAT or carry-forward-debt tenant who has overpaid nothing, which reads as 'you collected more than was owed' when nothing was overpaid.
broken.trigger: Open the current-month half-donut (MonthFigures) for a realm with at least one VAT-bearing lease or a tenant paying down a prior-balance debt this month. The bottom-right 'Εισπράξεις' number will exceed the sum of the dark paid arcs, and can exceed the bottom-left 'Οφειλές' number.

verdict.codeEvidence: MonthFigures.js:423 `const totalPaid = currentRevenues.paid || 0;` rendered as the legend "Receipts" (Εισπράξεις) at lines 536-541 `{t('Receipts')}: ... {formatNumber(totalPaid)}`. The "Owed" legend at 521-523 renders `totalDue` defined at 416-422 as `currentRevenues.baseRent + currentRevenues.charges + Σ(buildingChargesByType)` — VAT/debts/balance are NOT in that sum. Server side: dashboardmanager.ts:427 `const tenantPaid = rent.total?.payment || 0;` and :442 `acc[key].paid += tenantPaid;` — so `currentRevenues.paid` IS `rent.total.payment`. 7_total.ts:52-57 computes `payment = Σ(Number(payment.amount))` over ALL rent.payments — the gross cash sum, undifferentiated by category. 6_payments.ts:12,50-54 confirms `payment.amount` is the full gross figure (allocation[] is only metadata). The colored paid arcs use `_computePaidByBucket` which at dashboardmanager.ts:90-95 (lineKey fast-path: `if (cat === 'rent' || 'previousBalance' || 'vat' || 'extracharge')` only `_add('rent',...)` for rent, others `return` with no `_add`) and :150 (`// vat / previousBalance / extracharge: not on the pie.`) deliberately DROP vat/previousBalance/extracharge.
verdict.reasoning: The two legend numbers are computed from inconsistent bases, so they can disagree for any VAT-bearing or carry-forward lease. Concrete scenario: a lease with preTaxAmount(baseRent)=100, vat=24, charges=0, buildingCharges=0, balance=0 → grandTotal = 100+24 = 124 (7_total.ts:64-67). Tenant pays the full bill: payment=124 → rent.total.payment=124 → currentRevenues.paid=124 → legend "Receipts"=124. But totalDue (legend "Owed") = baseRent(100)+charges(0)+building(0) = 100 because VAT is excluded from the totalDue sum at MonthFigures.js:416-422. Result: "Receipts" (124) renders LARGER than "Owed" (100) for a tenant who paid exactly their bill and overpaid NOTHING — reads to the landlord as "you collected more than was owed." Separately, the dark paid arcs for that tenant sum to only 100 (the VAT €24 is dropped by _computePaidByBucket at line 91-95), so the colored arcs (100) are visibly less than the legend "Receipts" (124). Both sub-claims of the finding are reproducible against the code as written. The leak is the inconsistency between totalPaid (gross rent.total.payment, VAT/debts-inclusive) at MonthFigures.js:423 and totalDue (preTax+charges+building only, VAT/debts-excluded) at MonthFigures.js:416-422. Severity is medium: it is a display-only correctness defect (a confusing/misleading legend on the half-donut, not a money-movement or persistence bug), triggered whenever the realm has at least one VAT lease or a tenant paying down a prior balance in the current month.

broken.title: validateTerm accepts any 10-digit term (no day-01 enforcement); a repair chargeTerm or owner/monthly term with day != 01 created via API/legacy is silently dropped from the dashboard eksoda rollup, vanishing owed money
broken.line: 8 (TERM_RE = /^\d{10}$/), 94-110 (validateTerm) vs dashboardmanager.ts:639-654 termToKey/bucket guard and buildingmanager.ts:4406-4407 repair term match
broken.brokenShape: validateTerm only checks /^\d{10}$/ and a numeric range (2020010100..2099123100) — it does NOT normalize or require the DD segment to be 01. The dashboard eksoda rollup seeds termToKey ONLY with YYYYMM0100 terms (dashboardmanager.ts:639-644) and at line 652-654 does `const bucket = key ? byMonth[key] : null; if (!bucket) continue;` — any owedByTerm/repair.chargeTerm whose term has day != 01 finds no key and is skipped from totalYearExpenses, the per-month bars, and the Overview 'Συνολικά έξοδα' row (GeneralFigures.js:91). computeOwnerEksodaByMonth keys repair owed strictly on Number(repair.chargeTerm) (buildingmanager.ts:4406) and materialised owner rows on Number(row.term) (4246), so a stored non-01-day term produces owed that is computed but then dropped at the dashboard layer. addRepair/updateRepair validate chargeTerm only via validateTerm (buildingmanager.ts:4588, 4680), so a direct POST/PATCH with chargeTerm e.g. 2026031500 passes 422 validation, is stored, and its owner-portion silently disappears from the eksoda chart and year total.
broken.trigger: POST/PATCH /buildings/:id/repairs with chargeTerm='2026031500' (day=15, owner-borne cost), or any legacy ownerMonthlyExpenses row with term day != 01. The repair owner-portion is computed by computeOwnerEksodaByMonth but never lands in a month bucket, so the dashboard Έξοδα chart and Overview expenses total under-report by that amount. (Normal landlord UI always emits day-01 via RepairList.js:172/185, so exposure is API/legacy only.)

verdict.codeEvidence: validators.ts:8 `const TERM_RE = /^\d{10}$/`; validators.ts:99-108 validateTerm checks only TERM_RE.test(s) and range 2020010100..2099123100 — NO day-01/DD-segment enforcement. buildingmanager.ts:4587-4588 (addRepair) and 4679-4680 (updateRepair) gate chargeTerm solely via validateTerm; 4607 `(building).repairs.push(req.body)` stores it verbatim; building.ts:240 `chargeTerm: Number` has no setter/normalizer. _distributeRepairCharge buildingmanager.ts:3541 `const term = Number(repair.chargeTerm)` then 3570-3577 pushes ownerMonthlyExpenses row with `term` verbatim. computeOwnerEksodaByMonth keys materialised rows on buildingmanager.ts:4246 `const term = Number(row.term || 0)` and repairs on 4406 `const term = Number(repair.chargeTerm)`; year filter 4247/4407 `Math.floor(term / 1000000) !== year` passes for 2026031500 (=2026). dashboardmanager.ts:639-644 seeds termToKey ONLY via `moment.utc('${m}/${year}','MM/YYYY').format('YYYYMMDDHH')` which always yields ...0100; 652-654 `const key = termToKey[term]; const bucket = key ? byMonth[key] : null; if (!bucket) continue;` skips any non-day-01 term (parallel breakdown guard 666-669). UI always emits day-01: RepairList.js:172 `return \`${year}${month}0100\`;` and :185 `const term = \`${year}${month}0100\``.
verdict.reasoning: The full leak path is real in the current code and unguarded. A repair (or legacy ownerMonthlyExpenses row) with chargeTerm/term where DD != 01 — e.g. 2026031500 — passes validateTerm's 422 gate (only /^\d{10}$/ + numeric range, no day normalization), is stored verbatim (push at 4607, no schema normalizer at building.ts:240), and is materialised verbatim into ownerMonthlyExpenses (term: Number(repair.chargeTerm) at _distributeRepairCharge 3541/3570). computeOwnerEksodaByMonth then COMPUTES owed for it (its year filter Math.floor(term/1000000)===year passes for 2026), producing an owedByTerm entry keyed 2026031500. But _expensesRollup's termToKey map contains only the 12 day-01 month keys, so termToKey[2026031500] is undefined, bucket is null, and `if (!bucket) continue` (dashboardmanager.ts:654) drops it from totalYearExpenses, the per-month notPaid/paid bars, and the breakdown — silently under-reporting owed owner eksoda on the Overview total and Έξοδα chart. The normal landlord UI always emits day-01 (RepairList.js:172/185), so exposure is API/legacy only, matching the claimed medium severity. Minimal leak location: the day-01 assumption in dashboardmanager.ts:652-654 (and breakdown twin 666-669) combined with validateTerm never enforcing day-01 (validators.ts:94-110); the clean fix is either to normalize the DD segment to 01 in validateTerm (rejecting/normalizing non-01 terms) or to derive the bucket key from the term's YYYYMM rather than requiring an exact day-01 match.

broken.title: Move-in to a previously-vacant unit silently destroys recorded owner καταβολές on that unit's 'vacant' owner-expense row
broken.line: 3886-3997 (strip 3886-3895; re-push loop 3962-3997, occupied-skip 3966); reached via occupantmanager.ts:1136 → recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties 4008-4074
broken.brokenShape: _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges snapshots prior settlement into priorSettle (3874-3884), then UNCONDITIONALLY pulls every source:'vacant'/'owner-fixed'/'owner-resident' row for the term (3888-3895). The re-materialise loop skips occupied units (3966 `if (occupied.has(...)) continue;`). priorSettle entries are consumed ONLY via `.get(key)` inside that loop, so when a unit has flipped vacant→occupied for the term, no row is pushed and the carried payments (carryOwnerPayments 3978-3982) are never re-attached. There is no orphan re-emit after the loop (function ends at 3998). The read-time 'never drop a row carrying recorded payments' guard (4266-4270) cannot protect it because the row is already gone from the document at WRITE time, upstream of the dashboard read.
broken.trigger: Owner records a καταβολή against a vacant unit's chargeOwnerWhenVacant owner-expense share for term T (within the now-11..now+12 window). A tenant is then created/linked on that unit (POST /occupants), whose occupancy covers T. occupantmanager calls _recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties → _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges(building, T): the vacant row is stripped, the unit is now occupied so no row is rebuilt, and the recorded owner payment is permanently lost from the ledger, the owner Overview paid tile, and the dashboard Έξοδα 'paid' bucket.

verdict.codeEvidence: buildingmanager.ts:3875-3884 builds `priorSettle` from existing 'vacant'/'owner-fixed'/'owner-resident' rows for the term (captures payments). 3888-3895 strips ALL such rows UNCONDITIONALLY — `for (const e of stale) building.ownerMonthlyExpenses.pull(e._id);` — with NO payment-preservation check. 3942 `const occupied = await _occupiedPropertyIdsForTerm(...)`. Re-push loop 3962-3996: 3966 `if (occupied.has(String(unit.propertyId))) continue;` skips a now-occupied unit, so 3978-3982 `carried = carryOwnerPayments(priorSettle.get(`${expenseId}|${unit.propertyId}|${term}`))` is NEVER reached for that unit. Function ends at 3998 — no orphan re-emit of unconsumed priorSettle entries. Trigger path confirmed: occupantmanager.ts:1117 creates the tenant, 1126 `_syncOccupancyForProperties(...,'link')`, then 1136 `await _recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties(realm._id, linkedPropIds)`; `_occupiedPropertyIdsForTerm` (3824-3838) queries `Collections.Tenant` by occupancy date-range so the newly-created tenant IS in `occupied` for the covered term. payOwner records onto these rows: ownermanager.ts:752 `building.ownerMonthlyExpenses.id(a.ownerExpenseId)`, 776 `t.row.payments.push({...})` — a 'vacant' row is a settleable target. The read-time guard buildingmanager.ts:4265-4271 DOES preserve payment-carrying rows (`if (!hasPayments)` before any drop), and the repair-vacant write path is deliberately tenancy-change-immune (3709-3712), proving the asymmetry: the source:'vacant' WRITE-time strip alone lacks the "never drop a row carrying recorded payments" protection.
verdict.reasoning: The claim traces exactly to the code. _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges snapshots prior settlement (incl. payments) into priorSettle, then unconditionally strips every vacant/owner-fixed/owner-resident row for the term. The re-push loop skips units that are occupied for the term (3966), and priorSettle entries are consumed ONLY via .get(key) inside that loop. (2) A payment CAN exist on the row: owner-resident rows are persisted ownerMonthlyExpenses subdocs with a real ownerExpenseId handle (2768), payable via ownermanager.pay (752/776) and toggleable via setOwnerExpensePaid (2918).
