Minimal fix: normalize repair chargeTerm to YYYYMM0100 in addRepair/updateRepair the same way one-time expense startTerm is normalized at buildingmanager.ts:2999 (`Math.floor(t/10000)*10000+100`), or have validateTerm reject/normalize non-day-01 terms for this field. Severity: medium (requires a direct API call with a malformed-but-accepted term; normal UI flow always sends day=01).

broken.title: Un-terminate (clearing terminationDate) silently fails — $set drops undefined, stale terminationDate survives → tenant reads terminated while rent ledger is active; on chargeOwnerWhenVacant expenses the SAME share is double-billed to both the (still-active) tenant rent and the owner-vacant ledger
broken.line: 1529-1537 (with _stringToDate 30-40, _formatTenant 42-47); cascade: _attachTenantGroupsToBuildings 165/220, buildingmanager _occupiedFromOccupancyRows 3797, _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges 3942/3966/3990, computeOwnerEksodaByMonth STALE-VACANT guard 4281-4291
broken.brokenShape: update() builds occupantPatch by destructuring newOccupant (line 1529). When the landlord unchecks 'Terminated', LeaseContractForm._onSubmit (LeaseContractForm.js:379) submits terminationDate:'' ; _formatTenant calls _stringToDate('') which returns undefined (occupantmanager.ts:31,35-39), so occupantPatch.terminationDate===undefined. The write is `{ $set: occupantPatch, $inc:{__v:1} }` with NO $unset (line 1536) — Mongoose drops undefined keys from $set, so the OLD terminationDate stays in the DB. (extendLease at line 2161 is the ONLY path that $unset:{terminationDate:''}.) Contract.update is called with termination:undefined (line 1463) so the rent ledger IS correctly rebuilt for the full begin→end window — but every consumer that reads (terminationDate||endDate) still sees the stale past date: frontdata.toOccupantData reports terminated:true/status:'stopped' (frontdata.ts:445-451), dashboardmanager active-tenant count + topUnpaid exclude the tenant (dashboardmanager.ts:215-219, 320-322), occupantmanager.overview counts it inactive (1964-1972). MONEY double-count: _attachTenantGroupsToBuildings stamps the stale terminationDate onto the tenant's group (line 220); for terms after the stale date _occupiedFromOccupancyRows treats the unit as NOT occupied (uses terminationDate||endDate, line 3797). Then (a) 1_base equal-allocation still bills the tenant their unit's share on their rebuilt rent (the unit is occupied by entry/exit window, treated as a 'vacant party' carrier returning a non-zero share), AND (b) _recomputeVacantOwnerCharges materialises a source:'vacant' owner row for the same unit/expense/term (occupied set excludes it, line 3966) for any chargeOwnerWhenVacant expense, and computeOwnerEksodaByMonth's STALE-VACANT guard does NOT drop it because occ excludes the unit (line 4291). Same euro billed to tenant rent AND owner eksoda.
broken.trigger: Tenant on a unit in a building that has a chargeOwnerWhenVacant=true expense. Landlord terminates the lease (sets terminationDate in the past, e.g. last month), then realizes the mistake, opens the tenant lease form, unchecks 'Terminated', and saves. PATCH body carries terminationDate:'' and __v. Server keeps the old terminationDate. Result: dashboard active count and Top-5 unpaid drop the tenant; the building Έξοδα/eksoda dashboard bills the owner for the unit's expense share for every post-termination month while the tenant's rebuilt rent also bills the same share — a money double-count, plus the tenant's pay/edit buttons stay hidden ([id].js:365,370).

verdict.codeEvidence: occupantmanager.ts:31 `_stringToDate('')` → `undefined`; :1463 `termination: newOccupant.terminationDate` (=undefined → Contract.update rebuilds full begin→end ledger, no termination clamp); :1529-1536 write is `const { _id, __v, realmId, ...occupantPatch } = newOccupant; findOneAndUpdate({...,__v:documentVersion},{ $set: occupantPatch, $inc:{__v:1} })` — NO $unset; the ONLY $unset:{terminationDate:''} is extendLease at :2161. node_modules/mongoose/lib/helpers/query/castUpdate.js:267-268 `if (obj[key] === void 0) { delete obj[key]; continue; }` confirms Mongoose 6.13.6 (services/common/package.json:34) STRIPS the undefined `terminationDate` from `$set`, so the stale DB value survives. tenant.ts:58 `terminationDate: Date`. frontdata.ts:446 reads `occupant.terminationDate || occupant.endDate` → :450-451 terminated:true/status:'stopped'. LeaseContractForm.js:379 submits `terminationDate: lease.terminationDate ? ... : ''` and :400 hides the input when `!terminated`, so unchecking yields ''. In-flight rebuild: occupantmanager.ts:186 group.terminationDate = inFlightTenant.terminationDate (the override at :1439 passes only {_id,properties} so this is undefined) → :220 `terminationDate: t.terminationDate || null` = null → 1_base.ts:446 `_isGroupActiveForTerm` does NOT clamp → unit in occupiedThisTerm (1_base.ts:577-585) → tenant rent gets buildingCharges (1_base.ts:974-988). AFTER the write, occupantmanager.ts:1573 `_recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties` → buildingmanager.ts:4008 `recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties` re-reads DB fresh (:4013) over now-11..now+12 terms (:4030-4037), `_recomputeVacantOwnerCharges` (:3942) uses `_occupiedPropertyIdsForTerm`→`_occupiedFromOccupancyRows` :3797 `end = toYM(r.terminationDate || r.endDate)` (stale → unit vacant) → :3966 occupied.has false, :3970 flagOn passes, :3984-3990 pushes source:'vacant' owner row. Dashboard guard computeOwnerEksodaByMonth :4281-4291 only drops when `occ.has(propertyId)` — occ also reads stale terminationDate as vacant, so NOT dropped.
verdict.reasoning: Every link in the chain holds in the current code on disk. (1) The stale terminationDate genuinely survives: the write at occupantmanager.ts:1536 uses only `$set`+`$inc`, and Mongoose 6.13.6's castUpdate.js:267-268 deletes undefined-valued keys from `$set`, so the persisted past terminationDate is never cleared (the lone $unset path is extendLease:2161, not the form-edit update). (2) The tenant simultaneously reads terminated/stopped (frontdata.ts:446/450) while its rent ledger is active because Contract.update was called with termination:undefined (:1463), rebuilding the full begin→end window. (3) The tenant rent IS billed the building-expense share for current/future terms because the in-flight tenant group carries terminationDate:null (the :1439 override forwards only properties, so :186 reads undefined→:220 null), so _isGroupActiveForTerm:446 does not clamp and the unit is treated occupied during the rebuild (1_base.ts:577-989). (4) The owner is ALSO billed for the same unit/expense/term: the post-write recompute at :1573 re-reads persisted DB state (with the stale terminationDate) and _occupiedFromOccupancyRows:3797 clamps occupancy by terminationDate||endDate, so the unit reads vacant and a source:'vacant' owner row is materialised (buildingmanager.ts:3984-3990) for any chargeOwnerWhenVacant expense; the dashboard STALE-VACANT guard at :4281-4291 fails to drop it because its own occupancy check reads the same stale terminationDate as vacant. The result is a genuine euro-for-euro double-count (tenant rent buildingCharges + owner vacant eksoda) for every current/future term, plus a wrong terminated/stopped status and hidden pay/edit buttons on the tenant surface. The single minimal root cause: the un-terminate write does not $unset terminationDate (or send terminationDate:null) when the incoming value is empty.

broken.title: Payment write vs sibling/building recompute __v race is asymmetric: payment has a single __v-guarded write with NO retry (409 to user) while sibling recompute retries 8x with backoff — under sustained recompute the valid payment can never land
broken.line: _updateByTerm reads occupant.__v at 765, single findOneAndUpdate guard at 1235-1243 → throws 409 at 1245-1250 with no retry; contrast occupantmanager.ts sibling recompute 285-403 (SIBLING_MAX_ATTEMPTS=8, re-reads tenant each attempt, exponential backoff)
broken.brokenShape: _updateByTerm captures documentVersion=occupant.__v at line 765, does all the payTerm work, then commits with `findOneAndUpdate({_id,realmId,__v:documentVersion}, {$set:{rents},$inc:{__v}})` at 1235-1243. If a concurrent _recomputeSiblingTenantsInBuildings (triggered by ANY lifecycle/expense change touching the same building) bumps __v in that window, the payment's filter misses and it throws ServiceError 409 (1245-1250) — no retry. The sibling recompute, by contrast, retries up to 8 times re-reading the tenant on each attempt (occupantmanager.ts:291-298, 384), so the recompute always wins the race. A payment recorded against a tenant in a building undergoing recompute is rejected even though the payment data is valid; the read window (line 765 long before save) widens the race.
broken.trigger: Landlord records a payment on a tenant (PATCH /rents/payment/:id/:term) at the same moment another action on the same building fires _recomputeSiblingTenantsInBuildings (e.g. saving a monthly building statement, terminating/editing a sibling tenant, or a vacant-owner recompute). The payment 409s; under repeated recompute activity it never commits without the user manually retrying when the building is quiet.

verdict.codeEvidence: rentmanager.ts:758-765 — `_updateByTerm` reads `occupantDoc` via `findOne(...).lean()` then captures `const documentVersion = occupant.__v;` (line 765). All of payTerm runs after this. rentmanager.ts:1235-1243 — commit is a single `Collections.Tenant.findOneAndUpdate({_id, realmId, __v: documentVersion}, {$set:{rents}, $inc:{__v:1}}, {new:true})`. rentmanager.ts:1245-1250 — `if (!savedOccupant) throw new ServiceError('Payment conflict: another update was made simultaneously. Please retry.', 409)`. grep confirms this is the ONLY 409 and there is NO retry loop in rentmanager.ts (no MAX_ATTEMPTS / for-attempt). Callers `update` (690) and `updateByTerm` (727) call `_updateByTerm` once; routes.ts:235-236 maps PATCH /payment/:id/:term → updateByTerm via asyncWrapper (no retry layer). CONTRAST occupantmanager.ts:285-403 — `SIBLING_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8`, `siblingBackoffMs = Math.min(50*2^(attempt-1),800)` (286-287), re-reads the tenant fresh each attempt (295-298), commits with `findOneAndUpdate({_id, realmId, __v: Number(tenantObj.__v)||0}, {$inc:{__v:1}})` (367-371), and retries on null result with backoff (384). occupantmanager.ts:265-272 — `siblings` = every tenant whose property is in the building, excluding only the directly-mutated tenant — so a tenant T receiving a payment IS in the sibling set of any OTHER lifecycle/expense change in T's building, and both paths mutate the same tenant `__v`.
verdict.reasoning: The asymmetry is real and present in current HEAD f6f75966. The payment write (rentmanager._updateByTerm) holds a stale `__v` from line 765 across all payTerm work and commits with a single optimistic-lock guard at 1235-1243; on conflict it throws 409 (1245-1250) with no auto-retry — verified by grep returning zero attempt-loops and only one 409 in the file, and by both route callers invoking it exactly once with no wrapper. The sibling recompute path (occupantmanager.ts:285-403) targets the SAME tenant documents (siblings = all building tenants minus the one directly mutated, 265-272) and retries up to 8x with exponential backoff, re-reading the tenant's `__v` fresh on every attempt. So when a recompute (triggered by a sibling lifecycle/expense change, a monthly building statement save, or a vacant-owner recompute on T's building) bumps T's `__v` in the window between the payment's read (765) and its write (1235), the payment's filter misses and the user gets a 409 for valid payment data, while the recompute keeps retrying and wins. This is a genuine reject-valid defect. I do correct one overstatement in the finding: the payment does NOT 'never land' — a recompute is a per-event bounded operation (8 attempts then exits), not a perpetual background fight, so the loser is the single-attempt payment within one bounded window; the user recovers by retrying. Net: confirmed reject-valid, severity medium (manual retry recovers, no money lost or double-counted), with the asymmetric-retry root cause exactly at rentmanager.ts:765 (stale read) + 1235-1250 (single guard, no retry) versus occupantmanager.ts:285-403.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak: rentmanager.ts `_updateByTerm` captures `documentVersion = occupant.__v` at line 765 and commits via a SINGLE `findOneAndUpdate({__v: documentVersion})` at 1235-1243, throwing a non-retried 409 at 1245-1250. A concurrent `_recomputeSiblingTenantsInBuildings` (occupantmanager.ts:241+) bumps the SAME tenant's `__v` (it treats the paid tenant as a sibling of any other building change, 265-272) and itself retries 8x with backoff (285-403). The minimal fix is to give the payment write the same bounded optimistic-lock retry (re-read occupant + re-run payTerm + re-commit) that the sibling/building recompute paths already use, rather than surfacing a one-shot 409 for valid payment data.

broken.title: unarchive() never clears the terminationDate that force-archive invented, so 'Unarchive' brings a tenant back into lists permanently flagged terminated/inactive with pay+edit hidden
broken.line: 1640-1665 (force-archive sets terminationDate); 1911-1923 (unarchive only $set archived:false); restcalls.js unarchiveTenant bare PUT 172-175; [id].js onArchiveTenant 196-200
broken.brokenShape: remove() with ?force=true on a tenant that has paid rents but no terminationDate computes terminationDate=new Date(Date.UTC(yr,mo-1,1)) from the latest rent term (line 1647-1658) and sets {archived:true, terminationDate}. Later the landlord clicks 'Unarchive' ([id].js:196-200 -> unarchiveTenant -> PUT /tenants/:id/unarchive with no body). unarchive() (1914-1917) executes findOneAndUpdate($set:{archived:false}) ONLY — it does not $unset/clear terminationDate. The force-archive-invented terminationDate remains, so frontdata.toOccupantData reports terminated:true/status:'stopped' (frontdata.ts:446-451), overview countActive excludes it (1964-1972), and pay/edit stay hidden ([id].js:365,370). The tenant is visible again but frozen-terminated, and (same as the primary bug) the lease-edit form cannot clear it because terminationDate:'' is dropped by Mongoose.
broken.trigger: Admin force-deletes (?force=true) a tenant with paid rents but no explicit terminationDate -> archived with invented terminationDate. Later un-archives via the page toggle. Tenant reappears but is permanently flagged terminated/inactive with no working UI path to un-terminate.

verdict.codeEvidence: occupantmanager.ts:1640-1668 force-archive: when force && a paid tenant has no terminationDate, line 1647-1658 invents `terminationDate = new Date(Date.UTC(yr, mo-1, 1))` from the latest paid rent term (always a past date) and line 1663-1666 does `updateOne({ $set: { archived:true, terminationDate } })`. occupantmanager.ts:1911-1923 unarchive(): `findOneAndUpdate({...}, { $set: { archived: false } })` ONLY — it never $unset/clears terminationDate. frontdata.ts:421-425 formats the stored terminationDate to 'DD/MM/YYYY'; lines 442-452 then set `terminated=true`/`status='stopped'` whenever `moment.utc(terminationDate,'DD/MM/YYYY').isBefore(currentDate,'day')` — true for the invented past date. occupantmanager.ts:1855-1857 list endpoint re-includes the now-unarchived tenant (`tenants.filter(t => !t.archived)`), so it reappears flagged stopped. The edit form cannot clear it: _formatTenant (line 47) does `terminationDate: _stringToDate(tenant.terminationDate)` and _stringToDate (line 30-31) returns undefined for falsy input; update() at line 1529-1536 spreads `...occupantPatch` into `$set` — Mongoose drops the undefined terminationDate path, so the stale value persists. restcalls.js:172-175 unarchiveTenant sends a bare PUT (no body); [id].js:196-200 onArchiveTenant calls it with no payload.
verdict.reasoning: The mechanism is real and fully traceable in current code: unarchive() only flips archived:false and leaves the force-archive-invented terminationDate, which frontdata.toOccupantData (442-452) turns into terminated:true/status:'stopped'; the unarchived tenant reappears in lists (1855-1857) permanently flagged terminated; and the lease-edit form genuinely cannot clear terminationDate because _stringToDate('') -> undefined and the $set at 1536 drops undefined paths. That is a confirmed stale-state leak with no clean UI path to reverse. Two caveats that narrow but do not negate it: (1) the trigger (force-archive of a tenant with paid rents) is NOT reachable from the landlord UI — deleteTenant() (restcalls.js:202-204) sends a bare DELETE with no force=true, and the Delete button is disabled={selected.hasPayments} ([id].js:278); the only frontend force=true callers are E9/property import overwrite. So this requires a raw API call. (2) The reviewer's impact wording is partly imprecise: the Edit button is actually shown (showEditButton at [id].js:226-229 gates only on stepperMode + properties.length, NOT terminated), and payment is term-based (_isFrozen) not terminated-gated, so 'pay/edit stay hidden' overstates it — though the TenantTabs form does go readOnly (line 113: terminated || properties.length) and the un-terminate path is genuinely broken. Net: the core defect (unarchive leaves a tenant stuck terminated/inactive with no working UI to clear terminationDate) is confirmed in the code I read. The correct fix is a one-line $unset of terminationDate in unarchive(), mirroring how force-archive set it.
verdict.correctedDetail: unarchive() at occupantmanager.ts:1914-1917 must also clear the force-archive-invented terminationDate, e.g. `findOneAndUpdate({...}, { $set: { archived:false }, $unset: { terminationDate: '' } })`. Today it leaves the past terminationDate in place, so after a force-archive (?force=true on a paid tenant with no explicit terminationDate, line 1647-1666) -> unarchive sequence the tenant reappears in lists permanently flagged terminated:true/status:'stopped' (frontdata.ts:442-452) and read-only ([id].js:113), and the edit form cannot un-terminate it because terminationDate:'' is normalized to undefined (occupantmanager.ts:47 -> _stringToDate -> undefined) and dropped from the $set at occupantmanager.ts:1536. Reachable only via raw API (UI deleteTenant sends no force=true and the Delete button is disabled when hasPayments), and the 'pay/edit hidden' impact is overstated (Edit button still shows; payment is term-frozen, not terminated-gated).

broken.title: extendLease does not run the double-occupancy guard, so extending a lease past a successor tenant's entry creates overlapping occupancy on the same property that add()/update() would reject
broken.line: 1993-2168 (extendLease has no _assertNoDoubleOccupancy); guard defined at 773 and only called in add()1022 and update()1355
broken.brokenShape: extendLease() sets endDate=newEndDate (2090) and rebuilds rents (2142-2149,2160) for the new, longer window, but nowhere in the function is _assertNoDoubleOccupancy invoked (grep confirms the only call sites are 1022 add, 1355 update). _checkLostPayments inside Contract.update only guards against losing THIS tenant's own paid terms — it does not check sibling tenants. So if a successor tenant was already entered on the same propertyId after the original lease ended, extending the original lease's endDate past the successor's entryDate produces two active tenants occupying the same unit in overlapping per-property windows — exactly the state _assertNoDoubleOccupancy (773-863) raises 422 for on add/update. Downstream this corrupts building occupancy (BuildingDashboard), equal-allocation party counts, and per-unit rent attribution for the overlap period.
broken.trigger: Property P has tenant A (lease Jan-Jun) then tenant B (lease Jul-Dec) entered after A ended. Landlord imports a renewal PDF for A and uses extend-lease (PUT /tenants/A/extend-lease) with validityEnd in September. extendLease accepts it (no overlap check); A and B now both occupy P for Jul-Sep.

verdict.codeEvidence: occupantmanager.ts: grep confirms `_assertNoDoubleOccupancy` is called ONLY at line 1022 (inside add) and line 1355 (inside update); the definition is at 773-864. `extendLease` spans 1993-2211 and contains NO call to it. extendLease overwrites the lease window unconditionally: line 2088-2090 `const setPatch = { beginDate: newBeginDate, endDate: newEndDate, ... }`, and the only date guard is line 2030 `if (moment.utc(newEndDate).isSameOrBefore(moment.utc(newBeginDate)))` (end-after-begin only). The taxId gate (2045-2057) and __v lock (2005-2011) are the only other rejections. The rent recompute (2110-2149) calls `Contract.update`, whose only window guard is `_checkLostPayments` (contract.ts:362-395) — that function filters `contract.rents.filter(... !isBetween(begin,end) && _isPayment(rent))`, i.e. it only inspects THIS tenant's own embedded rents[] for payments falling outside the new window; it queries no sibling Tenant docs. So nothing in the extendLease path performs the cross-tenant per-property overlap check that _assertNoDoubleOccupancy (773-864) raises a 422 for ("Property is already assigned to another tenant during this period").
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak: `extendLease` (services/api/src/managers/occupantmanager.ts) mutates the same lease window field (`endDate`, set at line 2090) that add()/update() protect with `_assertNoDoubleOccupancy`, but never invokes that guard. Minimal fix location: between the date/taxId validation (after line 2057) and the write (line 2158), it must run `await _assertNoDoubleOccupancy(realm!._id, { ...existingDoc, beginDate: newBeginDate, endDate: newEndDate, properties: existingDoc.properties }, tenantId)`. Reachable trigger: property P has tenant A (Jan-Jun) and a successor B already entered Jul-Dec on the same propertyId; landlord imports a renewal PDF for A and POSTs /tenants/A/extend-lease with validityEnd in September. The server accepts it (taxId matches A, __v matches, end>begin), sets A.endDate=Sep — A and B now both occupy P for Jul-Sep. _checkLostPayments cannot catch this because it only inspects A's own payments, and add/update would have rejected the same state with 422.
verdict.reasoning: The reviewer's structural claim is correct against current code: the guard is defined once and called from exactly two of the three write paths that set a tenant's per-property occupancy window; extend-lease is the third and it overwrites endDate with zero overlap validation. I traced the only candidate alternate guards (the inline date check at 2030 is end-after-begin only; the taxId check at 2045 only matches the parsed PDF's primary to the existing tenant; the __v lock is concurrency only; _checkLostPayments only scans the tenant's own rents[] for out-of-window payments) and none of them performs a cross-tenant per-property overlap test. The trigger is concrete and reachable through the real route POST /:id/extend-lease (routes.ts:200-201) with a body whose primary taxId matches A. The wrong outcome is overlapping occupancy on one propertyId, which corrupts equal-allocation party counts (vacant/occupied), BuildingDashboard occupancy, and per-unit rent attribution for the overlap months — the exact class of state the guard exists to prevent. This is not a fixed historical bug; the gap is present at HEAD.

broken.title: Delete button's 'lease still active → terminate-then-delete' action always 422s (missing name + wrong date format) — tenant is neither terminated nor deleted, user sees only a generic error
broken.brokenShape: The active-lease delete path calls `saveMutation.mutateAsync({ _id: selected._id, __v: selected.__v, terminationDate: new Date().toISOString() })` — a minimal 3-field PATCH. Server `update()` runs `_formatTenant(req.body)` (occupantmanager.ts:1176); with no manager/company/name the derived `newOccupant.name` is undefined → `throw ServiceError('missing fields', 422)` at occupantmanager.ts:1214-1217. Even if name were present, `terminationDate` is an ISO string (`2026-06-16T...`) and `_stringToDate` parses with STRICT `'DD/MM/YYYY'` (occupantmanager.ts:35-38) → `moment.utc(iso,'DD/MM/YYYY',true).isValid()` false → `ServiceError('Invalid date', 422)`. Two independent 422 causes. The 422 is swallowed by the bare `catch { toast.error('Something went wrong') }` at line 387; `removeMutation` at line 384 never runs. The tenant remains active and undeleted.
broken.trigger: Open a tenant whose lease end is in the future and who has NO recorded payments, click Delete, then click the 'lease is still active' confirm button. Result: generic error toast, nothing changes.

verdict.codeEvidence: webapps/landlord/src/pages/[organization]/tenants/[id].js:379-389 — active-lease delete button posts a minimal body: saveMutation.mutateAsync({ _id: selected._id, __v: selected.__v, terminationDate: new Date().toISOString() }) (note: ISO string, NOT DD/MM/YYYY, and NO name/manager/company), then awaits removeMutation at line 384; bare `catch { toast.error(t('Something went wrong')) }` at 387-388. restcalls.js:197-200 — updateTenant PATCHes the body verbatim to /tenants/:id. occupantmanager.ts:1143-1217 — update() runs _validateOccupantPayload (passes: no guaranty/properties), then _formatTenant(req.body) at line 1176. _formatTenant (lines 42-47) calls _stringToDate(tenant.terminationDate); _stringToDate (lines 30-39) does moment.utc(dateString,'DD/MM/YYYY',true) and throws ServiceError(`Invalid date`, 422) at line 37 if invalid. Empirically verified: moment.utc('2026-06-16T18:18:10.071Z','DD/MM/YYYY',true).isValid() === false. This 422 fires INSIDE _formatTenant (line 1176), before the name check. Independently, _formatTenant line 68 sets name = name||manager = undefined for the non-company body, so the later validateStringField(name, {required:true}) / line 1214 `if (!newOccupant.name) throw ServiceError('missing fields', 422)` would also 422.
verdict.reasoning: I opened all files in the trace and confirmed every link. The button's onClick (lines 379-383) sends exactly {_id, __v, terminationDate} with terminationDate as an ISO string (new Date().toISOString()) and no name/manager/company — unlike onSubmit (lines 148-154) which spreads ...current. The server's update() runs _formatTenant(req.body) at line 1176, which calls _stringToDate on terminationDate. _stringToDate strict-parses with moment.utc(x,'DD/MM/YYYY',true); I verified empirically that an ISO string fails this strict parse (isValid===false), so it throws Invalid date 422 at line 37 — this is the FIRST 422, firing before the name check at line 1214. Even absent the date issue, the missing name would 422 at line 1214 (_formatTenant line 68 derives name from manager, which is also absent). The bare catch {} at line 387 swallows the 422 with a generic toast, and because saveMutation.mutateAsync rejects, removeMutation.mutateAsync at line 384 never executes — the tenant is neither terminated nor deleted. The trigger conditions (!hasPayments && endDate future-dated, lines 370) match the finding exactly. The finding is real and accurately described; the only minor refinement is ordering — the Invalid-date 422 fires first (inside _formatTenant) before the missing-name 422, but both are genuine and the user-facing outcome (generic error, no state change) is exactly as claimed. Note: this contradicts the comment at lines 376-378 which only anticipates a __v optimistic-lock 422; the real failure is the unformatted date plus missing name.

broken.title: bulkExpressPayment fans out concurrent __v-guarded writes with no per-tenant uniqueness guard — two items for the same tenant race and one valid payment is rejected (409 → reported failed)
broken.brokenShape: The validation loop (rentmanager.ts:484-502) checks only per-item shape — it never asserts tenantIds are unique across items. The writes then fan out via `Promise.allSettled(live.map(p => _updateByTerm(...)))` (line 625-628). Each _updateByTerm re-reads the SAME tenant doc and captures `documentVersion = occupant.__v` (line 755-765), computes its rents from the same base ledger, then commits under `findOneAndUpdate({ __v: documentVersion }, ...)` (line 1235-1241) with NO retry (throws 409 at line 1246). If a batch contains two items for one tenant (two different terms), both read __v=N, one commits (__v→N+1), the other's guard no longer matches → 409 → surfaced as `failed:true` in the results map (line 631-658). The recorded money for the losing item is NOT persisted and there is no auto-retry. The code's own comment (lines 518-520, 'each _updateByTerm operates on a DIFFERENT tenant doc so there is no cross-tenant contention') states an assumption the endpoint does not enforce. The shipped ExpressPaymentDialog emits at most one item per (tenantId,term) row so the in-app path is currently safe, but the POST /rents/express API accepts arbitrary 50-item batches.
broken.trigger: POST /rents/express with two items sharing the same tenantId (e.g. monthly for term A and previousBalance/monthly for term B of the same tenant). One item commits; the other returns failed:true with a 'Payment conflict' message and its payment is dropped from the batch.

verdict.codeEvidence: rentmanager.ts:484-502 — validation loop checks per-item shape (validateObjectId tenantId, validateTerm, monthly|previousBalance boolean) but NEVER asserts tenantIds are unique across items. rentmanager.ts:509-514 — tenantIds = items.map(...); prefetch via {_id:{$in:tenantIds}}; tenantById = new Map keyed by id (dedups the prefetch RESULT, not the items). rentmanager.ts:625-628 — const writeOutcomes = await Promise.allSettled(live.map(p => _updateByTerm(...))) fans out concurrently. rentmanager.ts:755-765 — each _updateByTerm independently does Collections.Tenant.findOne(...).lean() then const documentVersion = occupant.__v. rentmanager.ts:1235-1250 — findOneAndUpdate({_id, realmId, __v: documentVersion}, {$set:{rents}, $inc:{__v:1}}); if (!savedOccupant) throw new ServiceError('Payment conflict: another update was made simultaneously. Please retry.', 409) — NO retry loop (grep confirms _updateByTerm has no withVersionRetry/maxRetries wrapper at any of its 3 callsites: 627, 690, 727). rentmanager.ts:649-658 — losing item surfaced as {failed:true, error: '...409...'} and its payment is NOT persisted. rentmanager.ts:518-520 comment asserts 'each _updateByTerm operates on a different tenant doc so there is no cross-tenant contention' — an assumption the endpoint does not enforce. ExpressPaymentDialog.js:40-76 + 78-134 — UI maps over `rents` (one row per tenant) and selection is keyed by tenantId, so the SHIPPED UI emits at most one item per tenantId; race is API-only (POST /rents/express with hand-crafted body).
verdict.correctedDetail: Real but API-only (not UI-reachable). POST /rents/express accepts up to 50 arbitrary items (line 478) with no tenantId-uniqueness check (484-502). Two items sharing one tenantId but different terms both pass validation, both build independent paymentData, then fan out concurrently (625-628). Both _updateByTerm reads capture the same occupant.__v=N (765); the first findOneAndUpdate commits (__v→N+1), the second's {__v:N} filter no longer matches → savedOccupant null → throws 409 (1245-1249) with NO retry → that item returns failed:true (656) and its recorded payment is dropped. Minimal leak: lines 484-502 (missing per-batch tenantId-uniqueness guard) combined with line 627 concurrent fan-out + lines 1245-1249 no-retry 409. The shipped ExpressPaymentDialog cannot trigger it (one item per tenant), so user impact requires a direct/automated API call.
verdict.reasoning: I opened and read all four cited regions plus the dialog. Every mechanical claim is accurate against current code: (1) no tenantId-uniqueness guard in the validation loop; (2) Promise.allSettled fan-out; (3) per-call independent __v read; (4) __v-guarded findOneAndUpdate that throws 409 with no retry — grep confirms none of _updateByTerm's 3 callsites wrap it in a retry loop, unlike the building rebuild paths. Two same-tenant items in one batch genuinely race and one valid payment is dropped (failed:true, not persisted). The reviewer also correctly and honestly scoped this as API-only: the shipped ExpressPaymentDialog maps one item per tenant (rents = one row per tenant, selection keyed by tenantId), so it cannot emit a colliding batch. The finding is therefore confirmed as a real unguarded race in the current code, with the caveat that reachability is limited to direct POST /rents/express calls rather than the in-app flow. Because the code path to the wrong outcome (dropped recorded money under the stated trigger) is real and traceable, the finding is BROKEN, not HOLDS — the severity is appropriately medium given the API-only reachability.

broken.title: Express settlement destroys an existing partial payment for the term (payments array REPLACED, amount computed from gross owed not netted) → wrong receipt + lost audit trail, and posted amount ≠ amount shown
broken.line: 596-614 (paymentData built with only the single express payment) + 731-737 (payments REPLACED not appended) + 548-558/566-578 (monthlyOwed = gross _computeOwedLines, NOT netted by rent.total.payment) + 1052 (settlements.payments built solely from paymentData.payments)
broken.brokenShape: bulkExpressPayment builds paymentData.payments = [{ amount: monthlyOwed(+carry), type:'transfer', date: today, allocation }] with NO inclusion of the rent's existing payments. monthlyOwed comes from _computeOwedLines(targetRent) which sums preTaxAmounts/charges/buildingCharges/total.vat/debts at GROSS billed value and never subtracts targetRent.total.payment. _updateByTerm then REPLACES the payments array (documented PUT semantics at line 731-737) via settlements.payments = paymentData.payments.map(...) at line 1052. Meanwhile the client ExpressPaymentDialog (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:46-75) DOES net the existing payment (paid subtracted carry-first then monthly) and DISPLAYS only the remaining amount. So the dialog shows the remaining owed (e.g. €300) while the server posts the full gross monthly (e.g. €500) AND wipes the prior payment row.
broken.trigger: Tenant has current-month bill €500 with one existing recorded payment (e.g. €200 cash dated the 5th, type 'cash', a reference). Remaining owed = €300, so the row is eligible (monthly>0.005) and appears in the Express settlement drawer showing Monthly €300. Landlord ticks Monthly and clicks Record → POST /rents/express → server computes monthlyOwed=€500 (gross, un-netted) and posts a SINGLE €500 transfer dated today, REPLACING the €200 cash payment. Outcome: the €200 cash record (its date/method/reference, and any promo/extracharge it carried) is permanently destroyed; the month's receipt/CSV now shows a €500 transfer that never happened; the amount charged (€500) differs from the €300 the dialog displayed.

verdict.codeEvidence:
services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts:103-189 `_computeOwedLines` sums rent.total.balance (L106), preTaxAmounts (L120-128), charges (L132-141), buildingCharges (L148-160), total.vat (L169), debts/extracharge (L179) — and NEVER subtracts rent.total.payment. So monthLines.reduce at L555-557 yields the GROSS month bill.
services/api/src/managers/frontdata.ts:128-129,125 — client gets totalWithoutBalanceAmount = grandTotal − balance (gross month bill) and payment = total.payment (lump already paid) as SEPARATE fields.
webapps/landlord/src/components/rents/ExpressPaymentDialog.js:46-66,71 — dialog NETS: monthlyOwed=totalWithoutBalanceAmount, then subtracts r.payment (carry-first then monthly), DISPLAYS row.monthly = monthlyOwedRemaining (the NET). Submit (L120-138) sends only {tenantId, term, monthly:bool, previousBalance:bool} — no amount.
services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts:566-611 — bulkExpressPayment ignores client amount, sets amount = monthlyOwed (GROSS from _computeOwedLines), builds paymentData.payments = [{amount, type:'transfer', date:today, allocation}] with NO inclusion of targetRent.payments.
services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts:731-737 (documented REPLACE-not-append) + 1052 (settlements.payments = paymentData.payments.map(...)) + 1220 (Contract.payTerm).
services/api/src/businesslogic/index.ts:28 (rent.payments:[]) + tasks/6_payments.ts:10-56 (taskPayments pushes ONLY settlements.payments). Confirms the term's payments array is rebuilt solely from the single express payment — prior payment is dropped.
verdict.reasoning: I traced the full path and the finding holds. Concrete example: rent grandTotal=500, balance=0, total.payment=200 with one recorded {amount:200, type:'cash', date:'05/...', reference}. (1) DISPLAY vs POST mismatch: ExpressPaymentDialog shows Monthly = 500−200 = €300 (netting via L57-66), but the server's bulkExpressPayment recomputes monthlyOwed from _computeOwedLines = 500 (gross; total.payment is never subtracted) and posts amount=€500. (2) Dropped money / destroyed audit trail: paymentData.payments is built as a single fresh transfer (L600-608) with no targetRent.payments merged; _updateByTerm sets settlements.payments = paymentData.payments (L1052); Contract.payTerm → computeRent initializes payments:[] (index.ts:28) and taskPayments pushes only the settlements payments (6_payments.ts:50) — so the term's resulting payments array becomes [{500, transfer, today}] and the original €200 cash row (its date, method 'cash', reference, and any per-payment promo/extracharge it carried) is permanently gone; total.payment recomputes to 500. The eligibility filter (L75 row.monthly>0.005) plus server's `it.monthly===true && monthlyOwed>0` (L566) both pass because remaining 300>0, so the partially-paid row IS offered and IS processed. No guard re-supplies existing payments in the express path (I read the whole writePlans builder L520-614). This contrasts with the regular PATCH path (PaymentTabs) where the documented REPLACE semantics is safe because that dialog re-sends all existing payment rows — the express path constructs a fresh single-payment array from scratch, which is exactly what makes it leak. Real high-severity bug: wrong amount posted (gross vs netted) + permanent loss of a recorded payment (date/method/reference) for any term that already has a partial payment.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is the express-settlement path, not the documented PUT-replace itself. Two coupled defects: (A) services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts:548-557 — monthlyOwed = _computeOwedLines(targetRent) sum is GROSS billed and is never reduced by targetRent.total.payment, so for a partially-paid term the server posts the full month bill instead of the remaining amount the dialog showed; (B) services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts:596-611 — paymentData.payments is a single fresh transfer that does NOT include targetRent.payments, and because _updateByTerm REPLACES the array (L1052 → payTerm → computeRent payments:[] → 6_payments.ts), any pre-existing recorded payment for that term is destroyed (its date/type/reference/per-payment promo+extracharge lost) and total.payment is overstated. Minimal fix: in bulkExpressPayment, (1) net monthlyOwed/previousOwed against targetRent.total.payment (deduct already-paid before computing the express amount, e.g. cap each line by what remains unpaid), and (2) prepend targetRent.payments (mapped to the persisted shape) to paymentData.payments so the REPLACE-by-_updateByTerm preserves the prior payment rows.

broken.title: Express settlement only operates on the currently-visible filtered/paginated rent page (≤21 rows), silently under-collecting when a search/status filter is active or arrears span >21 tenants
broken.line: 645 (<ExpressPaymentDialog rents={rents} />) fed by rents/[yearMonth]/index.js:318-324 (renderList data) ← components/ResourceList/List.js:112 (chunks[safePageIndex-1], pageSize 21 at List.js:36) ← _filterData
broken.brokenShape: The `rents` prop handed to ExpressPaymentDialog is the post-filter, post-pagination chunk (one page of ≤21 rows from List._computeChunks), not the full month's rent set. ExpressPaymentDialog.eligible (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:39-76) is derived purely from that prop, and its 'Record' batch only ever includes rows on the visible page. There is no 'select all months/all pages' — the express batch is bounded by whatever the search/status chips + current pagination page happen to show.
broken.trigger: A realm with >21 tenants in arrears for the month, OR a landlord who typed a search / ticked the 'In arrears' chip before opening Express settlement. The drawer lists only the visible page (or only the filtered survivors), the totals line reflects only those, and Record settles only that subset — the landlord believes they batch-settled the month's outstanding rents but tenants on other pages / filtered out are left uncollected with no warning.

verdict.codeEvidence: List.js:36 `const pageSize = 21;`; List.js:39-42 `chunks = _computeChunks(pageSize, filteredData)`; List.js:98 `safePageIndex = Math.min(pageIndex, chunks.length)`; List.js:112 `renderList?.({ data: chunks[safePageIndex - 1] || [] })` — so renderList receives ONE page of ≤21 rows. rents/[yearMonth]/index.js:318-324 `renderList={({ data }) => (<RentTable rents={data} .../>)}` and line 312 `filterFn={_filterData}` where _filterData (27-110) first narrows by status chip (35-37) then by searchText (39-109). RentTable.js:550 `function RentTable({ rents = [], ...})`, line 642-645 `<ExpressPaymentDialog ... rents={rents} />` passes that same page chunk through unchanged. ExpressPaymentDialog.js:39-76 `eligible = useMemo(() => (rents || []).map(...).filter(...), [rents])` derives the dialog list purely from the prop; submitMutation.mutationFn (120-138) builds `items` only from `eligible` and POSTs them. The drawer has NO internal pagination, NO "all pages/all months" control, and the only paging UI (List.js:114-118 <Pagination>) lives outside the drawer. Dialog copy at ExpressPaymentDialog.js:226 "All tenants are up to date for this month." and footer 296-301 "{{count}} tenants" frame it as month-wide, but it is page-bounded.
verdict.reasoning: The data-flow trace in the finding matches the code on disk exactly. The full month's rents (useQuery at index.js:277-281) are filtered (_filterData) and paginated (List._computeChunks, pageSize 21) BEFORE renderList hands a single ≤21-row page to RentTable, which forwards it verbatim as the `rents` prop of ExpressPaymentDialog. The dialog's `eligible` list and its submit batch are derived solely from that prop, with no mechanism to reach rows on other pages or rows excluded by an active status chip / search. The strongest, undeniable leak is the pagination cap: a realm with >21 arrears tenants in a single month will only ever see the first 21 in the Express drawer — there is no pagination control inside the drawer and no warning — so a landlord who opens Express settlement to "clear the month" can only settle the visible page; the remaining arrears tenants are silently left uncollected. This is real under-collection by omission. I down-classify it slightly from the reviewer's framing in one respect: the dialog does NOT auto-tick or silently drop surplus — the user manually selects rows, so no recorded money is dropped or double-counted; the harm is unsettled (never-presented) arrears, not corrupted writes. But the core claim — Express settlement operates only on the currently-visible filtered/paginated page and silently under-collects when arrears span >21 tenants or a filter is active — holds against the current code. Minimal leak location: ExpressPaymentDialog.js:39-40 (`eligible` reads the page-bounded `rents` prop) combined with the absence of any full-month fetch; the structural cause is index.js:318-324 feeding `chunks[safePageIndex-1]` (via List.js:112) into RentTable.js:645 instead of the full `data.rents` set.

broken.title: Bulk rent-notice selection survives month navigation and sends the PREVIOUS month's documents
broken.line: 282-286, 159-161; RentTable.js:580-591,666-668; components/rents/RentOverview.js:99-100; frontdata.ts:345; emailmanager.ts:189
broken.brokenShape: `rentSelected` state lives in the `Rents` page component (index.js:282) and is only ever cleared in `handleActionDone` (line 285, fires after a successful send). The month-picker navigates via `router.push('/.../rents/YYYY.MM')` (RentOverview.js:99-100), which is a param-only change on the SAME page component — Next.js does NOT remount it, so `rentSelected` persists across months. `onSelectClick` (RentTable.js:584) captures the full rent object `[...selected, rent]`, including its `term`. A rent row's `_id` is the occupant `_id` (frontdata.ts:345), identical across all months for the same tenant, so RentTable's `isItemSelected = selected.map(r=>r._id).includes(rent._id)` (RentTable.js:666-668) marks the same tenants as selected on the new month's grid. Bulk send (`Actions`, index.js:159-161) emits `terms: values.map(r=>r.term)` = the STALE captured terms, and the server (emailmanager.ts:189 `const term = Number((terms && terms[index]) || defaultTerm)`) generates each document for that supplied term.
broken.trigger: On /rents/2026.04 select 3 tenants for bulk email; click the month picker forward to 2026.05 (no remount, selection persists and still renders ticked because _id==occupant._id); click 'Send by email → Invoice'. The server receives the April terms and emails April invoices/notices to those tenants while the landlord is looking at the May grid.

verdict.codeEvidence: index.js:282 `const [rentSelected, setRentSelected] = useState([]);` lives in the `Rents` page component; the ONLY reset is `handleActionDone` (index.js:284-286 `setRentSelected([])`), wired to `onDone` which fires only on send success (Actions onSuccess, lines 132-135/143). No `useEffect` keyed on `yearMonth` clears it — I read the whole file (1-331). Month navigation: RentOverview.js:97-104 `handlePeriodChange` → `router.push('/${org}/rents/${newPeriod.format('YYYY.MM')}')` — a param-only change on the SAME `[yearMonth]/index.js` page, so Next.js Pages Router reuses the `Rents` instance and `rentSelected` persists. Selection rendering: RentTable.js:666-668 `isItemSelected = selected.map((r) => r._id).includes(rent._id)`; the rent `_id` is the occupant `_id` (frontdata.ts:345 `_id: occupant._id`), identical for the same tenant across months, so the same tenants re-tick on the new month's grid. Capture: RentTable.js:580-591 `onSelectClick` does `rentSelected = [...selected, rent]`, storing the FULL previous-month rent object including `term` (frontdata.ts:121 `term: rent.term`). Send: index.js:155-161 `handleConfirm` POSTs `{document, tenantIds: values.map(r=>r._id), terms: values.map(r=>r.term)}` via `sendRentEmails` (restcalls.js:247-248 `apiFetcher().post('/emails', payload)`) — NO year/month in the payload. Server emailmanager.ts:189 `const term = Number((terms && terms[index]) || defaultTerm)` uses the client-supplied stale term (defaultTerm at line 153 is never reached because terms[index] is truthy), then emailmanager.ts:206-211 `_sendEmail({..., term})` generates each document for that stale term. The 60-min dedupe guard (emailmanager.ts:167-184) keys on (tenantId, term) and does NOT catch a wrong-month term that wasn't recently sent.
verdict.reasoning: Every link in the reviewer's chain is present in the current code on disk, and no guard breaks it. (1) `rentSelected` is page-level state cleared only after a successful send. (2) Month navigation is a router.push to the same dynamic route, which in Next.js Pages Router does NOT remount the page — the standard, well-established behavior for param-only transitions within `[yearMonth]/index.js`, so useState survives. (3) The List/ResourceList layer re-runs filterFn on the new `data` and repopulates the visible grid with the new month's rents, but it never touches the parent's `rentSelected`; RentTable re-marks the same tenants as selected because `_id` equals the occupant `_id` (constant across months). (4) The captured rent objects in `rentSelected` are references to the PREVIOUS month's rent objects and retain their old `.term`; the new fetch creates fresh objects but the stale captured ones are what `values` iterates. (5) The send payload carries `terms` (stale) and no year/month, so the server's defaultTerm fallback is dead and the document is generated for the stale term. Result: while the landlord views the May grid, the server emails April invoices/notices/payment-notices for the still-ticked tenants. This is a real wrong-document / wrong-period money-document leak. Minimal fix surface: clear `rentSelected` when `yearMonth` changes (a `useEffect([yearMonth])` in `Rents`), or re-derive `terms` server-side from year/month instead of trusting client-captured terms. I could not exercise the browser, but the data/lifecycle path is unambiguous in the code I read; defaulting-to-HOLDS does not apply because the exact path to the wrong outcome is traceable line-by-line.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak origin: `Rents` (webapps/landlord/src/pages/[organization]/rents/[yearMonth]/index.js:282) holds `rentSelected` with no reset on `yearMonth` change — only `handleActionDone` (line 285) clears it. Because month navigation (RentOverview.js:99-100 router.push to the same `[yearMonth]` route) does not remount `Rents`, the prior month's selection — including each rent's captured `term` (RentTable.js:584; term sourced at frontdata.ts:121) — persists and still renders ticked (RentTable.js:666-668 match by occupant `_id`, frontdata.ts:345). `handleConfirm` (index.js:160) then POSTs those stale `terms` with no year/month, and emailmanager.ts:189 honors `terms[index]` over `defaultTerm`, so the previous month's invoice/notice documents are generated and emailed to those tenants while the May grid is displayed. Minimal fix: add `useEffect(() => setRentSelected([]), [yearMonth])` in `Rents` (clears selection on month change), or have the server ignore client `terms` and derive the term from the request year/month.

broken.title: emailmanager.send aligns terms[] positionally to a $in query whose result order is not guaranteed
broken.brokenShape: `tenants` is re-fetched with `Collections.Tenant.find({ _id: { $in: tenantIds } })` (line 157-160). MongoDB `$in` returns documents in storage/index order, NOT in the order of the `tenantIds` array. The map callback then reads `terms[index]` (line 189) using the *result* index, assuming `tenants[index]` corresponds to `tenantIds[index]`/`terms[index]`. When the bulk-send payload carries heterogeneous terms (different months per tenant), a tenant can be issued another tenant's term, generating and emailing the wrong month's document to the wrong recipient. The same positional assumption also applies to the SMS path (line 132).
broken.trigger: Send a bulk email/SMS whose `terms[]` are not all identical (reachable by the cross-month stale-selection path in finding 1, where rentSelected mixes April and May term objects), to tenant ids whose Mongo storage order differs from the client-sent order. Tenant A receives a document built for tenant B's term.

verdict.codeEvidence: services/api/src/managers/emailmanager.ts:157-160 — `const tenants = await Collections.Tenant.find({ _id: { $in: tenantIds }, realmId: realm!._id }).lean();` (no `.sort()`, no input-order preservation). Lines 186-189 — `tenants.map(async (tenant, index) => { const tenantId = String(tenant._id); const term = Number((terms && terms[index]) || defaultTerm); ... })`. The `index` is the position in the `$in` RESULT array, but `terms[index]` is the client's array indexed by the position the client sent the tenant id. MongoDB `$in` does not preserve input-array order, so `tenants[index]._id` need not equal `tenantIds[index]`. The identical pattern is in `sendSmsOnly` at line 132. grep over the whole file confirms there is no `.sort()`, `findIndex`, or `_id`-keyed remap (only `find`/`flatMap` for unrelated phone dedup). The client (webapps/landlord/src/pages/[organization]/rents/[yearMonth]/index.js:159-160) builds `tenantIds`/`terms` positionally from the same `values` array, confirming the contract is by-index — which the server then breaks against the unordered query result. The `_sendEmail` postData (lines 13-18) carries `params.term = message.term`, so a mis-paired term is what the emailer/PDF actually renders.
verdict.reasoning: The technical core of the finding is accurate and present in HEAD code I read: the server pairs the client's positional `terms[]` (and the recipient's identity for SMS) to a `$in` query result whose ordering MongoDB does not guarantee to match input order, with no `_id`-keyed re-alignment anywhere in emailmanager.ts (lines 132 and 189). A heterogeneous `terms[]` is a valid, accepted shape on this bulk-send API contract (the `send`/`sendSmsOnly` handlers impose no same-term constraint), and when Mongo returns the documents in a different order than `tenantIds`, tenant A is emailed/SMS'd a document built for tenant B's term — a wrong-document-to-wrong-recipient outcome. I weighed the strongest reason to HOLD: the only current UI caller is the single-month rents grid, whose `values` (`rentSelected`) all carry the same `r.term`, so via that path `terms[]` is homogeneous and ordering is harmless. But the defect is in the accepted server contract, not gated by the UI; relying on the UI happening to send homogeneous terms is not a guard, and the SMS subject line / PDF term are driven directly by the mis-indexed value. The reviewer's wrong-money severity overstates it for the present UI (homogeneous terms render a correct month regardless of order), but the underlying positional-vs-unordered-result defect is real and unguarded, and is reachable with a legitimate heterogeneous bulk-send payload. Confirmed BROKEN, with the leak precisely at the `terms[index]` reads against the `$in` result order.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak: emailmanager.ts lines 189 (`send`) and 132 (`sendSmsOnly`) index the client-supplied `terms[]` by the position of the tenant within the `Collections.Tenant.find({ _id: { $in: tenantIds } })` result (lines 157-160 / 125-128). Because `$in` does not preserve input order and there is no `_id`-keyed remap, when the result order differs from `tenantIds` order a tenant is paired with another tenant's term. Harmless only while `terms[]` is homogeneous (the current single-month UI caller); with any heterogeneous `terms[]` bulk-send payload it emails/SMSes a wrong-month document to the wrong recipient. Minimal fix: build a Map from `String(tenant._id)` to its position in the original `tenantIds`, and read `terms[that position]` instead of `terms[index]` (same for the SMS path).

broken.title: Bulk selection is never reconciled against the refetched rent list after a payment status flip
broken.brokenShape: After a payment mutation invalidates [RENTS,yearMonth] and the list refetches, a row whose status flipped (e.g. notpaid→paid) leaves the active filtered set, but its captured object REMAINS in the parent `rentSelected` array (onSelectClick, line 580-591, never prunes against the new `rents`). The bulk-send Actions then still target that already-paid tenant. Additionally the select-all checkbox state (line 653-657) compares `selected.length` against the recomputed `selectableRentNum` (line 560-567): with a stale extra entry, `selected.length === selectableRentNum` is false and `selected.length < selectableRentNum` is also false, so the master checkbox renders unchecked even though every visible row is selected.
broken.trigger: Filter rents to 'In arrears', select-all, record a payment on one of them via the row dialog (which invalidates+refetches). The paid tenant drops out of the visible grid but stays selected; a subsequent bulk 'Send last payment notice' still emails the now-settled tenant, and the select-all box visibly mis-renders.

verdict.codeEvidence:
RentTable.js (read in full):
- L560-567 `selectableRentNum` = useMemo over the CURRENT `rents` prop, counting only entries with `occupant.hasContactEmails`. Recomputes from the refetched/filtered list.
- L580-591 `onSelectClick` only mutates `selected` on a checkbox toggle (`[...selected, rent]` / filter by `_id`); it never runs on a `rents` refetch. There is no useEffect reconciling `selected` against `rents` anywhere in RentTable.
- L653-657 master Checkbox `checked`: `selected.length > 0 && selected.length < selectableRentNum ? 'intermediate' : selected.length === selectableRentNum`. When `selected.length > selectableRentNum` (a stale entry no longer in the filtered `rents`), both branches are false → renders UNCHECKED.
- L666-668 per-row `isItemSelected = selected.map(r=>r._id).includes(rent._id)` → each still-visible selected row renders CHECKED. So master-unchecked vs rows-checked is a real visible inconsistency.

Parent page rents/[yearMonth]/index.js (read in full):
- L282 `rentSelected` state; L315 fed to `Actions values={rentSelected}`; L321 fed to `RentTable selected={rentSelected}`.
- L284-286 `handleActionDone` resets `setRentSelected([])` ONLY via `Actions onDone` (L132-136 sendMutation.onSuccess → onDone) — i.e. only after a SEND, never after a row-dialog payment.
- L147-165 `Actions.handleConfirm` sends to `values.map(r=>r._id)` / `values.map(r=>r.term)` with no cross-check against the live `rents`.
- A row payment goes through `handleEdit`→NewPaymentDialog (RentTable L599-605, L630-634), entirely orthogonal to `rentSelected`; it invalidates [RENTS,yearMonth].

ResourceList/List.js (read in full): L66-91 `handleSearch` re-runs filterFn(data,...) on every `data` refetch (deps include data); _filterData (index.js L34-37) drops rows whose `status` no longer matches the active filter → the now-`paid` row leaves the `rents` chunk passed to RentTable, while `rentSelected` is untouched.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak location 1 (stale bulk-send target): there is no reconciliation of `rentSelected` against the refetched/filtered rent list. After a row-level payment via NewPaymentDialog invalidates [RENTS,yearMonth] (RentTable L630-634 + handleEdit L599-605) and the row's status flips notpaid→paid, _filterData (index.js L34-37) drops it from the visible `rents`, but its captured object stays in parent `rentSelected` (only pruned by checkbox toggle, RentTable L586, or by a completed SEND, index.js L284-286). A subsequent bulk Send (Actions.handleConfirm, index.js L155-165) maps `values=rentSelected` to _id/term and emails the now-settled tenant. Leak location 2 (master-checkbox mis-render): with the stale entry, `selected.length > selectableRentNum`, so the RentTable L653-657 ternary evaluates both branches false → master checkbox renders unchecked while every visible row (L666-668) renders checked. Minimal fix: prune `selected`/`rentSelected` to the intersection with current `rents._id` on refetch (useEffect in the parent or a derived `effectiveSelected` in RentTable), and/or clamp the L653-657 comparison with a count of currently-visible selected rows rather than raw `selected.length`.
verdict.reasoning: I read RentTable.js in full, the parent rents/[yearMonth]/index.js in full, and ResourceList/List.js in full, and traced the exact data flow. The selection array lives in the parent (`rentSelected`) and is fed both to RentTable (as `selected`) and to the bulk-send Actions (as `values`). The only code paths that mutate it are: checkbox toggle (onSelectClick L580-591), select-all toggle (onSelectAllClick L569-578), and a post-send reset (handleActionDone, index.js L284-286). NONE of these run on a query refetch. A row-level payment (NewPaymentDialog, opened via handleEdit) invalidates [RENTS,yearMonth]; List.handleSearch re-filters on the new data and the status-flipped row leaves the visible `rents` — but `rentSelected` retains the stale object. Both claimed consequences follow directly: (A) Actions.handleConfirm sends to the stale tenant's still-valid _id/term with no live-list cross-check; (B) the L653-657 checkbox ternary renders unchecked when `selected.length > selectableRentNum`, contradicting the per-row checked state at L666-668. Neither is guarded anywhere in the chain. The finding is real (severity medium, as claimed). I confirm BROKEN. Note the trigger is the row-dialog payment, not a send; the reviewer described this correctly.

broken.title: Accounting page search filter calls .toLowerCase() on tenant name without null-coercion
broken.brokenShape: This parallel (non-ResourceList) search implementation filters via `t.name.toLowerCase()` (incoming line 94, outgoing line 99) and `s.tenant.toLowerCase()` (settlements line 103) with no `String(x ?? '')` coercion — unlike every shared `_filterData`, which all coerce first. The filter runs inside a useMemo with no try/catch, so a null/undefined `name`/`tenant` throws during render and crashes the whole Accounting page to the error boundary rather than degrading. `tenant: tenant.name` / `name: tenant.name` (accountingmanager.ts:201,262,378) is required at creation so a null name is unlikely on real data, lowering likelihood.
broken.trigger: Type any character in the Accounting search box for a year whose incoming/outgoing/settlement set contains a tenant with a null/empty name (legacy/imported row). The useMemo throws and the Accounting tab blanks via the error boundary.

verdict.codeEvidence:
webapps/landlord/src/pages/[organization]/accounting/[year].js — the parallel search implementation inside `filteredData = useMemo(...)`:
- L94-96: `accountingData.incomingTenants?.filter((t) => t.name.toLowerCase().includes(lc))`
- L98-100: `accountingData.outgoingTenants?.filter((t) => t.name.toLowerCase().includes(lc))`
- L102-104: `accountingData.settlements?.filter((s) => s.tenant.toLowerCase().includes(lc))`
None coerce; `lc = searchText.toLowerCase()` at L90; the useMemo (L87) runs synchronously during render, no try/catch.

Data source: services/api/src/managers/accountingmanager.ts returns these fields verbatim from the Occupant doc — `name: tenant.name` at L201 (_incomingTenants) and L262 (_outgoingTenants); `tenant: tenant.name` at L378 (_settlements rawData branch, which is the path feeding the JSON `all` endpoint).

Schema: services/common/src/collections/tenant.ts L12 `name: String,` — declared with NO `required` constraint, so a null/undefined name is schema-valid (legacy/imported/mongo-seeded rows).

Error handling: webapps/landlord/src/pages/_app.js L117 wraps the app in `<ErrorBoundary>` (class component with getDerivedStateFromError at ErrorBoundary.js:66) — a render-time throw replaces the page with the fallback.

Sibling contrast: webapps/landlord/src/pages/[organization]/owners/index.js L19-25 `_filterData` DOES coerce via `norm = (s) => String(s || '').toLowerCase()...`, so the accounting page is the un-guarded outlier.
verdict.correctedDetail: Un-guarded `.toLowerCase()` on tenant name/tenant fields in the Accounting page search filter at webapps/landlord/src/pages/[organization]/accounting/[year].js L95 (`t.name.toLowerCase()`), L99 (`t.name.toLowerCase()`), and L103 (`s.tenant.toLowerCase()`). These run inside the `filteredData` useMemo (L87) during render. If an incoming/outgoing/settlement row carries a null/undefined name (schema permits it: tenant.ts:12 `name: String` with no `required`; accountingmanager.ts passes `tenant.name` through verbatim at L201/L262/L378), typing any character in the Accounting search box throws TypeError during render and the global ErrorBoundary (_app.js:117) blanks the whole Accounting page instead of degrading. Minimal fix: coerce each side, e.g. `String(t.name ?? '').toLowerCase()` / `String(s.tenant ?? '').toLowerCase()`, matching the owners/index.js `_filterData` pattern. Severity is low: real data almost always has a populated name, so likelihood is low; impact is a recoverable blank-render, not money loss.
verdict.reasoning: I opened the file and confirmed the three cited lines match exactly (L94-95, L98-99, L102-103), all calling `.toLowerCase()` with no `String(x ?? '')` coercion, inside a synchronous useMemo with no try/catch. I traced the data source: accountingmanager.ts assigns `name: tenant.name` (L201, L262) and `tenant: tenant.name` (L378) directly from the Occupant doc. I confirmed the Tenant schema declares `name: String` without `required` (tenant.ts:12), so a nameless tenant is schema-valid and plausible for legacy/imported/mongo-seeded rows (the steering docs explicitly note seed data is created via direct mongo insert that bypasses validators). I confirmed a global ErrorBoundary wraps the app (_app.js:117), so a render-time throw blanks the page rather than degrading. I also confirmed the sibling owners/index.js `_filterData` (L19-25) DOES coerce with `String(s || '')`, making the accounting page the un-guarded outlier — exactly as the finding states. One nuance: the finding's claim that EVERY shared `_filterData` coerces is slightly overstated (tenants/index.js L44 calls `name.replace(...)` un-coerced too), but that does not weaken the confirmed accounting-page throw. The trigger and impact described are accurate. This is a genuine, currently-unguarded throw, correctly rated low severity (low likelihood, recoverable blank-render, no money impact).

broken.brokenShape: The non-settled footer pill formats the SAME owner.totalOutstanding value with `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }).format(outstanding)`. `undefined` locale = the BROWSER's default locale, and currency is hard-coded 'EUR'. OwnerListItem's footer pill uses raw `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, {style:'currency', currency:'EUR'})` while (a) the same component's own paid/total figures and (b) the owner-detail page + accounting tab render the identical owner.totalOutstanding value through the org-locale/currency path (NumberFormat → useFormatNumber → formatNumber). For the default el-GR/EUR realm on a non-Greek browser, the pill shows browser-locale grouping (e.g. €1,234.56) while the rest of the app shows 1.234,56 €. This is a confirmed visual/locale inconsistency on a money surface, no guard present. Severity is medium-low: it does not corrupt stored money or alter computation — purely a display divergence — and the EUR currency is correct for the user's actual (Greek) realm, so the most-likely-visible defect is grouping/symbol-placement when the browser locale != el-GR. The wrong-currency-symbol case only manifests for the (uncommon) non-EUR realm configuration. The minimal fix is to replace lines 130-133 with the project's NumberFormat/useFormatNumber path (e.g. render `${t('Outstanding')}:` followed by `<NumberFormat value={outstanding} />`, or call useFormatNumber()(outstanding) for the interpolated string).
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is confined to webapps/landlord/src/components/owners/OwnerListItem.js lines 130-133 (the `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }).format(outstanding)` expression inside the non-settled branch of the footer Badge). broken.title: Accounting owners search matches taxId case-sensitively / un-normalized while the Owners page normalizes it — same query yields different result sets across the two owner surfaces
broken.line: 80-85 (compare owners/index.js:18-27)
broken.brokenShape: The accounting Ιδιοκτήτες search filters owners with `(o.name||'').toLowerCase().includes(lc) || String(o.taxId||'').includes(searchText)` — name is lowercased but taxId is matched against the RAW (untrimmed/uncased) searchText and uses substring includes with no whitespace/punctuation stripping. The Owners list page (_filterData in owners/index.js:18-27) normalizes BOTH name and taxId via norm() which lowercases AND strips /\s|\.|-/gi before indexOf. Result: a query containing a space, dot, or dash (or trailing whitespace) that the Owners list matches against an owner will NOT match the same owner in the accounting tab, and vice-versa. The two surfaces present a different owner set for an identical search string.
broken.trigger: On accounting/[year] Ιδιοκτήτες tab type a taxId fragment with a space/dot (or with trailing space) that exists in the realm — owner disappears from the accounting list; the same string on /owners keeps the owner visible (and the statement-download path is only reachable from accounting, so the owner becomes unreachable for that query).

verdict.codeEvidence: accounting/[year].js:79-84 — `const lc = searchText.toLowerCase(); return list.filter((o) => (o.name||'').toLowerCase().includes(lc) || String(o.taxId||'').includes(searchText));` — taxId is matched against the RAW (un-lowercased, un-trimmed, un-stripped) searchText. Both surfaces consume the SAME aggregate: accounting/[year].js:71-74 uses `queryKey:[QueryKeys.OWNERS], queryFn: fetchOwners`, identical to owners/index.js:34-37. owners/index.js:18-26 — `const norm = (s) => String(s||'').toLowerCase().replace(/\s|\.|-/gi,''); const q = norm(filters.searchText); items = items.filter((o) => norm(o.name).indexOf(q)!==-1 || norm(o.taxId).indexOf(q)!==-1);` — Owners page lowercases AND strips spaces/dots/dashes from BOTH query and both fields (name + taxId).
verdict.reasoning: The two owner search surfaces are confirmed divergent in current code and feed off the same /owners aggregate, so they hold identical owner data. Owners page (owners/index.js:19-26) normalizes via norm() = lowercase + strip /\s|\.|-/gi on the query AND on both name and taxId. Accounting tab (accounting/[year].js:79-84) only lowercases name, and matches taxId against the RAW searchText with no trim/strip. Concretely: a realm owner with taxId "123456789" typed as "123 456" or "123.456" or with a trailing space "123456789 " matches on /owners but NOT on the accounting Ιδιοκτήτες tab (String("123456789").includes("123 456") === false). The divergence is real, present, and exactly as the reviewer described — not a misread and not already guarded. I mark BROKEN because the inconsistency is traceable in the code I read and a valid query effectively rejects (hides) an owner on the accounting surface that the sibling surface shows. Caveat: the practical impact is UX/cosmetic, not money-correctness — no money is shipped wrong, dropped, or double-counted; the owner reappears when the search is cleared or typed without separators, and the reviewer themselves rated severity 'none/low'. So it is a real but low-severity consistency defect, not a money/data-integrity defect.
verdict.correctedDetail: Leak is at webapps/landlord/src/pages/[organization]/accounting/[year].js lines 79-84: the taxId branch `String(o.taxId || '').includes(searchText)` uses the raw searchText (no .toLowerCase(), no trim, no separator stripping), whereas the canonical owner-search normalization in owners/index.js:19-22 strips /\s|\.|-/gi and lowercases both query and field. Minimal fix: reuse the same norm() helper for both name and taxId in the accounting filter so a taxId fragment containing a space/dot/dash (or trailing whitespace) yields the identical owner set on both surfaces. Impact is UX consistency only; no money correctness is affected.

broken.title: E9 re-import after a building address change reassigns property.buildingId unconditionally, leaving the property linked to a unit in BOTH the old and new building — owner-side vacant/expense share double-counts
broken.line: 1495-1498 (realm-scoped, NOT building-scoped Property.findOne by atakNumber); 1575 (property.buildingId = String(building._id) unconditional, not gated by forceOverwrite); 1634-1647 (fresh unit pushed onto the new building referencing the same propertyId); contrast with the explicit guard the MANUAL path has at 1948-1963 ('Otherwise rent computation walks both buildings and double-bills')
broken.brokenShape: importFromE9 looks a building up by ADDRESS only (1182-1223, exact street1+zip → street-only → greek-normalized). If a re-imported E9 carries a street1 that differs enough to miss all three (e.g. abbreviated/re-filed street), a NEW building B is created (1252-1270). The unit loop then does Property.findOne({realmId, atakNumber}) (1495-1498) — realm-scoped, not building-scoped — finds the EXISTING property still attached to building A, sets property.buildingId = B unconditionally (1575), and pushes a fresh unit onto B (1634) pointing at that propertyId. The unit-dedup at 1306-1308 only scans `building.units` of the CURRENT building (B, which is empty), so it never notices building A still holds a unit with the same propertyId. No post-loop step removes the orphan (reconciliation 1691-1766 only backfills taxIds; grep for units.pull/orphan cleanup finds none in the import path). The property is now referenced by units in TWO buildings.
broken.trigger: Realm with building 'ΟΔΟΣ ΖΗΤΑ 167' imported once (creates Property P, unit on building A). User imports an updated E9 for the same property whose street1 parses differently (e.g. 'ΟΔΟΣ ΖΗΤΑ ΛΕΩΦ. 167' or a typo'd/re-filed street) so the address lookup misses → new building B created. P.buildingId flips to B and B gets a duplicate unit for P. P is left vacant. On the owners page (_aggregateOwners iterates ALL realm buildings, ownermanager.ts:514/542, unitCount+=1 at :263) and per-building owner recompute (_recomputeVacantOwnerForProperties / dashboard), building A AND building B each derive a source:'vacant'/'owner-resident' ownerMonthlyExpenses row for the same propertyId+term → the owner's totalAmount/totalOutstanding double-counts that unit's expense share (and unitCount/buildingCount are inflated).

verdict.codeEvidence: buildingmanager.ts (importFromE9, starts line 1011): address lookup is exact street1+zip (1182-1186) → street-only (1189-1193) → greek-normalized (1204-1223); on a miss a NEW building is created+saved (1252-1273). The per-unit dedup short-circuits scan ONLY the current building's units: line 1306-1308 `(building as any).units.find(u => u.atakNumber === parsedUnit.atakNumber)` and the DEH variant at 1378-1385 — both reference the freshly-created (empty) building B, so they miss and fall through. Line 1495-1498 then does realm-scoped `Collections.Property.findOne({ realmId, atakNumber })` (NOT building-scoped) and finds the existing Property still attached to building A. Line 1575 `property.buildingId = String(building!._id)` is UNCONDITIONAL — only electricitySupplyNumber (1576-1582), surface (1592-1594), kaek (1597-1602) are forceOverwrite-gated; buildingId is not. Line 1634-1647 pushes a fresh unit onto B carrying `propertyId: String(property._id)`. Reconciliation 1691-1766 only backfills taxIds; the success path (1768-1792) has no orphan removal; grep over importFromE9 (1011-~1797) finds zero `units.pull`/orphan-removal (first such is the unrelated deleteUnit at 2183). The MANUAL addUnit path DOES guard this at 1948-1963: `Collections.Building.findOne({ realmId, 'units.propertyId': req.body.propertyId })` → 422 'Property is already linked to a unit in another building' with the comment 'Otherwise rent computation walks both buildings and double-bills the tenant.' Downstream, ownermanager.ts `all`/`one` load ALL realm buildings (514-516, 542-544) and `_aggregateOwners` does `agg.unitCount += 1` and `agg.buildingIds.add(bid)` per owner-row per unit (263-264), so the propertyId duplicated across A and B inflates unitCount/buildingCount and any propertyId-scoped vacant/repair-vacant row generated on either building attributes to that owner.
verdict.reasoning: Every step in the claimed path is verified against the code on disk. The trigger is reachable: the three address matchers are exact-string / exact-normalized (case+accent only), not fuzzy, so a year-on-year or re-filed E9 whose AADE street string differs by a token (e.g. ΛΕΩΦ./ΟΔΟΣ insertion) or typo defeats all three and creates a new building — the import's own comment at 1196-1203 concedes even case/accent variance would 'silently duplicate the building.' With building B empty, the by-ATAK/by-DEH short-circuits scan only B, miss, and fall through to a realm-scoped (not building-scoped) Property lookup that finds the property still attached to A; buildingId is flipped to B unconditionally (NOT forceOverwrite-gated) and a duplicate unit for the same propertyId is pushed onto B. Building A's original unit is never pulled and no post-loop cleanup runs. The manual addUnit path proves the maintainers know this exact hazard and guard it (1948-1963) — the import path lacks the equivalent. Result: the property is referenced by units in two buildings; _aggregateOwners counts it in both (unitCount/buildingCount inflated) and any vacant/owner-resident charge derived per building double-counts the owner's expense share. This is a real double-count / inflated-count defect in current code, not already guarded and not a misread. Minimal leak: the unconditional buildingId reassignment at line 1575 combined with the absence of an other-building orphan check before pushing the new unit at 1634; mirroring the addUnit guard (1952-1963) inside the import loop — or pulling the prior unit from its old building when buildingId changes — would close it.
verdict.correctedDetail: The E9 import path (buildingmanager.ts importFromE9) reassigns property.buildingId to a newly-created building B unconditionally at line 1575 and pushes a duplicate unit referencing that propertyId at lines 1634-1647, without the cross-building orphan check the manual addUnit path enforces at lines 1948-1963. When a re-imported E9 carries a street1 that defeats all three address matchers (exact street1+zip 1182-1186, street-only 1189-1193, greek-normalized 1204-1223) — plausible on a year-on-year/re-filed E9 with a reformatted Greek street string — a new building B is created and the existing property P (still attached to building A via the realm-scoped, not building-scoped, lookup at 1495-1498) is left referenced by units in BOTH A and B. ownermanager.ts _aggregateOwners iterates all realm buildings (514-516/542-544) and does unitCount+=1 / buildingIds.add(bid) per unit (263-264), so the owner's unitCount and buildingCount inflate and any propertyId-scoped vacant/repair-vacant ownerMonthlyExpenses row generated on either building double-counts that unit's owner-side expense share.

broken.title: E9 re-import steals a Property from its existing building and double-counts its expenses across two buildings
